Sports.title: Lewis Hall could be England’s left-back for the next decade after showing Tuchel what he was missing at World Cup
Sports.content:
Next

IF he plays his cards right, Lewis Hall could be England’s left-back for the next decade.

Because, after this sensational individual performance against the world champions, in their own backyard, the 22-year-old clearly has the talent to do it.



Newcastle star Hall was simply superb at Atletico Madrid’s Metropolitano stadium.

Both in attack, where he showed some outstanding dribbling ability, including a tasty double drag-back through the middle of the pitch inside the first ten minutes



And defensively, where he shut down Lamine Yamal, just as he did at St James’ Park last season in the Champions League.

It left fans even more puzzled as to why Thomas Tuchel left him out of his World Cup squad in the summer.

But at least the German is getting it right at left-back now, with Hall one of the big winners of this excellent Nations League campaign.

Hall’s partnership down the left-hand side with former Toon team-mate Anthony Gordon has blossomed all Autumn.

To the point here where the pair looked arguably the most in-sync full-back-winger combination since Gary Neville and David Beckham.

Gordon’s speed and Herculean effort in the press caused Spain all manner of problems.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

But the neat inter-play between the Barcelona wideman, Hall and Declan Rice on the left-hand side was the kind of slick, quick stuff England fans have been crying out for.

Perhaps it should be no surprise Hall has the technique to pull it off. After all, he grew up as a central midfielder coming through the ranks at Chelsea and he is as surprised as anyone that he now is a left-back.

His clever double drag-back on eight minutes was not only nifty but also a clever way to get out of trouble.



It left the Spanish midfielders bamboozled, given it is usually they who do that kind of thing to us, not the other way round.

Hall’s mazy dribble into the box on 18 minutes, which ended in a corner, was so skilful that you had to do a double-take to check it was he and not Gordon who had pulled it off.

The stats backed up what fans were seeing with their own eyes too, as Hall’s five completed dribbles in the first half was two more than every other on the pitch COMBINED.

But it was also his defensive work that caught the eye. Yamal was not getting much joy out of his opponent and resorted to falling down easily under Hall’s challenge at one point, winning an unjustified free-kick.

Moments later, it was Hall who was there to put in a well-timed interception, just when Yamal had played through a dangerous pass.



Erasing Lamine Yamal

The Londoner has developed a knack recently for England of intervening just when it is needed.

Even when Jude Bellingham fired a rare, inaccurate ball across the pitch to him, Hall readjusted his body and managed to head it on to Gordon, who then won a free-kick.

Hall took the resulting set-piece but fired it weakly into the Spain players for what was the only blot on his copybook for the night.

With Djed Spence back fit, Tuchel may have been tempted to go with the Inter Milan man after his stellar World Cup.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

But we are in the Tuchel 2.0 phase now where the progression has to be favouring technique over athleticism if we are going to take that final step.



In Hall, it feels like England have a young defender who can do both. After years and years of toiling away with different left-backs, his display here against the best suggested we have one to last.

Sports.title: England player ratings: Jude Bellingham stars in Madrid but Quansah looks out of his depth
Sports.content:
Next

ENGLAND put an end to Spain’s 43-game unbeaten streak with a thrilling 3-2 victory in Madrid.

Harry Kane, Ezri Konsa, and Ben White were on the scoresheet in a brilliant performance from the Three Lions — though lousy defending from Jarell Quansah gifted Spain a way back into the match.



The defender took too long on the ball, which Lamine Yamal pounced on before being brought down in the box by Elliot Anderson, who was promptly sent off.

The hosts then piled on the pressure, with Yamal switching gears and setting up Nico Williams for a Spanish second with 15 minutes to play.



It proved a tense final 15 minutes for the visitors, as James Trafford denied Fermin Lopez, Marc Cucurella, and Yamal, while White produced a vital intervention to thwart Williams and seal the win.

This is how SunSport England reporter Lloyd Canfield rated the players…

JAMES TRAFFORD – 7

The Jordan Pickford era for England might have ended tonight, with Trafford, 24, proving he can mix it with the best.

He was excellent at playing the ball out from the back, and there was little he could do about the penalty which saw Spain pull a goal back.

With the hosts pushing for an equaliser, he made a sharp stop to deny Fermin Lopez before producing several others to keep England ahead, including a remarkable double save in injury time.

BEN WHITE – 7

White hasn’t always been the most popular figure with England fans, but there were absolutely no issues with his inclusion tonight…



He was solid in defence, making a crucial block to deny Nico Williams before full-time, and got forward well to score the Three Lions’ third with a composed finish inside the box

EZRI KONSA – 7

Returned to the England side after missing the last game through injury, and marked his comeback with a goal.

It was a fine finish too, as he strolled through the penalty area unmarked, before unleashing a header into the back of UnaI Simon’s net.



Not massively troubled defensively by Mikel Oyarzabal and co, but always on hand when he was needed.

JARELL QUANSAH – 4

Was caught out by Lamine Yamal under pressure with half an hour to go, which led to Elliot Anderson bringing him down before being dismissed by the referee.

Spain targeted him from that point on, looking to capitalise on his mistake, but he did well to see the game out from that point when he could have completely crumbled.



LEWIS HALL – 7

The best player on the pitch in the first half, Hall pulled off a masterful bit of skill in the first half to escape the pressure of two Spanish midfielders.

Not only did he complete the most dribbles out of anyone in the first half, he also made the most defensive contributions, keeping Lamine Yamal of all people in his pocket for the most part.

Yamal grew into the game and started to make a difference late on, but Hall was still very impressive.

DECLAN RICE – 7

So much is made of the talent in this Spain midfield, but not enough is made of the level of player England also have.



Rice saw plenty of the ball and always kept things simple, which was very Spanish of him in a sense, just winning the ball and easily turning it over or round the corner to England’s more dangerous players where possible.

He capped off a good night with a perfectly-placed corner onto the head of Arsenal team-mate Konsa, with England embracing their inner “set-piece FC” thanks to that duo.

ELLIOT ANDERSON – 5

Elliot Anderson was always on hand to shut things down in midfield when Spain got on the ball, not allowing them too much time to dictate the game and grow into it when England were leading.

Unfortunately his decent performance was cut short when he was sent off following some lackadaisical defending from Jarell Quansah behind him.



JUDE BELLINGHAM – 8

Jude Bellingham, you are such a wonderful footballer. Came close to opening the scoring in his now-home of Madrid just a few minutes after kick-off, and continued to be a threat throughout the first half.

He was dynamic, diving into tackles one minute and taking a shot the next as he proved himself once more as one of England’s most dangerous players – proved by his involvement in the build-up to the Three Lions’ second and third goals.

He danced around the Spanish defence and won the corner which was whipped in by Declan Rice and headed home by Ezri Konsa, before setting up Ben White for the third goal.



MORGAN ROGERS – 6

Had the tough task of getting the better of Marc Cucurella as he started on the right side of England’s attack, but he still looked dangerous.

His physicality, combined with his ability to duck and dive through Spanish defenders is what makes him such a unique attacking prospect – and although he wasn’t involved in any goals he still caused plenty of problems for Cucurella.

ANTHONY GORDON – 6

A real danger to Spain down the left for England, and he brought his impressive form for Barcelona into this game, with a shot blocked early on in the game.

He was always an option on the left hand side, and combined brilliantly with former Newcastle team-mate Lewis Hall behind him, in what could be a great left side for England for as long as the next ten years.

It must be said though that his positioning and inability to move the ball on in the build-up to Spain’s second goal was poor.



HARRY KANE – 7

England’s Ballon d’Or winner was serenaded by the travelling supporters in front of Lamine Yamal, who sang “Harry Kane, the best in the world”, and, “Where’s your Ballon d’Or?” when the Spaniard got on the ball.

He showed immense strength to win a penalty for England deep into the first half, and of course he slotted it past Unai Simon.

Showed some really nice moments on the ball too, showcasing his strength and dribbling abilities that make him the best football player in the world.



SUBS:

MYLES LEWIS-SKELLY (HARRY KANE, 78) – 5

Added some legs and composure in England’s midfield, but that midfield was largely overrun after he came on – not through much fault of his.

DOMINIC CALVERT-LEWIN (ANTHONY GORDON, 83) – 6

Showed some nice moments of hold-up play and did his bit defensively, but it was a tough time for a striker to come on with Spain pushing for an equaliser.

DJED SPENCE (JUDE BELLINGHAM, 83) – 6

Bought on to nullify the threat of Lamine Yamal and did pretty well in doing so by making him uncomfortable and bringing him down a few times.

DAN BURN (BEN WHITE, 88) – N/A

Big Dan Burn came on to get the job done, and did so.

Sports.title: Spain 2 England 3: Fantastic Three Lions hold out with 10 men as world champs lose in Madrid for first time in 39 YEARS
Sports.content:
Next

AGAINST the world champions, this was almost perfect.

This was the best performance yet under Thomas Tuchel, as his heroic players took on Spain and proved THEY were the ones with the cojones.



It was even sweeter that leading by three goals and reduced to 10 men, the Three Lions fought for their lives to win.

Harry Kane, the Ballon d’Or winner, stuck a penalty past Unai Simon, the winner of the Golden Glove before half-time.





And 3,500 Englishmen then rubbed their eyes in disbelief as their team struck twice at the start of the second half with goals from Arsenal defenders Ezri Konsa and Ben White.

Trouble brewed when Elliot Anderson saw red for fouling Lamine Yamal with 27 minutes left. Euro 2024 matchwinner Mikel Oyarzabal scored from the penalty spot and Nico Williams pulled another back.

Yet the hero of the night was James Trafford, the young keeper from Leeds. As England struggled at the end, he saved the night with some stunning saves.

Tuchel gambled by replacing Jordan Pickford with the confident – some would say cocky – 24-year-old who was making only his fifth appearance but proved there will be many, many more.



Crucially, Trafford delivered game-saving, match-winning stops at the end, something we have not seen enough of from Pickford. Tuchel has now given himself a whacking great headache for the Nations League quarter-finals.

England go through as group winners and while this might mean nothing, this hugely encouraging, feel-good performance, will have given this team – a work in progress – some major belief.

In fact, this victory was laced with a sense of frustration. It should have been England and not Argentina in the World Cup final, had Tuchel not cocked things up. Maybe things would have been different.

But on this occasion, the defensive subs – particularly Djed Spence for Jude Bellingham and Myles Lewis-Skelly for Kane – actually worked. Unlike in Atlanta.

Dan Burn, the hero of Mexico, reprised that role and came on and delivered a late header before picky ref Clement Turpin blew his whistle for the millionth time.



After showing off the World Cup trophy, Spain struggled against a rock-solid England team and only had joy once they had a one-man advantage

Until the penalty, England were rock-solid in defence and in particular, Lewis Hall was outstanding against boy wonder Yamal.

In midfield, Rice and Anderson were in control although in fairness, Spain are not the same without Rodri and Dani Olmo.

Yet this clever-high-tempo football was exactly the sort of stuff that Tuchel has been calling for from his team. But equally, since the German arrived, we had not seen much of it.

Just before half-time, England’s noisy fans, who sang, “Harry Kane, the best in the world”, were able to celebrate when the skipper grabbed his 93rd international goal.



Kane was put to the ground by Pau Cubarsi. It was clever play from the Bayern Munich striker who knew what he was doing by putting his body between the ball and the defender but it was still a penalty.



Spain argued that Anderson fouled Marc Cucurella as he delivered the killer pass but as ever, the dislikable former Chelsea defender embarrassed himself. Cucurella remained motionless on the pitch in a pathetic attempt to try and win a free-kick but the VAR officials were not going to be conned.

Kane ignored the noise of thousands of whistles before planting an unstoppable penalty past Simon.

Spain’s players were still feeling aggrieved as they headed towards the tunnel with White involved, which is funny.

Because the last time he was here in the Champions League, back in April, with Arsenal against Atletico Madrid, he ended up in a furious row at the interval with Diego Simeone.

Sub Burn broke up the clash between Alex Baena and White while Cucurella – also got involved.



Remarkably, England started the second half as they finished the first period. In fact, they just took the pee.

Declan Rice’s outswinging corner was met with a header from Konsa who, unbelievably, was unmarked.



England’s fans chanted “we are top of the League” and they did not have to wait long for the third.

There was some delicious skill from Morgan Rogers, Kane played a part and Bellingham delivered a terrific ball and White took one touch before threatening a shot through Simon’s legs.

On this occasion, there was no one in England booing the Arsenal right-back.

There was drama, of course. England and Jarell Quansah got caught playing out from the back by Yamal and he was then dragged down by Anderson who was shown a straight red card. In hindsight, Anderson should have just let the Barcelona superstar score.



After Oyarzabal sent Trafford the wrong way from the spot, the remaining 10 England players had a quick huddle with Kane clearly shouting words of encouragement.

Predictably, Spain unleashed fire on the England team. Anthony Gordon lost the ball and Yamal squared for Williams to score although both Quansah and Konsa were caught out of position.

Trafford made brilliant saves to deny Yamal, Cucurella, Lopez and Aymeric Laporte and England hung on for a win they definitely deserved.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

What a performance. What a night. And here was a reminder that watching England can actually be fun.

And in Trafford, we surely have a new star.

The Manchester City midfielder played a superb ball to Harry Kane, who later won and converted a penalty in a 3-2 win.

Ian Wright thinks Anderson was blameless.

Sports.title: Arsenal suffer huge injury blow as star goes off holding hamstring during Spain vs England clash
Sports.content:

ARSENAL suffered a major injury concern during the international break with Martin Zubimendi hobbling off with an apparent hamstring issue.

Zubimendi, 27, started for Spain in their blockbuster Nations League clash with England at the Wanda Metropolitano but couldn’t finish the game.



The midfielder hobbled off in the 72nd minute when manager Luis de la Fuente replaced him with Nico Williams.

And the Arsenal star appeared to have held his hamstring as he made his way to the bench.



Zubimendi was already dealing with another knock during the game as he donned a dark protective mask.

The ex-Real Sociedad star broke his nose during Arsenal’s 2-0 win over Everton last month.

However, it looks like the Spaniard’s nose won’t be the only issue the Gunners will have to deal with when he returns to north London.

An assessment will be made on Zubimendi’s fitness before Saturday’s Premier League clash at Newcastle.

The defensive midfielder saw his international team’s stunning two-year undefeated streak crashing down against England in Madrid.

Spain were 3-1 down when Zubimendi limped out of the pitch with the Three Lions playing with one man down following Elliot Anderson’s red card that led to a penalty, which was converted by Mikel Oyarzabal.

Sports.title: Thomas Tuchel questions Elliot Anderson red card after 10-man England hold off Spain
Sports.content:
Thomas Tuchel questions Elliot Anderson red card after 10-man England hold off Spain

Elliot Anderson was sent off for fouling Lamine Yamal and denying a goalscoring opportunity, with Spain scoring from the resulting penalty to set up a nervy finish in Madrid

View 2 Images Thomas Tuchel questioned the red card and penalty decision (Image: David Ramos/UEFA via Getty Images)

Thomas Tuchel claimed England’s famous victory was like the “Azteca reloaded” after they beat world champions Spain in their own backyard.

‌



‌



England produced a heroic win despite having Elliot Anderson sent off and they were made to hang on for dear life as Spain came back from 3-0 down to push for a late equaliser.

‌



It was shades of England’s win in Mexico’s Azteca Stadium when they also went down to 10 men and were left hanging on for victory to end Spain’s 43-game unbeaten run and top their Nations League group.

‌



England boss Tuchel said: “We got it [the statement win]. We got it deserved. That's even more important. We were focused on our performance and our attitude, that's what we did. Cannot praise the team high enough.

“For me, the red card was more like the Azteca reloaded. Against this team half an hour feels like two hours. Full of quality. You can see the second goal coming and it's a long, long time to overcome it. That's the way it is.

"We showed that without the red card, we had a clear win. Brilliant performance overall. We were the better team. We put out a fantastic performance from start to finish. The red card and the penalty is always a big decision - and I need to understand why it's a double punishment.

"Then it was a long, long 30 minutes - but I don't want to focus on that. There was so, so many positive things about the result after 60 minutes. It was well deserved.

Sports.title: England banish Argentina demons with gritty win over Spain after Elliot Anderson self destructs
Sports.content:
England banish Argentina demons with gritty win over Spain after Elliot Anderson self destructs

SPAIN 2-3 ENGLAND: Elliot Anderson's red card made it harder for The Three Lions, but their backs-to-the-wall defending saw them over the line in Madrid

View 4 Images England defended for their lives to get over the line (Image: Thomas COEX / AFP via Getty Images)

This should have gone down as one of England’s greatest nights.

‌



‌



Instead, it became torture as well as being unforgettable as England’s heroic 10 men overhauled the world champions with a sensational performance.

‌



Harry Kane, Ezri Konsa and Ben White put them 3-0 up and in sight of one of their best and most convincing victories on foreign soil. Then Elliot Anderson pressed the self-destruct button by getting himself sent off after some reckless defending by Jarell Quansah and England made us all suffer once more.

‌



Blimey, can’t they ever make life easy? Mikel Oyarzabal scored the penalty, Nico Williams got a second and suddenly England were manning the barricades as if they were back at the World Cup on that famous night in Mexico.

But, unlike that woeful semi-final surrender to Argentina, this time Thomas Tuchel’s braves somehow held out for a famous, gritty and heroic victory.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

England keeper James Trafford made a string of heroic saves as England saw it out to see off Spain and top their Nations League Group with a famous win in the Metropolitano Stadium.

‌



Just to remind England of the task in front of them, Spain paraded the World Cup in front of the Metropolitano Stadium before kick-off.

The reigning world and European champions went into this game on the back of a 43 game unbeaten run and you could understand why Thomas Tuchel described it as “the biggest test in world football.”

‌



Tuchel’s men just took the game to Spain from the start with a high defensive line, a high press which showed no respect to the world champions. They put them to the sword.

View 4 Images Harry Kane put England 1-0 up from the penalty spot (Image: Chris Brunskill/Getty Images)

‌



England were fast out of the blocks, Spain looked slightly bewildered and were caught on the back foot. Tuchel’s men were on a mission. This night will live long in the memory.

Within the first two minutes, Jude Bellingham was denied by an incredible save from Spain keeper Simon. Declan Rice sent over a corner, the ball carried to Bellingham whose shot looked destined for the net until Simon’s sensational reflex stop.

‌



It was all England from then on. It was surely one of the best first halves of football England have produced - and showed just what they are capable of. Lewis Hall typified England’s dominance by owning the left flank as he put Lamine Yamal in his back pocket.

View 4 Images Lewis Hall shone at left-back (Image: Michael Regan/The FA via Getty Images)

‌



Rice was booked for a foul on Yamal and the Barcelona teenager turned to the crowd to try and whip up the home support because they had been left painfully quiet.

And suddenly the 3,515 travelling fans were making all the noise. Elliot Anderson won the ball, Marc Cucurella screamed foul but Kane led a charge, cleverly waited for the challenge and was brought down by Pau Cubarsi.

‌



It was a clear penalty. But there was huge pressure on Kane’s shoulders and deafening whistles but none of that stopped England’s Captain Marvel dispatching the spot kick into the far corner in the 44th minute.

Spain are not used to losing - and took it badly. Cucurella was still protesting and it took giant Dan Burn to intervene and stop a bust-up with Ben White and Spanish players as they headed down the tunnel at half time.

‌



England’s major problem at the World Cup was not seeing the job through. But clearly all the disappointment from that Argentina collapse did not haunt them as much as inspire them this time.

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



View 4 Images James Trafford made a crucial double save late on (Image: Diego Souto/Getty Images)

Soon it was 2-0. Rice sent over another corner and there was Ezri Konsa racing into the box and headed powerfully into the net. It was an England goal straight from an Arsenal set-piece.

‌



Then, five minutes later, England were 3-0 up. Kane held the ball up, Bellingham threaded the ball through to Ben White and the Arsenal defender fired the ball through the legs of the so-called best keeper in the world.

But then England became their own worst enemies. And the nightmare of the World Cup came back to haunt them. Jarell Quansah was caught in possession, Elliot Anderson pulled back Yamal as he got himself sent off and up stepped Mikel Oyarzabal to convert.

‌



Suddenly England were down to ten men, there were shades of Mexico in the summer and a touch of Argentina as they sunk deeper with a man less.

It soon became torture. Nico Williams set up a grandstand finish as he made it 2-3 against England’s 10 men but they somehow got the job done.

England withstood a Spain comeback to end their record 43-game unbeaten run in a fiery Nations League match in Madrid.

Harry Kane opened the scoring just before half-time from the penalty spot after drawing a foul from Pau Cubarsi. Ezri Konsa powered home a free header from a corner for 2-0 before his Arsenal team-mate Ben White added a third, nutmegging Unai Simon from Jude Bellingham's incisive pass.

The Three Lions were reduced to 10 men when Elliot Anderson brought down Lamine Yamal in the box, with Mikel Oyarzabal dispatching the penalty to cut the deficit. A mistake by Anthony Gordon then allowed Yamal to tee up Nico Williams to make it 3-2 from a rapid counter-attack.

But England dug in to secure the win and top the group. Here's how John Cross rated the England players from inside the Metropolitano Stadium.

Sports.title: Pep Guardiola's stance on replacing Mauricio Pochettino as US boss after next job hint
Sports.content:
Pep Guardiola's stance on replacing Mauricio Pochettino as US boss after next job hint

Mauricio Pochettino will leave his role with the United States men's national team next week to join Manchester United - and they want Pep Guardiola to replace him

View 2 Images US Soccer want Pep Guardiola to replace Mauricio Pochettino (Image: Darren Staples/AFP via Getty Images)

Pep Guardiola is expected to 'resist' any approach from US Soccer in their search for a successor to Mauricio Pochettino.

‌



‌



Pochettino was confirmed as the new manager of Manchester United this week despite signing a contract extension with the United States men's national team until 2030 recently. The Argentine will take up his new post following the second game of the US' double-header against Haiti, who they thrashed 6-0 on Saturday.

‌



With Pochettino's departure imminent, talk has swiftly turned to potential successors with Guardiola emerging as an ambitious target for US Soccer.

‌



However, The Telegraph claim that Guardiola will resist any attempts to lure him back into management after leaving Manchester City earlier this year.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



That's because Guardiola remains determined to enjoy a year-long sabbatical following his trophy-laden decade at The Etihad. He has been unattached since walking away from City at the end of the 2025-26 campaign, meaning any potential return to management is not expected until some time in 2027.

It is no secret that Guardiola wishes to experience international management with the 55-year-old confirming back in 2024 that he wanted to lead a team at a major international tournament in the future.

‌



Guardiola has already been approached for such roles since leaving Manchester City with Italy launching a failed bid for his services earlier this year.

He was also sounded out by the Football Association for the England job while at City before Thomas Tuchel was appointed back in 2024.

‌



View 2 Images Guardiola left Manchester City at the end of the 2025/26 season (Image: Getty Images)

Guardiola lived in New York during a previous sabbatical following his time in charge at Barcelona and has reportedly had contact with US Soccer in the past.

‌



Italy's bold bid to lure Guardiola back to the dugout earlier this year failed because of his determination to enjoy time out of the game, underlining the difficulties the US may also face if they do approach the Spaniard.

Italian football federation president Giovanni Malago confirmed as much to La Repubblica, saying: “Pep was honest. He took a sabbatical, partly for family reasons, but if he’d done anything, he would have done it with us.”

Sports.title: Gianni Infantino's presidency hopes alter as Arsene Wenger makes decision on FIFA role
Sports.content:
Gianni Infantino's presidency hopes alter as Arsene Wenger makes decision on FIFA role

Arsene Wenger has chosen not to stand for FIFA presidency, which will come as a huge plus to Gianni Infantino as he looks to fend off his opponents

View 2 Images Arsene Wenger has decided not to challenge Gianni Infantino for FIFA's presidency (Image: FABRICE COFFRINI/AFP via Getty Images)

Arsene Wenger will not stand against Gianni Infantino for the FIFA presidency with the controversial figure fending off another threat to his power.

‌



‌



The deadline for nominations to be submitted is just four days away and multiple reports state that the former Arsenal boss has chosen not to challenge the man who appointed him.

‌



Arsenal is the world governing body’s chief of global football development and been considering running against Infantino, but has made the late decision to back away.

‌



Wenger was not short of backers. UEFA are desperate to rid of Infantino and even French president Emmanuel Macron was thought to have contacted his compatriot to convince the 77-year-old to put his name forward, but failed to do so.

‌



Wenger was among those who publicly condemn Infantino’s £15billion World Cup sell-off plot and was seen as Europe’s best hope of unseating the controversial football executive.

European football’s governing body has not yet announced a candidate, but had been planning to throw its power behind Wenger. His decision to back out leaves them needing to find a new plan, with a host of their major football organisations, including FA, claiming Infantino is no longer fit for the role.

‌



The only individuals who have confirmed they plan to run are Kozo Tashima, the Japanese member of the FIFA Council, and Ramon Vega, the former Tottenham defender. The latter may struggle to get the necessary backing to mount a challenge.

‌



Infantino has claimed he retains support in South America, Africa and Asia. He recently insisted he has the backing of the "vast, vast majority" of world football. He has not been without his controversy and recently saw reports accusing him of an abuse of power.

The FIFA president is alleged to have asked his office asked for 'VIP treatment' for his daughters and their pet dogs on a trip from Miami to Qatar.

It is understood his office wrote to Miami airport officials asking for someone to 'assist' three of his daughters - and their pets - through security for a personal trip to Qatar.

Sports.title: Bruno Fernandes halts Man Utd contract talks - until Mauricio Pochettino 'proves himself'
Sports.content:
Bruno Fernandes halts Man Utd contract talks - until Mauricio Pochettino 'proves himself'

Bruno Fernandes has twice rejected contract offers from Manchester United and will now hold off on any further talks whilst Mauricio Pochettino shows his hand

View 2 Images Bruno Fernandes is yet to sign a new contract at Man Utd (Image: Harry Cornish/PPAUK/Shutterstock)

Bruno Fernandes will halt anymore Manchester United contract talks until he gets a sense of what the team will look like under Mauricio Pochettino.

‌



‌



The Argentine has just been hired at Old Trafford to replace Michael Carrick, who departs with the Red Devils sitting in the relegation zone. It has been a season to forget thus far and Pochettino has a huge job if he is to revive the team immediately.

‌



The former Tottenham and PSG boss arrives with an impressive reputation, and was firmly in line for the United gig previously. But he will inherit a squad that is underperforming and under resourced, which has left Fernandes wanting to watch on for the forseeable.

‌



Fernandes remains the club's talisman and has now knocked back two fresh contract offers, with his current deal expiring at the end of the season. And even though the change of manager brings fresh hope, he wants to see how things pan out.

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



Not until he's seen what a Pochettino United side look like will he choose to commit himself to the Red Devils, who do have a one-year option in their favour, which would prevent him walking out the door for nothing this summer.

A source told The Sun: “Bruno wants to see what happens for the rest of this season before committing. His relationship with the club has been up and down in the last few years.

‌



“He enjoyed a best-ever season but is unhappy with some of the decisions since Sir Jim Ratcliffe and Ineos bought into the club. He knows Poch is a good manager but wants to see the club back him properly - he and some other players think they have been set up to fail this season.”

View 2 Images Mauricio Pochettino is the new man at the helm in Manchester

‌



It is well documented that the club didn't get all their desire summer targets, including a left-back and a No 9. That saw Lisandro Martinez take aim at the hierarchy weeks ago for failing to add to the squad.

Fernandes too let his frustration spill over earlier this year when he opened fire on Carrick and his tactics following a loss at Como. That saw him bench days later for the loss to Bournemouth, where he was jeered by sections of the home crowd.

Article continues below

Fernandes is well paid at Old Trafford and is £300,000 a week salary is just shy of the club's top earner, Marcus Rashford, who penned his deal several years ago when he was in the form of his career. Saudi clubs previously expressed an interest in Fernandes and more recently he's been linked to Turkey.

Sports.title: Grand Slam of Darts: Four seeds crash out as Greaves exits despite win
Sports.content:
Seeds Jonny Clayton, Ross Smith, Josh Rock and Luke Woodhouse were all knocked out of the Grand Slam of Darts on Sunday, while Beau Greaves was also eliminated.

Fifth seed Clayton was demolished 5-1 in barely 10 minutes by former world champion Rob Cross, who posted an impressive 114 average and finishing stats of 83 per cent.

Clayton was the second seed to be eliminated on Sunday after 15th-seed Luke Woodhouse lost 5-1 to Krzysztof Ratajski.

In the final match of the afternoon session, eighth seed Josh Rock knew he could not afford to lose three legs to Kevin Doets, but he ultimately lost the match 5-3.

And in the evening session, sixth seed Smith beat Gabriel Clemens 5-4, but conceded too many legs and exits the tournament following Saturday's shock loss to Rusty-Jake Rodriguez.

Meanwhile, three-time Women's World Matchplay champion Greaves enjoyed a 5-3 win against Niels Zonneveld, but the scoreline was not enough to keep her in the competition.

Lisa Ashton, Cam Crabtree, Raymond Smith, Adam Sevada, Maik Kuivenhoven, Jan Schmidt, Carl Sneyd and Joe Hunt also had group-stage exits confirmed on Sunday.

Sunday's Grand Slam of Darts results

Group A: Niels Zonneveld 3-5 Beau Greaves

Beau Greaves recovered from 3-1 down to beat Niels Zonneveld 5-3, but the scoreline was not good enough to see her progress from this year's 'Group of Death'.

Greaves dominated her opponent in the second half of the match, but her 5-2 defeat to Luke Littler on Saturday night sees her once again fail to get out of a group with The Nuke now the hot favourite to progress to the last 16.

Group B: Alan Soutar 5-2 Lisa Ashton

Lisa Ashton will need to wait another year for her first win in the Grand Slam of Darts, as she fell to a 5-2 loss to Alan Soutar. That result means whoever wins Monday's clash between Soutar and Jermaine Wattimena will progress.

Group C: Josh Rock 3-5 Kevin Doets

After losing his opening match to Tommy Morris on Saturday, Premier League star Josh Rock knew he needed to beat Kevin Doets and concede no more than two legs in order to stay in the tournament.

However, Doets posted a 100 average and five 180s as he stormed to a 5-3 victory to eliminate Rock and set up a Monday night showdown with Morris.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Cam Crabtree nailed a mega 146 checkout against Ricky Evans during their Group K clash

Group D: Cameron Menzies 5-4 Raymond Smith

Cameron Menzies fought back from 3-1 down to beat Raymond Smith 5-4 and set up a Monday night decider with Stephen Bunting to see who tops the group.

A spectacular 162 finish in the sixth leg levelled the scores and helped to eliminate the unfortunate Smith, who lost final-leg deciders in both of his matches at the Grand Slam.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Take a look as Wayne Mardle was left in hysterics after Joe Hunt dropped a dart whilst trying to juggle

Group E: Sebastian Bialecki 5-4 Joe Hunt

Joe Hunt averaged more than 94 and threw a dozen 140s, but was still eliminated from the Grand Slam of Darts in a thrilling 5-4 defeat to Sebastian Bialecki on Sunday evening.

The Polish player edged a last-leg decider to pick up two points and he will now face Gerwyn Price on Monday night to decide who reaches the knockout stage.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Andrew Gilding punished Charlie Manby's wayward finishing to win their Grand Slam match on the bullseye

Group F: Andrew Gilding 5-4 Charlie Manby

Andrew Gilding averaged just 81, but still found a way to eliminate Charlie Manby from the Grand Slam with a 5-4 victory.

Manby missed his first 12 darts at double in the match before recovering to establish a 3-2 lead, but his opponent won three of the final four legs, ultimately securing the win with a classy 124 checkout on bullseye. He will face Ryan Searle on Monday to decide who progresses.

Group G: Jonny Clayton 1-5 Rob Cross

Jonny Clayton won the opening leg of his must-win clash against Rob Cross, but didn't attempt another double as he was knocked out of the tournament in brutal fashion.

Cross reeled off five legs in a row, including finishes of 138 and 137 in a ruthless performance and will look to take that form into his group decider with Anton Ostlund on Monday.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Niko Springer almost threw an amazing three 'Robin Hoods' in his match against Adam Sevada

Group H: Niko Springer 5-1 Adam Sevada

Niko Springer managed TWO Robin Hoods (where a dart lands in the flight of a previous dart and scores no points) but still cruised to a 5-1 win over Adam Sevada.

That means the winner of Springer's clash with Wessel Nijman on Monday night will reach the last 16.

Group I: Joe Cullen 2-5 Paolo Nebrida

Joe Cullen suffered a surprise defeat to Paolo Nebrida who kept his hopes of qualification alive with a 5-2 victory.

In a game of poor-quality finishing, the players missed 30 darts at a double between them in seven legs, and while Luke Humphries is now a heavy favourite to progress from Group I, all three players can still technically qualify.

Group J: Luke Woodhouse 1-5 Krzysztof Ratajski

World No 17 Luke Woodhouse became one of the biggest casualties of the tournament so far as he lost five legs in a row in a 5-1 defeat to Krzysztof Ratajski.

That makes it two defeats in two games for 'Woody', while Ratajski will take on Tom Sykes on Tuesday night to decide who makes it into the next round.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Cam Crabtree nailed a mega 146 checkout against Ricky Evans during their Group K clash

Group K: Ricky Evans 5-4 Cam Crabtree

After losing 5-1 to James Wade on Saturday, Cam Crabtree needed to avoid losing two legs against Ricky Evans on Sunday to stay in the competition.

The pair served up a quickfire contest to the Wolverhampton crowd and Crabtree missed two match darts, but was ultimately knocked out by Evans who will now face Wade to decide the group.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Take a look as Henry Coates roared after hitting a sensational 130 against Jeffrey De Graaf

Group L: Jeffrey de Graaf 4-5 Henry Coates

Henry Coates took Michael van Gerwen to a last-leg decider on Saturday night and the 20-year-old was involved in another thriller on Sunday as he beat Jeffrey de Graaf 5-4.

The result means all three players could still technically qualify from the group.

Group M: Bradley Brooks 5-3 Carl Sneyd

Carl Sneyd's tournament was ended by an impressive display from Bradley Brooks, who threw five 180s and averaged more than 97 in a 5-3 win.

Brooks will now take on third seed Gian van Veen on Tuesday night, seeking an upset victory to make his way into the second round.

Group N: Martin Schindler 5-0 Jan Schmidt

Martin Schindler whitewashed Jan Schmidt 5-0 in the opening match of the evening session to eliminate his fellow German from the tournament.

Both players struggled on their doubles, but Schindler is the only player who hasn't lost a leg and can now focus on Tuesday's winner-takes-all clash with Chris Dobey to decide who tops the group.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Take a look as Gabriel Clemens hit a classy 130 bullseye checkout against Ross Smith

Group O: Ross Smith 5-4 Gabriel Clemens

Ross Smith was one of the favourites to win the Grand Slam of Darts, but exits at the group stage despite a gutsy win over Gabriel Clemens.

The European champion needed to win 5-3 or better to keep his tournament hopes alive, but a checkout ratio of less than 19 per cent proved his undoing.

Group P: Karel Sedlacek 4-5 Maik Kuivenhoven

Maik Kuivenhoven was eliminated from the tournament but still recovered from 4-1 down to beat Karel Sedlacek 5-4.

That leaves Sedlacek needing a big win over Nathan Aspinall on Tuesday night to qualify.

Sports.title: England talking points: Tuchel learns Argentina lesson as full-backs shine
Sports.content:
After England beat Spain in their own back yard in a statement result, we look at the main talking points from a memorable moment in Madrid...

Bold England show their strengths with front-foot approach

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Thomas Tuchel believes victory over world champions Spain was England's best performance so far under his leadership

England's football DNA has been in focus this autumn. In Madrid, we saw the English style at its best. From the first whistle, England were boldly on the front foot, overwhelming Spain with pace, power and directness.

They snapped into tackles and gave short shrift to their opponents when they called for fouls. It was physical, it was aggressive. It was certainly not England trying to replicate the Spanish style.

The set-piece routine for the second goal was a reflection of how those phases have risen in importance in the Premier League and fittingly saw two Arsenal players combine to score it. Then, when down to 10 men, there was fight, heart and commitment to get over the line.

Roy Keane called England's performance "perfect" at half-time. The errors from Jarell Quansah, Elliot Anderson and Anthony Gordon meant it certainly couldn't be called that in the end. But England's attitude and approach outweighed their mistakes. This is football England fans will get behind.

Peter Smith

Tuchel has learned from the Argentina game

Image: Tuchel was more measured in his substitutions

Tuchel didn't want to be drawn too much on comparisons between this win and the World Cup semi-final loss to Argentina.

He signalled a few times that the main takeaways about his team should come in the first 65 minutes before the red card - and even said the dogged defensive display was more like the last 16 win over Mexico. "The Azteca reloaded," he said.

But the England manager has clearly learned his lessons from the Argentina heartbreak. This was a very different approach to hanging on.

There was no back five this time. Not for a single second, even with the man disadvantage. It was so different to the World Cup. Against Argentina, he went to a back five on 72 minutes. Against Mexico, it was Dan Burn time on 75 minutes.

But Elliot Anderson's red card prompted no panic from the England bench. Anderson's hole was replaced by Jude Bellingham, who shifted back from the No 10 role. The first sub came with 10 minutes to go. Burn was only introduced on 89 minutes, but only for another defender.

There was trust from the England manager that his team could hold off the best team in the world in a back four defensive shape. That confidence led to a composed challenge, whereas against Argentina, there wasn't that faith.

And as a result, England fans have more faith in Tuchel.

Sam Blitz

Kane shows his Ballon d'Or class

Image: Kane did brilliantly to win the penalty that he eventually converted

'Harry Kane, he's the best in the world' sang the England supporters about their Ballon d'Or winner, goading their Spanish hosts and a certain Lamine Yamal who finished in third place for the coveted prize.

In the build-up to this game, Spain player after Spain player came out to say their team-mate should have won it instead of Kane. But England's captain showed his brilliance where it mattered - on the pitch.

He won and coolly converted the penalty for the opening goal. Nerves of steel after crucially missing from the spot against the same opponents in September. He helped orchestrate the third goal, too, which was just one example of his many connections with Jude Bellingham.

England's record scorer and record appearance-maker is at the peak of his powers right now.

Peter Smith

Hall stars in battle with Lamine Yamal

Image: Lewis Hall won the battle up against Lamine Yamal

This was the night Lewis Hall went to a whole new level.

He won praise earlier this year for the way he marshalled Lamine Yamal at St James' Park in the Champions League. But Barcelona put seven past Newcastle in the second leg of that tie, so there was no guarantee this would be a positive experience for the left-back.

Hall, however, leaves Madrid with the England left-back spot nailed down and plenty wondering why he wasn't at the World Cup.

There was brilliant defending, including a couple of tackles just before half-time where he single-handedly stopped Lamine Yamal and Mikel Merino in the England box. And even in the final seconds, he expertly won a goal-kick when Alex Baena threatened.

His appetite to take the game to Spain also impressed. He made five dribbles, epitomising England's front-foot gameplan. An all-round excellent display.

Peter Smith

And don't forget Ben White too!

Image: Ben White has completed an incredible England comeback

Imagine scoring to put England 3-0 up against Spain in Madrid and it's not your best moment of the match.

For Ben White, that standout moment came on 84 minutes. With Nico Williams bearing down on goal, White pulled off a superb sliding challenge as the last defender to prevent the one-on-one.

It was like Djed Spence against Argentina all over again, only this time England got the job done.

Image: White denied Nico Williams a Spain equaliser with a last-ditch tackle as the last defender

White has completed an incredible comeback in England colours. For so long, many thought he'd never play for his country again. Many have hounded him for coming back into the fold.

But this time the headlines are not about England fans booing him. Now it's whether he can hold down this right-back spot as his own.

Like Hall at left-back, England's right-back spot has been far from settled. White is England's sixth starting right-back in their last 11 games, dating back to the start of the World Cup knockout stages.

But this was a reminder of how good White is, why he deserves his England spot after impressing for the best club team in the country.

Sam Blitz

Trafford makes his case to be No 1

Tuchel was keen to play down talk of James Trafford ousting Jordan Pickford as England's No 1 after the game. But the young goalkeeper showed he has the ability to shine on the biggest stage in Madrid.

His double save late in the game was a decisive moment, with his reactions to keep out the second, deflected shot razor sharp. Tuchel was equally keen to praise his distribution and composure as England built up from deep.

He may have conceded four goals in two appearances against Spain in this Nations League group phase but he comes out of this period with his reputation enhanced and as the clear challenger to Pickford.

The Everton shot-stopper has never let England down but if the changing of the guard is to come in the near future, Trafford is in pole position to step in.

Peter Smith

England find out who they will face in the Nations League quarter-finals when the draw takes place on Friday November 20 at 11am.

The two-legged ties are scheduled for the March international break, with the first legs to be played between March 25 and 27 and the second legs between March 28 and 30.

Sports.title: Ten-man England hold on to claim famous win over Spain
Sports.content:
England withstood a Spain fightback after Elliot Anderson's red card to secure a famous 3-2 victory and finish above the world champions at the top of their Nations League group.

Thomas Tuchel's side were sensational for an hour in Madrid, taking the lead when Harry Kane scored a penalty at the end of the first half and then adding quickfire goals from Ezri Konsa and Ben White.

But a one-sided game was turned on its head when Elliot Anderson was sent off for a last-man foul on Lamine Yamal following Jarell Quansah's error, allowing Mikel Oyarzabal to score from the spot.

Spain reduced the deficit to one goal when substitute Nico Williams converted Lamine Yamal's cross after Anthony Gordon had been dispossessed, but England clung on thanks to James Trafford.

Image: Bellingham and Kane celebrate England's win over Spain

The goalkeeper, selected ahead of Jordan Pickford, made a string of saves as Spain peppered the England goal, including a stunning double stop when he denied Fermin Lopez then somehow pushed Oyarzabal's follow-up around the post at full stretch.

His heroics, in addition to a vital last-man challenge by White on Williams, allowed the Three Lions to end Spain's 43-game unbeaten run with a historic victory which ensures they will be seeded in the Nations League quarter-final draw.

Image: Harry Kane was fouled by Pau Cubarsi for England's penalty

Image: Kane dispatched the penalty for his 93rd England goal

It appeared certain to be a more emphatic victory when White drilled the third goal through the legs of Unai Simon after Konsa had headed in Declan Rice's corner for the second. Spain had not even registered a shot on target at that point.

But Anderson's red card, after Quansah was caught on the ball by Lamine Yamal, reinvigorated Spain and meant England had to show the qualities demonstrated in their World Cup last-16 win over Mexico at the Azteca Stadium in July.

Their steel, and the contribution of their goalkeeper, got them over the line - and showed evidence of progress from their World Cup semi-final exit to Argentina, when they lost their lead late on.

Image: James Trafford celebrates his double save with Ezri Konsa

Tuchel: We were at the highest level

England boss Thomas Tuchel:

"We are fully aware of the performance we put out there for 60-65 minutes. To be 3-0 up and deservedly 3-0 up.

"Of course the red card and penalty changed the momentum and the characteristic of the game. Thirty minutes against Spain, in Spain, feels like three hours.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Thomas Tuchel believes victory over world champions Spain was England's best performance so far under his leadership

"That is the statement and significance of this victory: that it was deserved and the result followed the performance.

"It was on the highest level in terms of belief, team spirit and togetherness. It was on highest level football wise on all aspects of the game.

"That was an excellent performance. A wonderful feeling in the dressing room. Everyone was very tired. We overcame some difficult moments.

"We're aware what steps we took now after the World Cup. It's the best feeling."

Rice: We knew we were going to beat them

England midfielder Declan Rice to ITV:

"We knew we could beat them. We knew we were going to beat them today.

"The message from the manager after the Croatia game was so positive. The message from the boys, everyone pushing together, knowing that we're going to come here and not sit back and hit them on the counter.

"We knew from the first minute - our first 10 minutes was probably the best we've played in a 10-minute spell. Pressure, pressure, pressure, we could have had two or three.

"The red card changes the course of the game as it could have been a couple more goals if I'm being honest."

Analysis by Sky Sports' Peter Smith:

England's football DNA has been in focus this autumn. In Madrid, we saw the English style at its best. From the first whistle, England were boldly on the front foot, overwhelming Spain with pace, power and directness.

They snapped into tackles and gave short shrift to their opponents when they called for fouls. It was physical, it was aggressive. It was certainly not England trying to replicate the Spanish style.

The set-piece routine for the second goal was a reflection of how they have risen in importance in the Premier League and fittingly saw two Arsenal players combine to score it. Then, when down to 10 men, there was fight, heart and commitment.

Roy Keane called England's performance "perfect" at half-time. The errors from Quansah, Anderson and Gordon meant it certainly couldn't be called that in the end. But England's attitude and approach outweighed their mistakes.

This is football England fans will get behind.

Sports.title: Grand Slam permutations: How Littler can be knocked out on Monday
Sports.content:
The Grand Slam of Darts has a brutal new format for 2026, which means every match on Monday and Tuesday night has something riding on it.

The 48-player field is split into 16 groups of three with only one going through, meaning each player has only two pool matches to try and earn a place in the second round.

Monday sees the conclusion of Groups A-H with Groups I-P to be concluded on Tuesday.

Read on to see how Luke Littler, Luke Humphries and Nathan Aspinall can all lose their final matches and still qualify for the last 16...

Group A

Sat Nov 14: Luke Littler 5-2 Beau Greaves

Luke Littler 5-2 Beau Greaves Sun Nov 15: Niels Zonneveld 3-5 Beau Greaves

Niels Zonneveld 3-5 Beau Greaves Mon Nov 16: Luke Littler v Niels Zonneveld

Luke Littler can afford to lose to Niels Zonneveld on Monday night and still have a chance of progressing.

The Nuke simply needs to win three legs to reach the last 16 with Zonneveld needing to win 5-2 or better to reach the knockout stages.

Beau Greaves is one of the few players to be eliminated despite winning one of her matches.

Group B

Sat Nov 14: Jermaine Wattimena 5-2 Lisa Ashton

Jermaine Wattimena 5-2 Lisa Ashton Sun Nov 15: Alan Soutar 5-2 Lisa Ashton

Alan Soutar 5-2 Lisa Ashton Mon Nov 16: Jermaine Wattimena v Alan Soutar

Lisa Ashton has been eliminated after losing both of her first two matches, which means whoever wins Monday's match between Jermaine Wattimena and Alan Soutar will reach the last 16.

Group C

Sat Nov 14: Josh Rock 2-5 Tommy Morris

Josh Rock 2-5 Tommy Morris Sun Nov 15: Josh Rock 3-5 Kevin Doets

Josh Rock 3-5 Kevin Doets Mon Nov 16: Kevin Doets v Tommy Morris

Eighth seed Josh Rock has been eliminated after two defeats, which means whoever wins the Kevin Doets v Tommy Morris clash on Monday will qualify for the knockout round.

Group D

Sat Nov 14: Stephen Bunting 5-4 Raymond Smith

Stephen Bunting 5-4 Raymond Smith Sun Nov 15: Cameron Menzies 5-4 Raymond Smith

Cameron Menzies 5-4 Raymond Smith Mon Nov 16: Stephen Bunting v Cameron Menzies

Two last-leg defeats mean that Raymond Smith has been eliminated from the competition. Cameron Menzies will face Stephen Bunting in a winner-goes-through decider on Monday.

Group E

Sat Nov 14: Gerwyn Price 5-3 Joe Hunt

Gerwyn Price 5-3 Joe Hunt Sun Nov 15: Sebastian Bialecki 5-4 Joe Hunt

Sebastian Bialecki 5-4 Joe Hunt Mon Nov 16: Gerwyn Price v Sebastian Bialecki

Joe Hunt crashed out after losing both of his match, so Gerwyn Price and Sebastian Bialecki will clash on Monday night with the winner reaching the knockout rounds.

Group F

Ryan Searle 5-4 Charlie Manby Sun Nov 15: Andrew Gilding 5-4 Charlie Manby

Andrew Gilding 5-4 Charlie Manby Mon Nov 16: Ryan Searle v Andrew Gilding

Luke Humphries 5-3 Paolo Nebrida Sun Nov 15: Joe Cullen 2-5 Paolo Nebrida

Joe Cullen 2-5 Paolo Nebrida Tue Nov 17: Luke Humphries v Joe Cullen

In Group I, all three players are still in the tournament.

Luke Humphries needs to win four or five legs against Joe Cullen on Monday night to reach the last 16. A 5-4 defeat would still be enough for him to qualify.

Cullen must win that match 5-0 to get through - while Paolo Nebrida will reach the last 16 if Cullen wins by a scoreline of 5-1, 5-2 or 5-3.

Group J

Sat Nov 14: Luke Woodhouse 3-5 Tom Sykes

Luke Woodhouse 3-5 Tom Sykes Sun Nov 15: Luke Woodhouse 1-5 Krzysztof Ratajski

Luke Woodhouse 1-5 Krzysztof Ratajski Tue Nov 17: Krzysztof Ratajski v Tom Sykes

Luke Woodhouse became the first seed to be eliminated from the competition as he lost both of his group matches. Whoever wins Tuesday night's match between Krzysztof Ratajski and Tom Sykes will therefore qualify for the knockout rounds.

Group K

Sat Nov 14: James Wade 5-1 Cameron Crabtree

James Wade 5-1 Cameron Crabtree Sun Nov 15: Ricky Evans 5-4 Cameron Crabtree

Ricky Evans 5-4 Cameron Crabtree Tue Nov 17: James Wade v Ricky Evans

Cam Crabtree was beaten in both of his Group K matches, which means this is another pool where the final match will decide the winner. James Wade will take on Ricky Evans on Tuesday with the winner going through.

Group L

Image: Group L

Sat Nov 14: Michael van Gerwen 5-4 Henry Coates

Michael van Gerwen 5-4 Henry Coates Sun Nov 15: Jeffrey de Graaf 4-5 Henry Coates

Jeffrey de Graaf 4-5 Henry Coates Tue Nov 17: Michael van Gerwen v Jeffrey de Graaf

This is the group where things could get very interesting with all three players still in contention to top the group.

Any sort of win for Michael van Gerwen on Tuesday will see him qualify for the last 16. However, a victory of 5-3 or better would see Jeffrey de Graaf take top spot.

If De Graaf was to beat Van Gerwen 5-4 then Henry Coates would still be in the mix as all three players would be tied.

The group would then be decided on legs won against throw and then the highest total tournament average (to two decimal places).

Group M

Sat Nov 14: Gian van Veen 5-2 Carl Sneyd

Gian van Veen 5-2 Carl Sneyd Sun Nov 15: Bradley Brooks 5-3 Carl Sneyd

Bradley Brooks 5-3 Carl Sneyd Tue Nov 17: Gian van Veen v Bradley Brooks

Group M is another group where the final match is a straight shoot-out for a place in the last 16. That match will take place between Gian van Veen and Bradley Brooks after Carl Sneyd was eliminated following two defeats in his first two matches.

Group N

Sat Nov 14: Chris Dobey 5-2 Jan Schmidt

Chris Dobey 5-2 Jan Schmidt Sun Nov 15: Martin Schindler 5-0 Jan Schmidt

Martin Schindler 5-0 Jan Schmidt Tue Nov 17: Chris Dobey v Martin Schindler

Jan Schmidt lost both of his matches to drop out of the tournament, which means it's a straight shootout between Chris Dobey and Martin Schindler on Tuesday night to see who tops the group.

Group O

Sat Nov 14: Ross Smith 3-5 Rusty-Jake Rodriguez

Ross Smith 3-5 Rusty-Jake Rodriguez Sun Nov 15: Ross Smith 5-4 Gabriel Clemens

Ross Smith 5-4 Gabriel Clemens Tue Nov 17: Gabriel Clemens v Rusty-Jake Rodriguez

Gabriel Clemens is one of the few players to have lost a match but can still qualify for the last 16. He must beat Rusty-Jake Rodriguez 5-3 or better to top Group O.

Rusty-Jake Rodriguez simply needs to win four legs to qualify. A victory of a 5-4 defeat would be enough for him.

Group O favourite Ross Smith has already been eliminated, but can still finish second in the group if Rodriguez wins Tuesday's final match.

Group P

Sat Nov 14: Nathan Aspinall 5-1 Maik Kuivenhoven

Nathan Aspinall 5-1 Maik Kuivenhoven Sun Nov 15: Karel Sedlacek 4-5 Maik Kuivenhoven

Karel Sedlacek 4-5 Maik Kuivenhoven Tue Nov 17: Nathan Aspinall v Karel Sedlacek

Nathan Aspinall doesn't even need to win on Tuesday night. He will qualify if he wins just three legs against Karel Sedlacek.

After throwing away a 4-1 advantage against Maik Kuivenhoven, Karel Sedlacek knows he must beat Aspinall 5-2 or better if he wants to reach the next round.

Kuivenhoven has been eliminated from the tournament but will finish second in the group if Aspinall wins.

How does the new format work?

Instead of eight groups of four, the expanded 48-player field is now split into 16 groups of three.

Rather than the top two in each group progressing like in previous editions, only the top player from each group will progress.

In the group stage, two points will be awarded for a win, and no points are awarded for a defeat.

Should there be a three-way points tie in any group after the round-robin games have been played, these would be split as follows:

Total leg difference

Total legs won

Total legs won against throw

Highest total tournament average (to two decimal places)

Highest winning match average (to two decimal places)

If players cannot be split after the above criteria, a play-off will be organised between the players at the end of the session in which the final group game is played and will be a two or three-way nine-dart shootout in which the player scoring the most points is deemed the winner.

The order of throw would be determined by PDC ranking, with the highest ranked player having the option to throw first, second, or third.

Following the completion of the Group Stage, each group winner will progress to the knockout stage from the last 16 onwards, and the tournament will proceed in bracket order as follows:

Winner Group A v Winner Group B

Winner Group C v Winner Group D

Winner Group E v Winner Group F

Winner Group G v Winner Group H

Winner Group I v Winner Group J

Winner Group K v Winner Group L

Winner Group M v Winner Group N

Winner Group O v Winner Group P

Sports.title: Arsenal's wait for home WSL win goes on after Earps masterclass
Sports.content:
Arsenal's wait for a home WSL win continues as they drew 1-1 against London City Lionesses on Sunday - their fifth draw in a row at the Emirates this season - with an inspired Mary Earps denying the Gunners victory.

While the result extends Arsenal's unbeaten home run to 24 league matches, it is becoming an increasing concern and a spectre on the shoulder that the Gunners have been unable to secure three points at the Emirates this year.

Giving her view to Sky Sports after the game, Renee Slegers - managing her 50th Arsenal game - said: "We spent more time than we normally do without the ball; partly the game plan and partly them asking questions of us on the pitch.

"We create big chances, could have done more with those. That's the frustrating part. This is the fifth [home game] and we couldn't give the fans the win. Unfortunately we couldn't do it for them."

Image: Mary Earps made a string of spectacular saves to keep London City Lionesses on level terms at Arsenal

It was two early goals that decided the fixture too. Frida Maanum scored for a second game in a row - having netted against Barcelona in the Champions League in midweek - slotting home from an Alessia Russo cross to put Arsenal ahead.

But a minute later, London City were level. Leah Williamson lost the run of the lively Izzy Goodwin, and the striker lashed into the roof of the net.

From then on, it was a goalkeeping masterclass from former England No 1 Earps especially that kept Arsenal from scoring another with her counterpart Misa Rodriguez also making her fair share of saves, albeit not as frequently.

The Gunners simply could not find a way past the inspired London City stopper as Lionesses boss Sarina Wiegman watched on from the stands.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player London City Lionesses were not behind for long as Isobel Goodwin cancelled out Frida Maanum's opener

The pick of her string of world-class saves came when she tipped a Maanum shot onto the crossbar. It came shortly after substitute Delphine Cascarino had also rattled the woodwork at the other end.

The result does little to improve either side's WSL standings, and Arsenal's hopes of finishing in the Champions League places takes another hit. They are sixth on 14 points - already six behind London City in third.

"We were happy with the one point, we wanted and needed three today," Slegers added. "Every game is three points for Arsenal when we play for this club.

"At the moment, with our position in the table and how we need to stay connected and compete for the top three positions for the Champions League, this one was very important for us.

"With that being said, the season isn't over. It's still November and we have to look at what it looks like in May."

10: GOAL! A sweeping move is finished by Maanum after Russo's cutback to give Arsenal the lead.

11: GOAL! London City immediately equalise as Goodwin fires into the roof of the net.

22: SAVE! Earps makes a good stop to deny Lisa Baum, who cuts in from the right-hand side.

27: SAVE! Misa Rodriguez on hand this time to deny Alexia Putellas.

29: SAVE! Again from Earps! This time it's a flying effort to keep out another Baum shot.

68: CROSSBAR! Cascarino pings an effort off the top of the woodwork.

77: DOUBLE SAVE! Earps pulls off another brilliant double save, first to deny Smith then Maanum.

85: CROSSBAR! Earps fingertips a Maanum shot onto the crossbar.

How's your luck? Arsenal face dazzling Earps as home woes continues

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Mary Earps reflects on a hard-earned point for the London City Lionesses, as former England team-mate Millie Bright heaped praise on the goalkeeper

Analysis from Sky Sports' Charlotte Marsh at the Emirates:

Before Sunday's game, Sky Sports asked whether Arsenal have lost their fear factor at the Emirates this season.

The answer surely has to be yes - although after the game, Slegers was adamant that the fear factor has not gone, despite being without a win.

Teams have come to the Emirates and sat in a low block that the Gunners have been unable to break down more than once.

London City were never going to do that. It's not in their DNA. They closer resemble the Barcelona team Arsenal faced on Thursday where, funnily enough, they drew 1-1.

But what they might not have been banking on was an ingenious performance from Earps. While Arsenal did not have to worry about defenders sitting back, they did face a goalkeeper putting in one of the performances of the season. How's your luck?

Image: Isobel Goodwin celebrates after equalising for London City Lionesses at the Emirates

She made eight saves as Arsenal continued to pepper her goal - her most in the WSL since 2017 - and the second-most in the WSL this season after the goalkeeper that replaces her at Man Utd, Phallon Tullis-Joyce.

When asked how she found the game, Earps told Sky Sports: "Tiring. It's a big point away from home.

"Either team could have won it in terms of chances. Happy with the point - would have liked three. All the girls put their bodies on the line. I love defending. It was tough today and I thought we did a good job."

It was perhaps made all the sweeter for her that her former England boss Sarina Wiegman was watching on. It is well-documented how she departed the national team, but it certainly showed the Lionesses head coach what she was missing.

Earps has had to bide her time at London City, with Elene Lete continuing to be the No 1 until recently. The former England No 1 has now started in three games, and while she is yet to keep a clean sheet, she will have staked a huge claim to the permeant spot with her performance on Sunday.

"Mary is amazing," her boss Eder Maestre said after the game. "It's not just because of the talent she has, she delivers the commitment and the togetherness that she can bring to the team because of her experience. Watching her in that performance was a pleasure."

Slegers: Players left everything on the pitch

Arsenal boss Renee Slegers to Sky Sports:

"Two good teams going against each other. I think we started the game well, score a very good goal, but we let them come back into the game too easily.

"I must say the players left everything on the pitch. They were absolutely dedicated, playing with hunger and focus. There are things in our game we must do better. We want to be dominating the ball. Being more ruthless. It's very basic but that's what it's about."

On Maanum: "She was very big for us against Barcelona and good for us tonight again. You can always count on her with runs into the box. The finish was very good."

On 50th Arsenal game: "I'm proud to represent Arsenal. I want to do everything I can for Arsenal."

Maestre: Our targets are bigger than a draw with Arsenal

London City Lionesses boss Eder Maestre to Sky Sports:

"We are happy because this kind of environment is always difficult to cope with, but at the same time, we want to win every game so we cannot be [too happy] just because it's the first time we've drawn against Arsenal.

"Our targets are even bigger. We have the hop to have the performance. We improve quite well in the second half. We had the chances, and they did as well.

"They're one of the best teams in the world and playing knowing that they need the points to push for the Champions League positions. We already knew how close it was going to be."

Sports.title: Scotland edge out Australia in Nations Championship
Sports.content:
Scotland eked out a hard-fought 15-12 win over Australia but were unable to get the bonus point they craved in a Nations Championship match that failed to catch fire.

First-half scores from Matt Fagerson and Jack Dempsey gave the Scots the edge at the break, with Harry Potter responding for the Wallabies.

Finn Russell's late penalty eventually gave the Scots some breathing space before Max Jorgensen's 80th-minute try offered the visitors a glimmer of hope but the Scots held on for a win that elevated them above Wales into fourth place in the Northern Hemisphere table.

Image: Australia's Harry Potter breaks free to score his side's first try of the game.

"When we saw the rain half an hour before kick off, you still hope you'll be able to move the ball. You could tell defences were coming off the line a bit quicker, knowing they could pressure the ball carrier," Scotland head coach Gregor Townsend told ITV,

"Both teams had to adjust and I thought we did that well. Defensively, that's one of the best performances I've seen in the last couple of years. Set after set we were putting them under pressure.

"We were on that edge of physicality but disciplined, hitting hard in the tackle, putting pressure on, listening to the referee, getting back onside. That makes it hard for the opposition to get into our 22m, which was a learning from last week.

"It was just constant effort. Today, we showed we can play another game, too."

Sports.title: England fend off fiery Spain fightback after Anderson’s red to top Nations League group
Sports.content:
It was the game to show Thomas Tuchel where his rebooted England team had got to; surely the ultimate test in international football. Spain in Spain. A world champion team who, in Tuchel’s words, had “forgotten how to lose.” Before this Nations League group decider, they had been beaten only once in 43 matches – on penalties against Portugal in the final of this competition last year.

What England produced for 65 minutes was extraordinary. What followed was equally so for different reasons. When it was over, England had made the most sensational of statements. Back in 2018, on their previous visit to Spain, England won 3-2 in Seville in the Nations League; it was one of Sir Gareth Southgate’s most famous results, an ignition point. It was the same scoreline and the same feeling for Tuchel on Sunday night.

England led 3-0. It was Harry Kane, of course, who put them in front from the penalty spot; the best player in the world damaging the best team. When Ezri Konsa and Ben White added the others, the travelling supporters were pinching themselves. With Jude Bellingham to the fore, England had run riot.

It was not over. Far from it. Everything changed when Jarell Quansah made a big error as the last man, robbed by Lamine Yamal, who got into the area and was fouled by Elliot Anderson. It was a red card for the England midfielder and a penalty for Spain. When Mikel Oyarzabal converted, it was the prompt for a siege.

Spain knocked hard at the door. They scored again through the substitute Nico Williams, created by an assist from the frankly ludicrous Lamine Yamal, a talent who sprinkles his magic liberally, and England were placed in grim survival mode. We have been here before under Tuchel and the equaliser looked on. The manager made a couple of defensive changes – Myles Lewis-Skelly for Kane and Djed Spence for Anthony Gordon. Bellingham was removed, too, and he departed shaking his head. Dan Burn came on towards the very end.

England held out. One of Tuchel’s major selection calls was to start James Trafford over Jordan Pickford in goal and he produced a remarkable stoppage-time double save to ensure England got the result they needed to leapfrog Spain and advance to the quarter-finals as the group winners. The second part of it was to deny Aymeric Laporte. It was a breathtaking moment; one to advance Trafford’s claim on the No 1 jersey. There were many others on a night that pulsed wildly from the outset – pretty much from when Spain paraded the World Cup trophy before kick-off. Had they not already had their homecoming with the gold? It was a power play.

England brought the swagger. They pressed hard on to the front foot. It was thrilling to see how they took on those in red and beat them, creating the sense of possibility. It was worth mentioning a spin move by Lewis Hall on halfway in the eighth minute when he could not afford to lose the ball. He did not, getting England up the field. There were other examples of the proactivity from other players; the desire to drop shoulders and surge forward, to be direct.

View image in fullscreen Harry Kane wheels away after opening the scoring from the spot – he got up from the foul that resulted in the penalty. Photograph: Michael Regan/The FA/Getty Images

It was England who looked likely to score first and Spain needed a superb save from Unai Simón to deny Bellingham in the early going. He ran on to a Declan Rice corner, centrally placed and, with the ball slightly behind him, he had to dig out the half-volley rather than hit it more cleanly. Simón’s reflexes were nevertheless impressive. Gordon had a shot blocked by Martín Zubimendi. Kane fizzed another one just wide.

Spain kicked out a foothold in the 15th minute. It was Lamine Yamal, inevitably, who dragged them back into it. He nutmegged Hall and blasted away from him, Rice bringing him down to pick up a yellow card. What Hall did next spoke volumes about England’s approach, not to mention his courage. It was a slicing run from him, on a diagonal towards goal, which laid waste to a host of Spain players. He almost found Morgan Rogers with his cross.

It was an excellent first half for England; Rogers bristled with confidence on the ball, Bellingham threatened. They deserved to take a lead into the interval. Bellingham appeared to be fouled by Marc Cucurella, but Anderson did not stand on ceremony, driving a first-time pass up the inside right channel for Kane, who cut inside Pau Cubarsí to set up the shot.
