Sports.title: England deliver the spectacular as Three Lions strip world champions Spain of their invincibility and give Thomas Tuchel the proof that his coaching IS working, writes OLIVER HOLT
Sports.content:
Thomas Tuchel had said he wanted evidence. He needed to believe his coaching was working. He needed to see something that told him he could help England overcome those DNA deficiencies he had identified in the aftermath of the devastating World Cup semi-final defeat to Argentina.

He needed a glimpse of his England team closing the gap to the best. He needed to cling on to the idea that they could overhaul Spain, that the work he was doing could improve England so much they could win the European Championship in 2028 and end this country’s cursed cycle of despair.

Proof of concept, he called it on Saturday night when England arrived in Madrid. ‘This will be proof of concept on the highest level,’ Tuchel predicted. ‘It's the biggest test in world football. Spain seems unbeatable but we are trying to take it away from them. We are up for something spectacular.’

Something spectacular is what Tuchel promised and something spectacular is what both he and England delivered. Spain had not lost for 43 matches, a world record, but number 44 was beyond them. For just over an hour, England destroyed them. They outplayed them. They stripped them of their invincibility.

And then, when Elliot Anderson was sent off after 63 minutes for pulling back Lamine Yamal, and Spain stormed back into the game, England somehow managed to hold on for a momentous victory in the screaming, yelling cauldron of the Metropolitano. This was proof alright. This was proof positive.

Sure, it was nervy for half an hour. And, yes, England nearly found a way to throw it away. But the way they played when it was 11 v 11 was enough for any England fan to believe that England under Tuchel can climb back to the summit of a major tournament and gaze down on a view they have not seen for 60 years.

England recorded a famous victory over Spain in Madrid as they won a five-goal thriller

Elliot Anderson's red card opened the door for the world champions to mount a comeback

James Trafford made a superb double save in stoppage time to preserve England's lead

Yes, this was a Nations League dead rubber because both teams were already guaranteed progress to the quarter-finals next March, but there was no mistaking its wider significance. This was proof England are good enough to turn away from the trail of tears that has been their path for so long. Before the game, Spain had held the World Cup aloft again as one final reminder of England’s failure but by the end, by the time goalkeeper James Trafford had added to the drama with a miraculous double save, the glory and the 3-2 triumph was England’s.

Spain had won their last 12 matches in succession and the sport’s last two major tournament. They had not been beaten since March 2024 and had not lost at home since September 2022. England ended that run with 10 men. What a night. It was a special kind of crazy.

England had celebrated Harry Kane’s Ballon d’Or triumph and caps record at Wembley last week but Spain took things a stage further before the game. The boys who won the U15 World Cup were introduced to the crowd. Then the World Cup itself was carried on for goalkeeper Unai Simon to hold aloft.

England ignored it all. They started the game like an express train. They nearly took the lead inside the first two minutes when Jude Bellingham met a corner from Declan Rice on the edge of the six-yard-box and was only denied by a brilliant reaction save from Simon. Gordon’s follow-up was destined for the bottom corner before it was blocked by a Spain defender.

Spain were rattled. The crowd whistled. England forced their opponents into mistake after mistake at the back. From one of those successful presses, Kane drilled a shot inches wide. Gordon, who has made such a fine start to his Barcelona career, revelled on the stage and caused right back Marc Pubill all manner of anxieties.

Spain could barely break out of their own half but when they did, after a quarter of an hour, Yamal ran at Lewis Hall and nutmegged him before Rice chopped the teenager down. Rice was booked by French referee Clement Turpin and Lamal windmilled his hands in the air to wind up the crowd.

Pubill was replaced midway through the half. It looked like an injury but it could have been hurt pride or twisted blood. Gordon had barely given him a moment’s rest. In fact, Gordon was tireless. He harried Martin Zubimendi off the ball with ease and almost set up a chance for Bellingham.

England got the goal they deserved a minute before half-time. The build-up was controversial. Anderson played a fine through ball to Kane that doubled as a crunching tackle on Marc Cucurella. Cucurella went down as if he had been shot, which is what Cucurella always does.

Ben White slotted the ball through the keeper's legs after a brilliant England move

Harry Kane celebrates goal No 93 for England after giving them the lead from the penalty spot

The referee allowed play to continue. Kane advanced on goal and turned inside Pau Cubarsi, Spain’s brilliant young defender. Cubarsi brought him down and the referee pointed to the spot. Cucurella still lay prone. Bellingham, his Real Madrid teammate, leaned over him and told him what he thought of him.

There were a whole host of VAR checks but England passed all of them. The crowd whistled their distaste. Kane missed a penalty in the Wembley game between these two teams in September but he did not miss this one. Simon guessed the right way but Kane hit it too fiercely and it bulged the back of the net. It was his 93rd goal for England.

Spain are not used to being bossed around like this. Tempers flared after the whistle blew for half-time. Ben White and Fabian Ruiz joined in a disagreement of some sort and soon there was a flurry of pushing and shoving. It stopped short of being a melee but it was obvious Spain were shaken.

Eight minutes into the second half, England went further ahead. Rice swung a corner into the centre of the box and, as the usual wrestling match unfolded, Ezri Konsa ran in gloriously unmarked and nodded the ball down and past the helpless Simon from close range.

Four minutes later, against a general backdrop of disbelief, England were three ahead. What a goal it was, too. Bellingham, who had been his usual superhuman self, muscled his way free in the centre and fed the ball out to Kane.

Kane held the ball up and played it back to Bellingham on the edge of the box. Bellingham spotted the overlapping run of White and found him with a clever pass. White took a touch and slotted the ball past Simon. It was the Arsenal full-back’s first competitive England start, too. Maybe now England fans will stop booing him.

This was the night Thomas Tuchel had been crying out for as he got the evidence he demanded

Ezri Konsa met Declan Rice's set-piece to plant an unstoppable header in the back of the net

But then, midway through the half, England gave Spain a lifeline. Jarell Quansah was caught in possession by Yamal and as Yamal bore down on goal, Anderson pulled him back. Anderson was shown a red card and Spain were awarded a penalty. Oyarzabal waited for Trafford to commit himself and then stroked the ball into the opposite corner.

The atmosphere in the stadium was transformed. Spain sensed vulnerability in England for the first time. Fifteen minutes from time, they pulled another goal back. Yamal sprinted away down the right and slid the ball into the middle for substitute Nico Williams, who sidefooted it past Trafford.

Now, it was like the Alamo. Yamal tormented England. Trafford dived at full length to push away one of his shots and then got down at his near post to divert a shot that was creeping in. White produced another of the moments of the night with a flying block to keep out a goalbound shot from Williams.

Spain through everything at England but England would not yield. When Trafford made that double save, everyone knew. It was to be England’s night. Tuchel had his proof of concept.

Sports.title: Thomas Tuchel's 'best night' as England manager: Three Lions boss hails heroes after Spain victory - but hits out at Elliot Anderson decision made by referee he previously labelled a 'one out of 10'
Sports.content:
Thomas Tuchel's 'best night' as England manager: Three Lions boss hails heroes after Spain victory - but hits out at Elliot Anderson decision made by referee he previously labelled a 'one out of 10'

Thomas Tuchel hailed the 'best performance of my time as manager' after England beat world champions Spain in a crazy, brilliant see-sawing drama of a Nations League tie.

England played the best football of Tuchel's two-year reign as coach to end Spain's world record 43-match unbeaten run.

England raced into a 3-0 lead with a penalty from Harry Kane, and further goals from Ezri Konsa and Ben White.

But they played the last half an hour of the game with ten men after Elliot Anderson was sent off for pulling back Lamine Yamal.

Spain got two goals back to set up a nerve-wracking finish but goalkeeper James Trafford, in the team ahead of Jordan Pickford, pulled off a miracle double save in the dying minutes to seal the win.

'What a performance we put out there for 60 minutes to be deservedly 3-0 up,' Tuchel said after the game. 'Thirty minutes against Spain with ten men feels like three hours.

Thomas Tuchel said England's display in the win over Spain was the best in his time as boss

'It was a statement victory. It was on the highest level football-wise. It is a wonderful feeling for us in the dressing room.

'It is the best performance of my time and they are unbeaten for 43 matches and that was a complete performance in that environment. To impose our identity on them was a real achievement.

'Declan Rice said he knew we were going to win and I could feel the true belief. This was the moment we wanted to prove ourselves. You need to rely on your teammates. That is why I am very proud of the win.'

Tuchel also questioned the decision to give Anderson a straight red, made by a referee he once labelled a 'one out of 10'.

The Man City midfielder was sent off because Clement Turpin adjudged him not to have been making an attempt to play the ball when he fouled Yamal.

'The red card and the penalty is always a big decision and I needed to understand why it was a double punishment but... OK,' Tuchel told ITV Sport.

'From then it was a long 30 minutes but I don't want to focus on that because there were so, so many positives.'

Sports.title: Jarrad Branthwaite left out of England squad for Nations League decider with Spain - as James Hill and Dan Burn leapfrog defender in Thomas Tuchel's pecking order
Sports.content:
Jarrad Branthwaite has been left out of England’s matchday squad for the Nations League decider in Spain, raising questions over his future involvement under Thomas Tuchel. The Everton centre back’s omission means that two rivals who were not in the original squad but were added last week, Dan Burn and James Hill, are now seemingly ahead of him in the pecking order. There was a clue as to Tuchel’s uncertainty over Branthwaite when, ahead of last Thursday's Croatia game, he revealed concerns over his suitability to England’s way of playing. ‘Jarrad Branthwaite is doing very well but it's a very different style of play for him from Everton towards us,’ said the head coach. Tuchel then selected Burn ahead of him for the 2-1 win, and said: ‘You can see that Dan Burn is straight away a big voice in training and is more used to the style with Newcastle from the last two seasons with Eddie Howe, where they followed in a high press and man-to-man.’ It had been thought that Branthwaite, 24, could emerge as a starter at left-sided centre back, given his good club form this season. That now feels unlikely, with Burn and Marc Guehi, who is currently injured, preferred by Tuchel. Jarrad Branthwaite has been left out of the England squad for their clash against Spain James Hill and Dan Burn, who were both added to the England squad last week, appear to have jumped above Branthwaite in the pecking order Branthwaite has made two substitute appearances under the German, totalling 28 minutes. Also left out of the matchday squad for Sunday’s game in Madrid are Josh King and James Garner. Everton midfielder Garner came off the bench against Croatia at Wembley and thought he had scored his first England goal, only for VAR to rule it out for offside. He now misses the chance to build on that cameo against the world champions. For King, 19, the wait for a senior debut continues after his maiden call-up, a reward for an impressive start to the season with Fulham. Tuchel was forced to trim three players from his 26-man travelling squad, with the return to fitness of defenders Ezri Konsa and Djed Spence increasing competition for places.

Sports.title: Spain 2-3 England PLAYER RATINGS: Which star was the man of the match for Thomas Tuchel? Who was key to their energy and adventure? And who now deserves a run in the side?
Sports.content:
Spain 2-3 England PLAYER RATINGS: Which star was the man of the match for Thomas Tuchel? Who was key to their energy and adventure? And who now deserves a run in the side?

England secured a historic victory over Spain in the Nations League to secure top spot in their group ahead of their quarter-final matchup next year.

Thomas Tuchel's side raced out the blocks to cause the world champions trouble early on, but Unai Simon ensured Spain held firm and weathered the early storm.

England did get their reward, though, just before half-time when Harry Kane won and scored a penalty to give his side a deserved lead.

After the break, they went up a gear, with Arsenal defenders Ezri Konsa and Ben White netting to leave England in dreamland.

That was until Elliot Anderson was sent off – conceding a penalty against Lamine Yamal in the process – and Spain were back in it through Mikel Oyarzabal. Nico Williams then ensured it would be a nervy last 15 minutes for England, but they held on and secured the 3-2 victory.

Daily Mail Sport's CRAIG HOPE was in Madrid to rate the Three Lions players.

England secured a thrilling 3-2 win over Spain on Sunday to top their Nations League group

James Trafford produced a fantastic double save in stoppage time to keep his side in front

ENGLAND (4-2-3-1)

James Trafford – 8

His big test and was hardly tested first-half. That changed when down to 10 and produced three big saves, including a stunner in stoppage-time.

Ben White – 8

Solid if unspectacular… at least until spectacular, overlapping goal for England’s third. Shades of Carlos Alberto. Warrants a stay in side.

Jarell Quansah – 5

Looked composed until needless dawdling on ball that cost his team a penalty, a goal and a man. Spoilt decent display.

Ezri Konsa – 9

Furthered claims as first-choice centre back. Was commanding, organised well and headed brilliant second goal. Player of the match.

Lewis Hall – 8

Surely England’s No1 left back now. Two early dribbles were Yamal-esque. A tougher second-half and was out of position for Spain’s second.

Elliot Anderson – 6

Superb ball to free Kane for penalty and was his usual commanding self, until desperate tug on Yamal at expense of penalty and red card.

Elliot Anderson was sent off after bringing down Lamine Yamal in the penalty box at 3-0

Declan Rice – 7

Best work was in own half for most part but set-piece deliveries were teasing and accurate, including corner for Konsa goal. A strong showing.

Morgan Rogers – 6

Quieter than star-man display on Thursday but his work was diligent on right and included some classy touches.

Jude Bellingham – 8

Drove England forward second-half and was key to energy and adventure. Won corner for second and assisted third.

Anthony Gordon – 7

More energy and purpose than Croatia, even if killer ball was still missing. An honest shift and played his part.

Harry Kane – 7

Showed cunning and class to win and convert first-half penalty. Sacrificed at 2-3 after another masterclass in centre forward play.

Substitutes

Myles Lewis-Skelly (on for Kane) – 6

Dominic Calvert-Lewin (on for Gordon 83) – 6

Djed Spence (on for Bellingham 83) – 6

Dan Burn (on for White 90) – 6

Manager

Thomas Tuchel – 8

At 1-0 up against a top nation (remember Argentina) he kept his side on the front foot and was rewarded, until they went down to 10 men. A big night for the head coach.

Thomas Tuchel kept his side on the front foot when ahead against a top nation and was rewarded until the red card

SPAIN (4-3-3)

Unai Simon 5; Pubill 5 (Porro 20, 5), Cubarsi 4 (Huijsen 46, 6), Laporte 5, Cucurella 5; Merino 4 (Lopez 46, 6), Zubimendi 5 (Williams 72, 7), Fabian Ruiz 5 (Pedri 46, 6); Lamine Yamal 7, Oyarzabal 6, Baena 5

Manager

Luis de la Fuente – 5

Referee

C Turpin (France) – 7

Sports.title: PGA Tour thrown into chaos as final day of $6m tournament is called off amid dismal weather in Texas
Sports.content:
PGA Tour thrown into chaos as final day of $6m tournament is called off amid dismal weather in Texas

The final round of the Austin Championship has been postponed because of 'unplayable' conditions in Texas.

The PGA Tour event at Fazio Canyons was set to conclude on Sunday with Trace Crowe taking a one-shot lead into the final round.

But the action was postponed until Monday with the PGA Tour citing 'unplayable course conditions'.

Officials announced on Saturday that they would move tee times earlier on Sunday morning to try and beat the bad weather in Austin.

They then moved back a number of times before finally conceding defeat and shunting play back to Monday. Play will begin at 8.30am ET.

It comes just weeks after the Butterfield Bermuda Championship was shortened to just 54 holes because of high winds.

The last round of the Austin Championship was postponed because of 'unplayable' conditions

The tournament will finish Monday with Trace Crowe taking a one-shot lead into the final round

It promises to be a nervy final round in Texas with five players within two shots of Crowe, who leads on 14-under.

Chad Ramey, Sami Valimaki and Erik van Rooyen are one back on 13-under, while Max Greyserman and Ben Kohles are two back at 12-under.

At stake for Crowe is a chance to win for the first time on the PGA Tour, which comes with a spot on the elite Championship Series in 2028 with $20 million purses.

Crowe capped off a roller-coaster third round in cool, blustery conditions by holing a bunker shot for birdie and closing with a tough up-and-down for birdie that salvaged a one-under 71 on Saturday.

'I´ve been doing this long enough to know that everyone´s really good and they´re just going to keep making birdies,' Crowe said.

'My mindset tomorrow is to go attack the day and see what it gives, but just try to play the best I can and hopefully I come out on top.'

Sports.title: Ronaldinho makes return at age of 46: Brazil legend plays full first-half for Italian third-tier team and hints he may play again despite 'publicity stunt' criticism
Sports.content:
Ronaldinho makes return at age of 46: Brazil legend plays full first-half for Italian third-tier team and hints he may play again despite 'publicity stunt' criticism

Former Ballon d'Or winner Ronaldinho made a stunning comeback to professional football at the age of 46 as he turned out for a third-division Italian side on Sunday.

The former Barcelona, Paris Saint-Germain and AC Milan superstar announced his retirement from football after a short stint with Fluminense in 2015.

Having enjoyed retirement for 11 years, he shocked world football by agreeing a surprise transfer to Serie C outfit Ravenna, where he was set to undertake a marketing role.

It was initially understood that he would not be making a playing return, but the Brazil legend laced up his boots on Sunday and played a part in his side's opening goal.

Ravenna's honorary vice president Ariedo Braida said in June that the World Cup winner would regrettably not be able to play for the club due to his age.

But it appears that went up in smoke, with Ronaldinho playing 45 minutes on his return in the league clash – despite his move being dubbed a publicity stunt by the club.

Brazil icon Ronaldinho has made a stunning comeback to professional football at the age of 46

He played the first-half of the game, playing a role in the first goal for his new side

He helped set up Giulio Donati's opening goal of the match, and raced across the field to mob the goal scorer as he celebrated.

He started the game, playing the first-half before being replaced by Matteo Maggio. Before his substitution, he embraced the fans in the stands at the interval.

The icon hinted there could be more games to come, however.

He told Sky Italia after the game: 'It went by too fast, that has always been football for me.

'Is this my last one? I don't know. If the president keeps calling me, I will come back. It is always a pleasure. I told the president, if he needs me, then I will be here.

'It was lovely to be here, playing, having the build-up in the dressing room. Football has always been the most wonderful thing in my life.'

Ronaldinho has also become a shareholder in the club.

During his illustrious career, he won the World Cup, a Champions League, two LaLiga titles and a Serie A trophy before hanging up his boots in 2015.

He also won a string of individual accolades including the Ballon d'Or in 2005 and FIFA World Player of the Year in 2004 and 2005.

Sports.title: Distraught Rory McIlroy breaks down in tears as he reveals his dad Gerry has been in hospital for two months after undergoing 'huge operation'
Sports.content:
A tearful Rory McIlroy revealed his father underwent a double lung transplant and has been in hospital for two months after equalling Colin Montgomerie's record of eight Race to Dubai titles on Sunday.

The world No 2 had just secured the DP World Tour's order of merit crown for a fifth straight year in Dubai when he disclosed in a post-tournament interview that Gerry McIlroy, 67, underwent a 'huge operation' in September.

He later clarified the sheer scale of the ongoing trauma by detailing that McIlroy Snr has battled his health issues for 18 months and a transplant was the 'last resort'. McIlroy added that his father is now 'recovering well' in hospital in Cleveland, having visited him before jetting to the Middle East for the end of the DP World Tour season.

McIlroy said: 'My dad is a massive part of my life, and has been my biggest supporter, is the one that got me into the game and the one that told me to follow my dreams and never give up. It's obviously been difficult.

'He's been living with this for a while, for 18 months, and it got to the point where the last resort was he needed a transplant, so he had a double-lung transplant in September. Thankfully, operation was a success and he's recovering well.

'It's been a stressful time for our family. I've been up in Cleveland a lot because that's where he is. I didn't know if I was going to go to India (last month) because I spent nine days in the ICU with him while he was recovering.

Rory McIlroy broke down in tears as he revealed his father's ongoing health issues on Sunday

Gerry McIlroy (left) has been in hospital in Cleveland for two months after a 'huge operation'

'If things were not looking as good as they were, I probably wouldn't have felt comfortable travelling or being too far away. But he's got an amazing team up there, and the doctors and nurses are absolutely incredible.

'So I felt comfortable going to India and travelling and knowing that I could obviously get back to him if I needed to, but he was obviously in wonderful hands.

'He's been making a really steady recovery. I went up to see him before I left a couple of weeks ago, and he said to me, "Rors, go and win me The Race to Dubai".

'That was in my head for the last two weeks, and I really wanted to do it for him and I know he's in hospital in his hospital bed, and he would have been watching this morning. It was nice to be able to get it done for him.'

McIlroy often speaks about the sacrifices his father made for him to be able to reach the top of the golfing world.

Gerry has been by Rory's side throughout his life, including when he completed the Grand Slam

Gerry and Rory still maintain a healthy rivalry on the golf course and play together often

Growing up as an only child in Holywood, Northern Ireland, McIlroy's father worked multiple jobs to finance his career, with his mother Rosie doing the same.

Back in 2024, McIlroy celebrated his father's 65th birthday by playing the Old Course at St Andrews with him, and the pair still enjoy a healthy rivalry on the golf course.

McIlroy delivered on his father's wish by finishing second in the DP World Tour Championship behind Tyrrell Hatton, allowing him to pip Eugenio Chacarra on the final day of the season-long points race.

The historical significance should not be understated – matching Montgomerie's record haul is considerable in its own right, let alone for a player who spends the majority of his season on the PGA Tour.

McIlroy said: 'Winning eight Order of Merits was never really in my list of goals when I was growing up. I remember Monty being obviously a stalwart of the European Tour, going to watch him at the World Match Play at Wentworth over the years. I remember playing with him for the first time at The London Club at The European Open in 2008.

McIlroy's parents Gerry and Rosie both worked multiple jobs to be able to fund his golf career

McIlroy hugs dad Gerry and mom Rosie after winning the Masters at Augusta in April 2026

'So to pull up alongside him and to win eight of these things, yeah, it means the world to me. I'm a very proud European player. I'm proud to be a part of the DP World Tour.'

Hatton's win on the Earth Course capped a strong season, albeit a turbulent one, with the Englishman having finished third at the Masters before he went on to claim a title on the LIV circuit in June.

The 35-year-old's rebound from the demise of LIV has been impressive – this was his ninth DP World Tour crown and followed a runner-up spot in Abu Dhabi a week ago.

Hatton, whose 15-under-par total left him five clear of McIlroy, said: 'This is really special. I was really nervous today. I didn't say anything to anyone in my team, but I've had a bit of heartbreak around here, and I felt like it was going to be a difficult day. I'm just really proud. It feels so good to win here.'

Sports.title: Man Utd line up Premier League star for January transfer in boost for Mauricio Pochettino
Sports.content:
Man Utd line up Premier League star for January transfer in boost for Mauricio Pochettino

Mauricio Pochettino will be looking to add new faces to his Manchester United squad in January and the club have their sights set on Fulham's Calvin Bassey after a fine start to the season

View 2 Images Calvin Bassey is a Manchester United target for January (Image: Marc Atkins)

Calvin Bassey is emerging as a serious target for Manchester United ahead of the January transfer window, it has been claimed.

‌



‌



United are expected to be active in the winter window after installing Mauricio Pochettino as their new head coach. The Argentine arrives at Old Trafford following the club's disastrous start to the season, with Pochettino inheriting a team who have won just one of their 10 Premier League games this term.

‌



One of Pochettino's first and most important tasks will be improving United's shoddy defensive record, with the Red Devils dropping into the relegation zone after shipping 19 goals in 10 games.

‌



With defensive reinforcements highly likely to be on Pochettino's January wishlist, The Telegraph are reporting that Bassey is one player of interest.

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



The 26-year-old has impressed for Fulham this season and is viewed as a 'strong option' for United, who would benefit greatly from Bassey's pace and power.

Bassey, a Nigeria international, is into the final 12 months of his contract at Craven Cottage which could tempt Fulham into doing business mid-season for a premium price. The London outfit do, however, hold an option to keep Bassey in west London for a further year.

‌



The Fulham head coach, Alvaro Arbeloa, has lauded Bassey publicly and would like to keep the former Ajax and Rangers star. “Calvin is one of the best defenders in the Premier League,” Arbeloa said recently. “He plays at a high level with and without the ball. He is doing so well.”

View 2 Images Mauricio Pochettino will want to add to his squad in January (Image: JC Ruiz)

‌



Gary Neville highlighted the need for Manchester United to recruit new defenders in January following last week's 4-4 draw with Aston Villa. Speaking on NBC Sports, he said: “The reason Manchester United have conceded four goals is because they haven’t invested in the defence in the transfer window. Every one knew they had to do that, they needed defenders. The current ones are making mistake after mistake after mistake.

“The defenders that finished that game will get you relegated. Watch the defensive errors… we all screamed in the transfer window that they have to bring some defenders in. They had to bring the transfer budget forward and bring defenders in.”

Sports.title: Aryna Sabalenka addresses accusation she fired Russian insult at Ukraine's Elina Svitolina
Sports.content:
Aryna Sabalenka addresses accusation she fired Russian insult at Ukraine's Elina Svitolina

Aryna Sabalenka was accused of hurling a Russian insult at Elina Svitolina during her loss in the WTA Finals whilst the war in Ukraine continues

View 2 Images Aryna Sabalenka has rejected claims she insulted her opponent in Russia

Aryna Sabalenka has denied that she hurled an insult in Russian at Elina Svitolina, her Ukrainian opponent, during her loss in the WTA Finals.

‌



‌



The recently dethroned World No 1 was seen cursing during her loss to Svitolina, who secured a 6-3 3-6 6-1 success. Immediately her words were interpreted by some as a dig at her opponent, whose country remains at war with Russia.

‌



Sabalenka has denied that and maintained that her anger was directed at a section of the crowd who were cheering against her, but concedes she could've handled the situation differently.

‌



She said: “My comment was not directed at Elina. I was frustrated with a small group of spectators who were aggressively cheering my mistakes, and I reacted emotionally in the moment.

"That said, I should have handled my frustration differently, and I apologise to anyone offended. Elina played a great match, and I wish her all the best for the rest of the tournament.”

Elina Svitolina and Gael Monfils supported after divorce as 'nasty' comments cause fury READ MORE :

Since Russia's invasion into Ukrainian their players do not shake hands with Russian or Belarusian players, nor do they take pre-match photographs with each other. Svitolina has been one of the most outspoken Ukrainian athletes regarding the war and its impact.

‌



Despite that she's still called for Sabalenka to be respected. She said: "As we see there's many, many Ukrainians, many, many flags and of course they want me to win this particular match. We've played many times with Aryna. She has her fans. I have my fans.

"I just hope the matches between us [are] respected. Sometimes in some matches that we've played also there have been not great comments towards me in regards of the war. It is like this in the social media, sometimes the things are turned around a little bit."

‌



View 2 Images Elina Svitolina marched on in the WTA Finals

Svitolina recently announced her divorce from fellow tennis star Gael Monfils after five years. She cited however the Russia-Ukraine war and its emotional impact had caused her to lose herself in her marriage.

Article continues below

"When you've been living through the reality of war for more than 4.5 years, experiencing so many different situations, emotions, and difficult moments, you naturally start seeing life differently. Your perspective changes, your values and priorities shift, and you begin to understand what you truly want out of life," she said.

Svitolina will face Mirra Andreeva, this year's French Open champion, in the showpiece event of the WTA Finals after the Russian teenager hammered Linda Noskova 6-2 6-1 in the semi-finals.

Sports.title: Man Utd's January offer to Mauricio Pochettino is needed - but also a recipe for disaster
Sports.content:
So Mauricio Pochettino is set to be backed in January as he bids to turn Manchester United's season around and get his tenure off to a positive start.

Is that needed? Undoubtedly. Is it still a recipe for disaster? Absolutely.

United's recruitment post Sir Alex Ferguson has, on the whole, been pretty poor. Their January dealings have been even worse and, were it not for a certain Bruno Fernandes, then their midseason transfer business would be looked upon woefully.

The senior figures at Old Trafford missed out on a number of their targets in the summer, and the team are now feeling the impact of that. A left-back and a No 9 would be most welcome right now, but any success is dependant on quality actually being landed in those positions.

‌



As we know, that is never easy in January. And it will probably prove even harder for a club whose talent identification and scouting has not proved a strength over the past decade or so.

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

Fernandes is an example of what can go right with a January arrival, inspiring the team in his opening six months and, largely, continuing to do so ever since.

‌



But that capture in January 2020 is an outlier. Every football executive up and down the country will tell you signing players in the New Year is a tough gig. Clubs don't want to sell, so as a result they'll hike any prices. Players that are available are often making the step up from the, so called, lesser clubs. Take a look at Patrick Dorgu from Leece as an example.

In January you'll tend to sign one of four things.

Genuine quality, unlikely. Overpriced stars, Alexis Sanchez. Young stars for the future, Ayden Heaven. Or players jumping up a level or two, which is a decision you take at your risk, Dorgu.

View 3 Images Ineos have made a number of underwhelming moves in the transfer market (Image: Jacob King/Press Association)

‌



It was only last weekend that a former United player remarked that a back four containing Dorgu and Heaven would get the team relegated. They both are January signings.

In fact, since 2013 and the ending of United's dominance, the club have signed seven players permanently in January. Juan Mata, Victor Valdez, Sanchez, Fernandes , Amad, Dorgu and Heaven.

Bar Fernandes none of those could be classed as a 'hit'. That is the challenge that faces Pochettino and the Ineos hierarchy. It must be said, for all Pochettino's managerial quality, signing players hasn't actually been his greatest strength. Enter the likes of Vincent Janssen and Moussa Sissoko.

So here we have a concoction of Pochettino, an Ineos hierarchy who have shown themselves to be among England's worst decision makers and a United team whose transfer market history suggests they overpay for players who underdeliver.

‌



View 3 Images Bruno Fernandes is Man Utd's most successful January signing but others, like Patrick Dorgu, have not totally convinced

Whilst Pochettino may look at this United team and think 'I need players' - of which he is right by the way - there is also a school of thought that says bringing in two or three players who don't cut the mustard and pen two or three years deals will only set the whole project back even further.

The irony, and frustration for those sitting in the Old Trafford stands, is that their rivals have constantly shown that value and quality very much exists in the New Year's market. Virgil van Dijk heading to Liverpool, Luis Diaz's move to Anfield, Newcastle signing Bruno Guimaraes, Arsenal's capture of Martin Odegaard. To name a few.

United's neglect in the summer, which means their defence is now more than two years without a major arrival, leaves the club with little option but to go into the market in around 7 weeks time.

‌



The danger of course, as the latest new era begins, is that the fanbase watch the club and their hugely unpopular owners undertake business that will only set the club back even further.

Sports.title: Man Utd flops face brutal Mauricio Pochettino ban with Michael Carrick rule changed
Sports.content:
Man Utd flops face brutal Mauricio Pochettino ban with Michael Carrick rule changed

Mauricio Pochettino is set to change one of Michael Carrick's rules after becoming Manchester United head coach for their Premier League match against Liverpool

View 2 Images Mauricio Pochettino is set to make one change straightaway as Manchester United's head coach (Image: Eston Parker/ISI Photos, ISI Photos via Getty Images)

Mauricio Pochettino will reportedly not grant Manchester United players a day off following matches and instead have them report to Carrington for recovery sessions. Michael Carrick is understood to have seldom demanded the squad be at their training ground the day after fixtures.

‌



‌



However, the new head coach will apparently insist that they turn up for recovery work. Carrick and the United squad were notably not at Carrington on Monday following their 4-4 draw with Aston Villa at Old Trafford.

‌



Several international call-ups reduced the club's first-team squad this week. The Sun reports Pochettino is implementing the shift to boost their fitness levels. His eldest son, Sebastiano, is also arriving as a specialist coach dedicated to that department.

‌



Man Utd already complete first transfer of Mauricio Pochettino era as wonderkid signs READ MORE :

Man Utd star sends alarming message to Mauricio Pochettino as he confirms blow READ MORE :

Charlie Owen is already a fitness coach at the club and has been for more than seven years since stepping up from the academy. His involvement has seen him work with Carrick, Erik ten Hag, Ole Gunnar Solskjaer and Ruben Amorim.

The latter, like Pochettino, brought his own fitness coach to United, Paulo Berreira. However, he departed with Amorim in January, and they have since been reunited in Milan.

Make sure you don't miss the best Man Utd coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



View 2 Images Sebastiano Pochettino has become the fitness coach in his father's support staff (Image: John Dorton/ISI Photos/USSF, Getty Images)

Toby Alderweireld, who spent five seasons working with Pochettino at Tottenham Hotspur, has warned United's underperforming squad what to expect. He told the BBC: "First of all, he made us very fit. Pre-season was brutal.

‌



"The way he wants to play - on the front foot, putting people under pressure, a high line, very dynamic play - you need to run. You need to be capable of running and be capable of high-intensity runs - the basic is to be fit.

"Every manager wants a good pre-season and time to give the players their ideas and the fitness, but the players are going to feel straight away that it's a different level. This is every day at the training ground; it's 100% - that's what he asks, what he demands. It will be a big difference for the players, and they're going to see results there straight away."

‌



The Belgian defender also recalled: "In the Champions League semi-final, we were 3-0 down [against Ajax] and he didn't have a tactical half-time talk. He just said, 'You're going to be physical, you're going to fight, you only need one goal to be back in the game, believe that everything is possible.'

"That was a big moment because we were nowhere near Ajax at that time, especially in that game. But we changed everything by intensity, by duels.

Article continues below

"I remember the long ball to [Fernando] Llorente and just fighting and asking, 'How badly do you want it?' It changed from that moment."

Sports.title: Erling Haaland hits back at Man City charges question – ‘Am I supposed to answer that?’
Sports.content:
Erling Haaland hits back at Man City charges question – ‘Am I supposed to answer that?’

Manchester City striker Erling Haaland was asked about the Premier League charges they are facing - and hit back at the interviewer while on international duty

View 2 Images Erling Haaland spoke candidly about the Premier League charges Manchester City face (Image: TV 2)

Erling Haaland maintains he is very happy at Manchester City despite the Premier League charges they are currently appealing. The goal machine was speaking after his latest finish and assist for Norway in their 3-1 victory at home against Wales in the Nations League.

‌



‌



During a live television interview after the match, Haaland was asked about the "situation" at City. The club have been found guilty of 114 charges related to serious violations of the league's financial regulations over a nine-season stretch.

‌



However, they are appealing against an independent commission's decision. City insist they are innocent of the allegations made against them.

‌



Speaking to the Norwegian television broadcaster TV2, Haaland said: "The investigation covered 2009 to 2018. In 2009, I played for Bryne U9s. In 2010, the U10s; in 2011, the U11s; 2012, the U12s; 2013, the U13s. Shall we continue? We don't need the whole list."

Man City appeal date set as new fears emerge over Premier League sanctions READ MORE :

He nonetheless continued: "2014, the U14s; 2015, the U15s and the national team, then the U16s, I think. In 2016, I moved up to Bryne's first team, second team and youth team. In 2017, I went to Molde. In 2018, I was with Molde: the first team, Molde 2 and a bit with the youth team.

"So this is a question I struggle to answer because it's a legal battle... It's a case between the Premier League and Manchester City that a panel will deal with. Am I supposed to answer that? I'm not really sure."

‌



View 2 Images Haaland gave a lengthy response after being asked about City's Premier League charges (Image: Mateusz Slodkowski, Getty Images)

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



Haaland then proceeded to reel off several of his fellow Norwegians who were at City during that era. He said: "There were quite a few Norwegians at the club during that period, I think. Abdisalam Ibrahim, Martin Samuelsen and Omar Elabdellaoui were there. Kjetil Haug was there too. I think there were a couple more, but I can't remember.

"But it's a difficult question to answer when I don't really know that much about it. I assume the answers will come... I don't know when. I haven't read much about it.

‌



"To be completely honest, I'm focused on trying to perform for Manchester City. A club I signed a five-year deal with in 2022 and a new nine-and-a-half-year deal in late 2024. I think that says everything about the matter. I'm a City player, and I'm incredibly happy there."

‌



When quizzed on whether the situation influences his thoughts on his long-term future at City, Haaland responded: "I understand that you want a little headline here, but as I said, I signed a long-term contract in 2024. I'd say I made a pretty good choice by joining City in 2022. We can all agree on that. I won't say it myself, but look at the trophies I've won and how I've developed on and off the pitch.

"I'm standing here after winning an international 3-1, and we're top of our group in Europe. Things aren't going so well for City in the league, but we'll try to turn that around against Fulham. But we can't focus on that now. Now we have to focus on Denmark."

Sports.title: Anthony Joshua makes honest admission about world title for Tyson Fury fight
Sports.content:
Anthony Joshua makes honest admission about world title for Tyson Fury fight

Anthony Joshua and Tyson Fury are expected to go head-to-head for the WBA 'super' heavyweight world title next month in Cardiff

View Image Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua face off (Image: Getty Images)

Anthony Joshua admits he is very 'confused' with what's on the line for his fight with Tyson Fury, but insists he only cares about 'beating up' the person in front of him.

‌



‌



Joshua and Fury will finally end their decade-long feud on December 11 at Cardiff's Principality Stadium. Following the official announcement, it seemed that there would be little at stake other than the chance to secure the bragging rights.

‌



That said, the world of boxing was left stunned after the WBA made the decision to put their 'super' heavyweight world title on the line for the all-British clash. Joshua's good friend Oleksandr Usyk vacated his titles earlier this year, and it seemed as if Murat Gassiev would be recognised as the champion.

‌



However, the Russian finds himself in an awkward situation having been downgraded to the 'regular' belt holder. Ahead of next month's dust-up, Joshua offered his verdict about the world title being up for grabs. "To be honest, it's a very odd situation because Usyk vacated the belt, then they said Gassiev, who at that time was like the regular champion, so to speak and I assumed he was going to be the only champion," he said on the Mr. Verzace Podcast.

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources

‌



Fabio Wardley makes final retirement decision after Daniel Dubois KO READ MORE :

Anthony Joshua reveals Oleksandr Usyk advice for Tyson Fury fight READ MORE :

"And then next thing I know there was an announcement that the WBA title for the Super Championship [was on the line], because I thought when they said WBA title, they were going to put the regular belt at stake, but they said, 'No, we're putting the Super belt at stake, Gassiev is still the regular champion'.

"I think [the regular belt] should have been [on the line]. I know that there's going to be a very special solid gold Ring Magazine belt that's staked in this fight to the winner, but to me, I haven't spoken to Gilberto from the WBA to understand why they made the decision for the belt to be on in this fight, because when they announced it, it got confusing and I said, 'Did Gassiev vacate the belt or what?' ell, let's say this to Murat Gassiev: we still respect you as champion.

‌



Eddie Hearn accepts Dana White fight offer on one condition READ MORE :

Eddie Hearn slams Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua fight card READ MORE :

"He's only done what he was supposed to do. And for me, I'm not fighting for no championship; I'm just fighting to be better than the man across the ring from me . If I'm honest with you, I don't care about no belt; I'm just fighting to beat up the person that's in front of me, and that's it."

If Joshua emerges victorious next month, he seems willing to chase more silverware. That is according to Eddie Hearn, who recently revealed his star client wants to avenge his defeat by Daniel Dubois. “I can’t speak on Tyson’s behalf, but for [Joshua], he still wants to be in the biggest fights of the sport,” said Hearn. “I’ve got to be honest with you, and I know it’s a very dangerous fight, but he wants to rematch Daniel Dubois. [Joshua] is a competitor, so he’s looking at that…and anyone who has ever beaten him, he’s rematched, apart from Daniel Dubois.

Article continues below

“He wants to have another go at Daniel Dubois, and this is second nature to him. He wants to try to avenge that defeat. It’s a dangerous fight, but if he goes through Tyson Fury and stops Tyson Fury, then why not? That would be for a title unification – or for a fight against [Filip] Hrgovic.”

Sports.title: Portugal suffer nightmare start to life without Cristiano Ronaldo in Denmark drubbing
Sports.content:
Portugal suffer nightmare start to life without Cristiano Ronaldo in Denmark drubbing

PORTUGAL 1-4 DENMARK: Jorge Jesus' Portugal did not enjoy the best of nights in their first outing since Cristiano Ronaldo's international retirement, losing heavily on home soil

View 2 Images Portugal suffered a heavy loss on home soil against Denmark (Image: Miguel Riopa/AFP)

The evening started with the unveiling of a permanent re-design for the No 7 icon as Portugal embraced a new dawn without their polarising record cap holder and goalscorer.

‌



‌



Seemingly revered and maligned in equal measure these days, it had been suggested that Portugal would be now better off without Cristiano Ronaldo, whose powers in an international shirt had waned significantly prior to an explosive early exit from last month's camp which turned out to be the catalyst to him calling time on representing his country.

‌



But life after the former Manchester United and Real Madrid attacker didn't get off to the ideal start as Jorge Jesus' side were thrashed 4-1 in their own backyard by Denmark.

‌



Goncalos Ramos once again led the line with a supporting cast of Joao Felix, Bruno Fernandes and Pedro Neto. Not exactly a shortage of star-power.

View 2 Images Portugal paid tribute to Cristiano Ronaldo before the game

‌



But it was the other end where the goals flowed with Pierre-Emile Hojberg's 43rd minute penalty well and truly opening the Portuguese floodgates.

Rasmus Hojlund, who missed out on playing with Ronaldo at Old Trafford by seven months, was then at the double netting four minutes after the break and then eight minutes after that. Joachim Anderson scored a fourth in the 75th minute to rub salt in Portuguese wounds.

‌



Bernardo Silva did find the back of the net in additional time but the damage had already been done on a desperately sobering night for the natives in Braga.

While defeat for Jesus' side means they will have to wait until the final matchday to discover if they will win their Group A4, Denmark would still need to win and hope Portugal lose in order to pip them to top spot.

Sports.title: Thomas Tuchel responds after Spain boss hits back over racism message to England stars
Sports.content:
Thomas Tuchel responds after Spain boss hits back over racism message to England stars

Luis de la Fuente sent a message directly to Thomas Tuchel after the England manager said he would remind his team of protocols ahead of a first game in Madrid since players were subjected to abuse in 2004

View 2 Images Thomas Tuchel hit back at Spanish reporters ahead of Sunday's game vs Spain

Thomas Tuchel has become involved in a war of words over a racism storm ahead of England’s Nations League clash with Spain.

‌



‌



Tuchel hit back over questions from Spanish journalists in Madrid when he was asked about comments he made after England’s win over Croatia. This will be the first time England have played in Madrid since 2004 - they actually refused to play in 2009 and the game was moved to Seville - after black players were abused in that fixture 22 years ago.

‌



The England boss was answering a question about whether he would remind his players about UEFA’s anti-racism protocols.

‌



Bit those comments did not please Spain boss Luis de la Fuente, who was asked at his press conference and snapped back: “Tell Tuchel there is no racism in Spain. It’s that blunt. Exactly the same as in England. We are not racist.”

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



But Tuchel then snapped back at Spanish journalists himself for effectively running to De La Fuente with his remarks when the England boss insists he was just answering a question.

Tuchel said: “I was polite enough to ask a question from your colleagues, and you run and ask Spain's coach and tell them that I talked about racism in Spain.

‌



"I never talked about racism in Spain. I answered politely a question. I never expect racism. The dressing room is the most anti-racism place in the world. This is a perfect example of how you create confusion out of nothing.”

View 2 Images Luis de la Fuente insisted "there is no racism" in Spain ahead of Sunday's game

‌



Tuchel's comments ahead of the game were that, although England "do not expect anything", he would talk to his players to remind them of the protocol in place ahead of the game.

He said: “I still think the protocol is in place and it's important that the players know about the protocol. And then yes, we will give our answers if stuff like this happens. The best answers are on the pitch. I think we had the same discussion before the Serbia game.”
