World.content:
NewsFeed Yemen’s Houthis unilaterally release 600 war detainees

Yemen’s Houthis have released 600 people imprisoned during the country’s civil war. The group says the move brings the total number freed through its unilateral amnesty initiatives to 2,612. The ICRC says the operation was separate from negotiated prisoner-exchange agreements.

World.title: Israel Kidnapped Iranian Generals in Hunt for Ron Arad
World.content:
Gen. Abdullah Saberi, an Iranian commander, stepped out for a jog early one morning in an upscale diplomatic quarter of Syria’s capital. Israeli intelligence officers waited nearby. Posing as movers, they had slipped past the neighborhood’s security checkpoints.

As he headed for a nearby park, General Saberi passed two men who carried an oversize refrigerator box. In a flash, the men restrained the general, drugged him, threw the box over his head, shoved him into a white van and left as if nothing had happened.

He was whisked to Israel for interrogation, according to numerous officials in the Middle East, including senior Iranian officials close to General Saberi and a Syrian official who reviewed video of the September 2021 kidnapping.

As a veteran of Iran’s powerful Islamic Revolutionary Guards Corps, General Saberi knew many secrets. But his interrogators were interested in only one.

World.title: In Banff, a Grizzly Bear Known as ‘the Boss’ Rules the National Park
World.content:
To the scientists and wardens of Banff National Park he is grizzly bear 122. But to everyone who lives in or near Canada’s oldest national park, and many of its 4.5 million annual visitors, he is the Boss.

He has been struck by a freight train without apparent ill effect. He has shrugged off being hit by cars. Scientists have confirmed that he killed and snacked on a black bear at least once, and he is believed to have fathered many, if not most, of the bears in his 2,000-square-kilometer territory.

Most of all, the Boss has become Canada’s 700-pound celebrity bear king. When he strolls along the Trans-Canada Highway looking for dandelions, “bear jams” swiftly follow. His battles with a rival bear known as Split Lip are legendary. (He caused the split lip.) His annual awakening from hibernation, usually in March, is reported by news outlets across Alberta.

World.title: Jordan Sentences 3 to Death Over Greek Orthodox Church Attack
World.content:
A military-run court in Jordan sentenced three men to death on Sunday after they were convicted in connection with an attack at a church last month that killed nine people, the Jordanian Armed Forces said in a statement.

The shooting at a Greek Orthodox church, which also wounded about three dozen people, was one of the deadliest militant attacks in the country in years, and King Abdullah II vowed that it would be met with “the harshest retaliation.”

The three men were sentenced after being convicted of violating antiterrorism laws, according to the Jordanian military. They were found guilty of carrying out deadly terrorist acts, possessing weapons and ammunition with the intent to commit terrorism, and promoting the ideas of a terrorist group.

That group was not named in the armed forces statement.

The sentences are subject to appeal, the military statement noted.

World.title: Iran Attacks Bahrain for the Second Time in Days
World.content:
A spokesman for Iran’s Foreign Ministry, Esmaeil Baghaei, said on Sunday that Iran would continue to respond to any military aggression by the United States or others.

Asked in a news conference in Tehran whether the Iranian attack in Bahrain signified a change to the country’s approach, and whether Iran was still awaiting an official American response in the negotiations, Mr. Baghaei said that Iran was “not waiting for anyone” and was focused on safeguarding its security.

Mr. Trump has zigzagged over whether or not he might order a return to full-blown war. The initial campaign failed to compel Iran to abandon its nuclear program but did ensnarl global energy markets, which contributed to a resounding defeat for the Republican Party in the recent midterm elections.

It is far from clear whether a new U.S. or Israeli attack on Iran could force Tehran to make new concessions. The country has said it has rebuilt its military capabilities during the truce, and U.S. and Israeli officials will also have to consider whether they are willing or able to contend with Iranian missile and drone attacks across the Middle East, given their depleted stores of aerial interceptors.

Mediators from Qatar and Pakistan have shuttled to Tehran in recent weeks in an effort to avert a return to all-out war. Iran’s foreign minister, Abbas Araghchi, will travel to Pakistan and Oman in the coming days, Mr. Baghaei said on Sunday.

World.title: Saudi-Backed Forces Retreat in Yemen, Leaving Key Strait in Houthi Control
World.content:
Forces backed by Saudi Arabia in Yemen said on Sunday that they were withdrawing from the country’s Red Sea coast, where they have been fighting for weeks to retake strategic territory from the Iran-aligned Houthi militia.

A group of fighters called the Southern Armed Forces, who are allied with the government of Yemen, said in a statement that they were “redeploying” to protect the interim capital, Aden, citing recent battlefield developments and “threats targeting” the city.

Aden has been the seat of the internationally recognized government for more than a decade, since the Houthis seized control of Sanaa, the Yemeni capital.

The retreat is a blow for the Yemeni government and Saudi Arabia as the balance of power in Yemen continues to tilt toward the Houthis, analysts said.

World.title: Is Italy the Model for Europe’s Future?
World.content:
In the time since, I have seen an Italianization of politics all around the continent, with coalitions of small parties resulting in instability, with fed-up voters desperate for new saviors. But more than anything, I have seen — in Britain, France, Germany — countries following the Italian model by allowing the far right into the political mainstream.

Spain, where I’m now The New York Times’s bureau chief, will hold elections this month. Polls show the far-right party Vox — which largely feeds on anti-Muslim, anti-migrant and anti-E.U. sentiment — is likely to join the mainstream conservative party in a new government. The current left-wing government led by Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez, a beacon for Europe’s liberals, is trying to mobilize supporters by warning against the regressive politics Vox represents. Some of his officials invoke the dictatorship of Francisco Franco.

But I keep thinking back to Mr. Berlusconi.

The Italian Laboratory

Soon before I arrived in Italy as a student in the late 1990s, Mr. Berlusconi, who many see as creating the mold for President Trump, first brought in “the fascists,” as he called the far right, to help govern with him. Berlusconi’s calculus was purely political. He needed the votes to form a winning coalition in 1994 and to gain power, not least to protect his vast business interests from prosecutors.

His decision broke a major postwar taboo. Mr. Berlusconi eventually claimed credit for upending the political establishment that had governed Italy since the end of World War II. Those mainstream politicians had made something of a backroom deal to keep the fascist forces descended from Mussolini, the dictator who had nearly destroyed the country, away from power. Mr. Berlusconi clearly understood he had violated that pact. “We let them into the government in ’94 and we legitimized them,” he said.

World.title: In Europe, an Emboldened Iran Contributes to a Sense of Anxiety
World.content:
Officials in Spain, Germany, France and Britain all declared they would not take part in America’s offensive attacks on Tehran, even as some host American military bases. Despite that, they appear to have become collateral damage as Iran seeks to show the consequences if Mr. Trump resumes aggressive actions.

“Iran is signaling very clearly to the Europeans that if the U.S. resumes the war, Europe is going to also become part of the target list for counter escalation,” said Ellie Geranmayeh, a Middle East and North Africa expert at the European Council on Foreign Relations. “It’s a sign of Iran’s desperation that they are trying to drag the Europeans into this global pain.”

Gen. Roly Walker, the chief of the general staff in Britain, told troops last month that “there is extreme jeopardy in the world at the moment,” adding that “very soon, the political leaders of this country will start to have a frank conversation with the citizens of this country, about just what is going on and where the risk lies.”

Of course Iran is not the only source of threats in Europe. Russia’s war of aggression in Ukraine has led to an increasing number of sabotage operations, including the jamming of aviation signals over Sweden, drones flying over Danish and Belgian airports and the smuggling of explosives into Poland in cans of corn. Western officials accuse Russia of trying to undermine European support for Ukraine.

Not all of the disruption has a clear origin. This past week, bomb threats were emailed to thousands of schools in Italy, forcing hundreds of them to be evacuated. That came after planes in Italy, Poland, Spain and elsewhere were grounded or diverted because of bomb threats that turned out to be hoaxes. Officials have not determined who was behind the threats.

World.title: A ‘Generational Clash’ Is Fueling Europe’s Protests
World.content:
Sébastien Ducros, a French data analyst who supports the widespread student protests in his country, has identified an obvious culprit for the lack of government funds for dilapidated schools.

“A huge portion of the money is going toward retirees, while many other things are being neglected,” said Mr. Ducros, 36. “I honestly think — even if it feels strange to say — that people like my parents are in a position where they should and could” surrender some of their pension payments, he added, saying that they were about to retire.

But Laurent Grinwald, 72, who retired recently after decades as a postal worker, isn’t eager for his pension to be reduced, particularly to pay for other state-funded services. Especially, he said, as rents and the cost of living have shot up.

“We’ve been working all this time,” Mr. Grinwald said, “and now, suddenly, the stance is, ‘Well, no, we’re going to start taking a bit more?’”

World.title: Zelensky urges US and Musk to lift Starlink restrictions and be on 'right side of history'
World.content:
Ukraine uses the normal Starlink service for communications on the battlefield, while Starshield is used for the interception of missiles and drones in Ukraine airspace.

The issue of speed restrictions was first identified in October. It led to conflicting accounts by both Elon Musk and US President Donald Trump.

Musk said the US government was responsible as Starshield was controlled by them, but Trump denied being responsible and said he had told the billionaire owner to "put it back".

It appeared to be returning to normal after a week, following which Ukraine said the restrictions were still being implemented.

The connection issues coincided with a tense diplomatic stand-off between Zelensky and Trump over Ukrainian strikes on oil infrastructure within Russia.

Trump said the strikes on Russian oil refineries, which Kyiv says are crucial to stemming the main revenue source for Moscow's war effort, had pushed global prices higher.

On Sunday Zelensky said Ukraine was struggling to intercept Russian jet-powered drones targeting electricity substations because "restrictions on the operating speed of Starshield terminals along the front line and in the temporarily occupied territories are still there".

"Our interceptor drones lose connection with their operators at a speed of 161km/h (100mph) and simply cannot catch up with Russian jet-powered 'shaheds'," he posted, referring to the drones that follow an Iranian design.

On Friday Zelensky said speed limits of around 100mph had been enforced on the network since Monday, but only in Russian-occupied areas and not the whole of Ukraine.

"It already has political implications. If you impose restrictions there, you are already partially recognising the temporary occupied territories as not ours," the New York Times reported him as saying.

World.title: Suspected China spy linked to Nvidia's ex-boss left in 2025, Megaspeed says
World.content:
Alice Huang, a suspected China spy who has been linked to Nvidia's former boss Jensen Huang, left her executive role at Megaspeed in August last year, the company says.

Jensen Huang resigned as chief executive of the AI chip-making giant Nvidia after it emerged he had allegedly had affairs with Alice Huang as well as with one of his employees.

Megaspeed is the biggest buyer of Nvidia chips in South East Asia and the scandal at Nvidia has raised questions about the possibility that high-end AI chips may have ended up in China despite US export restrictions.

The Singapore-based company said on Sunday it had launched an internal investigation into its business.

Megaspeed said it was aware of reports "containing assertions about our business, supply chain and global operations that are not supported by verifiable evidence".

It added that it "conducts legitimate and lawful business" and has "retained external legal counsel to conduct a thorough internal investigation".

Also on Sunday, US Congressman John Moolenaar said that Jensen Huang has agreed to testify before the Select Committee on China, which he chairs, as well as the House Foreign Affairs and the House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence.

The committee heads had threatened to issue subpoenas to Huang if he did not comply with their requests to testify.

Moolenaar told CBS, BBC's US partner, that none were ultimately issued. Huang's testimony is expected to take place behind close doors, with the dates still being finalised.

"That's going to be a very important meeting to understand to what degree privileged information was accessed, and to what degree this potential alleged Chinese spy influenced Nvidia's philosophy and may have had an influence on some of our policies with respect to AI and export controls," the congressman told the Face The Nation programme.

Separately, a group of tech leaders, including Space X's Elon Musk, have been trying to rally support to have Huang reinstated as Nvidia CEO.

A representative for Huang declined to comment on a report in the Financial Times Sunday suggesting that he was discussing a comeback to the firm he co-founded.

On Friday, US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent blamed fellow Trump cabinet colleague Howard Lutnick's commerce department for failing to properly oversee the export of high-end chips.

Bessent told CNBC that several agencies "were in favour of putting Megaspeed on the entity list for months... but Commerce has the pen... and you will have to ask them about their internal process".

The so-called entity list restricts US trade with overseas firms and individuals.

Lutnick has been called to testify before the Senate Banking Committee next month over his department's role in allowing Nvidia to export its advanced chips.

Other congressional committees have asked both Lutnick and his department to retain all records relating to Nvidia and Jensen Huang.

Megaspeed is suspected of giving backdoor access to Nvidia chips to Chinese companies via its data centres in Malaysia, Indonesia and Thailand.

World.title: Mexican drug lord Miguel Angel Felix Gallardo dies age 80
World.content:
Notorious Mexican drug lord Miguel Ãngel FÃ©lix Gallardo has died in hospital aged 80.

FÃ©lix Gallardo was widely considered one of the biggest drug smugglers in history and is credited with building an alliance between criminal groups in Colombia and his own Mexican cartel.

Known as The Godfather or the 'Boss of Bosses', FÃ©lix Gallardo was the head of the all-powerful Guadalajara Cartel, which reigned over Mexican drug trafficking at the height of the cocaine boom of the 1980s.

At the time, it created a new modus operandi in the illegal drug trade which endures to this day. He had been in state custody since 1989.

The name Miguel Ãngel FÃ©lix Gallardo will echo through the annals of drug-trafficking history more than any other except perhaps Pablo Escobar's.

He led the organisation which revolutionised drug smuggling in the region by entering into partnership with the Colombian cartels, particularly Escobar's MedellÃ­n Cartel, to combine production in the Andes with Mexican transportation across the border into the United States.

At one point an estimated 80% of all cocaine that entered the US came from the MedellÃ­n Cartel. FÃ©lix Gallardo and his organisation played a major role in smuggling it in.

At its height, the Guadalajara Cartel under FÃ©lix Gallardo influenced Mexican politics and law enforcement, controlling entire police networks and state governorships.

In 1985, the net started to tighten around the leaders of the cartel following the torture and murder of a DEA agent, Enrique 'Kiki' Camarena.

Camarena had angered them after he had discovered and then destroyed a vast marijuana plantation in Chihuahua, which belonged to the criminal group.

His death sparked one of the biggest manhunts the US government has ever launched in North America.

In 1989, FÃ©lix Gallardo was captured and sentenced to decades in prison. In ill health, he was placed under house arrest since 2022 and died in hospital in his native Guadalajara.

In the 1980s, Joaquin 'El Chapo' GuzmÃ¡n was introduced to FÃ©lix Gallardo, who put him in charge of handling logistics for his drug organisation.

From the subsequent break-up of FÃ©lix Gallardo's organisation after his arrest, the Sinaloa Cartel emerged, led by GuzmÃ¡n, now another man synonymous with large-scale drug trafficking.

In 2019, GuzmÃ¡n was sentenced to life in prison for charges including drug trafficking and money laundering following one of the most high-profile trials in recent US history.

World.title: South Korea's top scorer in tax accountancy exam admits cheating
World.content:
A candidate who came first in South Korea's certified tax accountancy exam has admitted cheating by using a miniature camera, mobile phone and AI tools.

Han Won-seok confessed in a video on the YouTube account of his lawyer, Lee Don-Ho, adding that he had confessed to the Seoul Metropolitan Police Agency and offered details on how he cheated.

The 34-year-old scored 397.5 out of 400 points in the first round, getting just one of 160 questions wrong, which initially raised suspicions and sparked online speculation.

Standardised national tests play an outsized role in career trajectories for South Koreans, making their results - and efforts to unduly inflate those results - of great importance.

"I cheated in both the first and second rounds of the tax account exam by using electronic devices and generative AI," Han said in the video published on Sunday.

"I used a microcamera to photograph the test questions and sent them to an AI then checked my answers on my smartphone to commit the cheating."

When accusations he had cheated first began to surface, Han had denied any wrongdoing - but said he had changed his mind after thinking about the feelings of the candidate who had come second in the exam.

He went on to apologise to the other entrants who had passed the tests fairly.

"It seems that because of me, other successful candidates are being suspected," he suggested.

The Ministry of Employment and Labour and the Human Resources Development Service held an emergency meeting after Han admitted cheating.

The South Korean president's policy chief Ha Jun-kyung said new measures would be introduced to prevent cheating and warned "past crimes" would be "tracked down and apprehended to the very end".

Those found to have used AI to cheat in the tax accountancy exam will have their qualification revoked and will be banned from retaking the test for five years, the government said.

The scandal comes just days before the east Asian nation's annual college entrance exam, a crucial hurdle for students.

World.title: Pope Leo rides in helicopter cockpit during Peru trip
World.content:
Pope Leo XIV shared a cockpit with pilots from the Peruvian Air Force during his tour of Latin America.

Sharing the video to social media, the force said having the Pope join its pilots on Saturday was "an honour and an unforgettable memory".

On Sunday, the pontiff arrived in Cusco, a southern Andes Mountains city that was once the heart of the Inca empire.

There, the Pope visited an ancient Inca fortress, where he said religious traditions could help counter an age marked by "divisions, wounds, mistrust," stressing that faith should unite people and bring them together "in the light of faith and love."

The Peruvian leg of his tour holds special significance for the Pope.

He not only lived in Peru for long periods between 1985 and 2023 but also became a citizen of the country in 2015, forging close ties with local communities.

Read more on the significance of the Pope's visit to Peru

World.title: Steering failure preceded New Orleans cruise ship collision, says NTSB
World.content:
The tanker was upbound on the Mississippi River as it moved toward the east bank of the river just before the collision, said the NTSB, based on findings from the vessel's voyage data recorder.

Minutes before the crash, investigators said audio consistent with the ship's warning system was broadcast, along with commands to deploy the vessel's anchors and emergency ship handling orders.

"We are aware that there was an issue with the steering on board and causing the rudder to remain at a starboard position, causing the heading of the vessel to veer towards the east bank," investigator-in-charge Bart Barnum said during the news conference.

The exact issue with the steering has yet to be determined, he added.

A preliminary report from the NTSB is expected in 30 days.

Calls about the collision began around 13:30 EST (18:30 GMT) on Friday, when people began trying to help passengers escape the boat as it took on water, Port of New Orleans chief Melanie Montroll said after the incident.

There were about 129 passengers, in addition to crew members, on the American Heritage at the time of the collision, according to the port authority.

Passengers began getting off the paddlewheeler vessel, operated by American Cruise Lines, as it started listing before tipping onto its side.

Tugboat operators, police and other rescuers rushed to help while officials shut down traffic in the Mississippi River during the rescue effort.

The American Heritage had been finishing an eight-day cruise calling at destinations in Louisiana and Mississippi along the waterway.

World.title: Czechs rally against plan to switch funding of public media
World.content:
Thousands of people have gathered in central Prague to protest against the Czech government's plans to scrap the licence fee and use the state budget to fund public media.

Critics say the plans would allow politicians to stifle media freedom.

The coalition government - which consists of the populist ANO party and two right-wing Eurosceptic parties - insists the change will not affect editorial independence, but wants broadcasters to cut costs.

Parliament passed the first draft of the proposal late last month. Since then, thousands of Czechs have taken part in protests.

Czech households currently pay â 205 crowns ($9.44; Â£7.06) a month for public TV and radio.

Sunday's protest was organised by the Million Moments for Democracy association which said "roughly 400,000" people had attended.

"I know that our entire Czech Television is a guarantee of truth and objectivity," pensioner Milana Rudolfova, 72, told Reuters news agency.

"If we do not have public television and radio then unfortunately we will not be able to believe anything anymore."

World.title: Police ban protests near 10 schools and five universities in Paris
World.content:
Police in Paris have issued a five-day ban on protests near 10 secondary schools and five universities as authorities try to control weeks of blockades and violence at educational venues in France.

The order prohibits unauthorised gatherings or marches within 100m of the sites from 16 to 20 November.

Paris police chief Patrice Faure said the ban was necessary due to "numerous disruptions and blockades around certain secondary schools and establishments of higher learning" and "persistent violence".

A wave of protests began in France September over poor secondary school conditions, before spreading to universities, workers and a "yellow-vest" movement against the cost of living.

Announcing the order, the Paris police chief said blockades around certain secondary schools and universities have led to damaged public property, violence against members of the educational community and clashes with law enforcement.

Mayors of eight Parisian districts had contacted the regional education authority to call for measures to "secure the entrances and exits" of blockaded secondary schools, local media report.

Some 1,548 people have been arrested in Paris since the start of the protests, Faure said on Sunday.

World.title: Tanzania vs Nigeria: Super Eagles arrive in Zanzibar for crucial clash
World.content:
Nigeria’s Super Eagles have arrived in Zanzibar ahead of Tuesday’s crucial 2027 Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) qualifying encounter against Tanzania.

The Nigerian delegation included 23 players, coaches, backroom staff, representatives of the National Sports Commission (NSC) and Nigeria Football Federation (NFF), selected journalists and members of the supporters club.

The team travelled to the East African island on Sunday, two days after securing a 3-1 victory over Tanzania in the first leg at the Godswill Akpabio International Stadium in Uyo, Akwa Ibom State.

A second-half brace from substitute Tolu Arokodare helped the Super Eagles claim all three points after Alhassan Yusuf had given Nigeria an early lead in the encounter played on Friday.

Yusuf opened the scoring in the second minute, but Tanzania drew level through Alphonce Msanga in the 32nd minute.

Arokodare, introduced at the start of the second half, restored Nigeria’s advantage in the 52nd minute before completing his brace eight minutes later to secure the victory.

The Super Eagles will now seek another win when both teams meet at the Amaan Stadium in Zanzibar on Tuesday.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The return fixture is particularly important for Nigeria, who are chasing the only available qualification ticket from Group L, with Tanzania already assured of a place at the tournament as co-hosts alongside Kenya and Uganda.

Nigeria currently have six points from three matches and occupy second position in the group, one point behind leaders Guinea-Bissau, who have seven points.

The Super Eagles began their campaign with a 2-1 victory over Madagascar in Uyo before suffering a disappointing 3-0 defeat away to Guinea-Bissau.

The victory over Tanzania restored some confidence in Eric Chelle’s team, but another positive result on Tuesday would be important to their qualification ambitions.

Nigeria will, however, be without Ademola Lookman, who has been ruled out of the return fixture after sustaining a knee ligament sprain during Friday’s encounter.

The forward was instrumental in Nigeria’s opening goal in Uyo before being substituted in the first half.

With Guinea-Bissau also competing for the group’s remaining qualification place, the Super Eagles cannot afford another slip-up as the race for the 2027 AFCON ticket intensifies.

World.title: NAF to hold memorial for victims of October 5 aircraft crash
World.content:
The Nigerian Air Force (NAF) has announced plans to hold a memorial service and wreath-laying ceremony for victims of its NAF 931 aircraft crash in Igbokoda, Ondo State, on 26 November,

The ceremony, scheduled to take place at the National Military Cemetery in Abuja, will honour those who lost their lives in the 5 October accident, as the air force continues investigations into the circumstances surrounding the crash.

In a statement on Sunday, the NAF spokesperson, Ehimen Ejodame, said the ceremony would bring together bereaved families, colleagues, friends and members of the military community to pay their last respects to the deceased and recognise their service and sacrifice.

PREMIUM TIMES reported that NAF announced it had recovered the aircraft’s Cockpit Voice Recorder (CVR), alongside other wreckage and relevant evidence from the crash site.

Mr Ejodame reiterated these recoveries, saying data retrieved from the recorder was being analysed and would contribute significantly to the ongoing investigation.

He added that recovery operations had yielded several human remains and aircraft fragments, while the identification of the recovered remains was still ongoing.

The air force spokesperson attributed the difficulties encountered during the exercise to the swampy nature of the terrain and the depth to which some of the wreckage had penetrated the ground.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

He said the investigation was progressing in collaboration with the Nigerian Safety Investigation Bureau (NSIB) and the Nigerian Civil Aviation Authority (NCAA).

Mr Ejodame noted that NAF was engaging relevant agencies to address environmental concerns arising from the recovery exercise and ensure appropriate remediation after the operation.

This newspaper reported that the traditional ruler of Igbokoda raised an alarm over water and air pollution following the crash, warning that the community faces a public health and economic crisis.

Background

The accident occurred when the ATR-42 aircraft, designated NAF 931, crashed in a swampy area near the Naval Base in Igbokoda, Ilaje Local Government Area of Ondo State, while travelling from Benin City to Lagos on a routine mission.

Air traffic controllers reportedly lost contact with the aircraft at about 9:13 am, after which the wreckage was located near the Naval Base. All 25 people aboard, comprising five crew members and 20 passengers, died in the accident, according to the air force.

PREMIUM TIMES reported that the casualty figure was initially disputed after Aviation Minister Festus Keyamo announced that 32 people, comprising 25 passengers and seven crew members, were aboard.

However, the NAF subsequently clarified that 25 people were on the aircraft, explaining that the discrepancy resulted from differences in the interpretation of aviation terminology.

It said the final figure comprised five active crew members and 20 passengers, including two military officials classified as non-active crew members but travelling as passengers.

Following the crash, the Chief of the Air Staff, Sunday Aneke, ordered a comprehensive investigation and search-and-rescue operations. The NAF confirmed that no survivors were found and subsequently released the names of all 25 victims. Mr Aneke, an air marshal, also expressed condolences to their families and assured them of the Service’s support.

On 13 October, the air force announced the constitution of a 12-member specialist aircraft accident investigation board to establish the circumstances and causes of the crash and recommend measures to prevent a recurrence.

World.title: How Tinubu’s reforms averted Nigeria’s economic collapse – Gov Mbah
World.content:
Governor of Enugu State, Peter Mbah, says Nigeria would have suffered total economic collapse but for President Bola Tinubu’s courageous reforms, arguing that the removal of fuel subsidy and floating of the naira only waited until the President’s assumption of office in 2023 because the nation delayed the ‘evil day’ and lived on borrowed time.

He gave the insights at the weekend during the launch of “As Tinubu Mbah Moves” (ATM), a support group convened by the Minister of Innovation, Science and Technology, Dr. Kingsley Udeh (SAN), and dedicated to the re-election of President Tinubu and Governor Mbah in Enugu.

Speaking to the mammoth crowd, he said, “It would have been a lot easier for any leader to just continue with the status quo and carry on on the basis of business as usual. But for Bola Ahmed Tinubu, it was business unusual that led to the bold initiatives.

“As a person who had played very actively in the oil and gas sector, I had written quite a lot of features and articles arguing against the fuel subsidy regime long before now, for it was clear to me, even from the point of a major player in that sector, that the subsidy regime was not sustainable because of the economic devastation it was causing to us as Nigerians. We were just basically postponing the evil day.

“We were just digging our poverty pits continually. We were actually digging deeper into that pit of poverty. And it would have taken a very courageous leader in his first term to say, ‘Look, if we have to build for the future, if we have to think about our children, then we must take out the subsidy and we must also unify the exchange rate regime.’”

Mbah took a swipe at the foreign exchange regime before the floating of the naira by Tinubu, describing it as a cesspool of corruption.

“We got to a point in this country where even salary earners, once they get paid, would run to the bureau de change to change it rather than hold their salary in naira. Confidence was completely eroded in the naira. Nobody wanted to touch it with the tip of their finger. And that was the recipe for a failed nation.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“If you wanted to do a study or research of any failed nation, it is when the country, the citizens themselves, begin to lose confidence in their currency. And that was the environment that this President inherited.

“It was a major cesspool of corruption. The arbitrage was obvious and people were being taken advantage of. What was happening between the official and the parallel market was terrible. And some people were benefiting from that arbitrage at the expense of the economy. But it took this President’s understanding of the economy to be able to make those bold decisions,” he explained.

Continuing, he said that the stabilisation of the nation’s macroeconomic indicators by the Tinubu administration had encouraged Foreign Direct Investments (FDIs) necessary for improving Nigeria’s microeconomic indices, such as household incomes and employment.

“This essentially is something that is largely driven by private capital. But government enables it by policies because I can tell you that private capital does not go to where you do not have stability.

“If your macro indicators are under pressure; if you have not addressed your foreign reserve, your foreign exchange regime, your inflationary rates, and all that, you do not have any chance of attracting private capital because private capital is blind. It is not emotional. It goes to where it makes return on investment, where it can be guaranteed some high level of security.

“Because we did not have all those before now, private capital was not coming. So, what the bold policies and initiatives this President took have done is that those macro pressures have largely been eased. And what you are now witnessing in our economy is a growth trajectory.

“So, private capital is now looking towards our country. You can see quite a number of FDI deals being closed – not MoA (Memorandum of Agreement) or MoU (Memorandum of Understanding). These are final investment decisions being made across different sectors, particularly in the oil and gas sector. You can see billions of dollars coming towards this direction today.

“People who have dollars are now going back to exchange their dollars because that confidence has been restored.

“So, now that we have stabilised our macro indicators, we have now started witnessing growth, albeit not to the level we aspire.

“The next thing is going to be shared prosperity because you are going to see that growth cascade. You are going to see it get to the households. You are going to see it create employment. So, our unemployed youths would be gainfully employed. That is the way it works,” he explained.

Citing Enugu State as an example, Mbah also credited the President with freeing funds that could have been sunk into subsidy, thus arming states with resources to embark on massive development projects that impact the lives of the people.

The Governor, therefore, urged Nigerians to vote en masse for the President to complete the job he started, saying it was the only realistic option.

“Nations are not built by abandoning challenges halfway through. If we have gone through this whole process of difficult periods when it appeared as if all was doomed to a point where we are beginning to see the light at the end of the tunnel, we cannot abandon what has been started. No great sailor abandons his ship because of a rough sea, mid-sea. You have to sail to get to your destination,” he said.

He urged ATM members to take the message of the successes of Tinubu’s reforms and the President’s various infrastructural and policy interventions in the South East to the electorate.

Meanwhile, Dr Udeh (SAN) said the support group would focus its mobilisation efforts on non-members of the All Progressives Congress (APC) across the 4,145 polling units of Enugu State ahead of the 2027 general elections, deploying technology to register members, track their participation and monitor its mobilisation activities through an online registration portal.

World.title: Tinubu prepares five-year plan to end Boko Haram insurgency, tackle insecurity
World.content:
President Bola Tinubu’s five-year plan to end the 17-year Boko Haram insurgency and tackle other security threats across Nigeria is ready, the All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential Campaign Council has said.

PREMIUM TIMES reports that Nigeria’s multidimensional security threats have triggered Mr Tinubu’s security reforms, including a recruitment drive, expansion of commands, plans for the creation of state police and investment in military hardware and infrastructure.

Boko Haram insurgency has entered its 17th year, spreading from the North-east to the North-central and South-west, where Boko Haram kidnapped schoolchildren in two separate attacks, as documented here and here.

The military has attributed Boko Haram’s expansion to its sustained offensive against terrorists, vowing to maintain the pressure. However, terrorist groups continue to exploit security vacuums and local grievances in poorly governed areas, consolidating their presence, winning over sections of local communities while continuing to kill and abduct their targets.

The five-year plan

The plan is designed to strengthen the country’s security architecture, improve military effectiveness and provide a coordinated response to terrorism, banditry, kidnapping and other forms of criminality.

Dele Alake, spokesperson for the APC Presidential Campaign Council, disclosed this in a statement on Sunday, saying the framework would align defence priorities, operational requirements, military capability development and expenditure with Nigeria’s current and anticipated security challenges.

Mr Alake, who doubles as the Minister of Solid Minerals, stated that the Tinubu administration has recorded the elimination of more than 15,000 Boko Haram insurgents and bandits in the last three years, while over 130,000 Boko Haram fighters and their dependents have surrendered through Operation Safe Corridor, a controversial federal government rehabilitation programme for repentant insurgents.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

National Security Adviser (NSA) Nuhu Ribadu had shared similar figures at an APC summit.

Mr Alake said the recent figures reflected the administration’s “two-phase” approach to insecurity, combining sustained military operations with non-kinetic interventions.

As part of efforts to expand the military’s operational capacity, Mr Tinubu has created four new Nigerian Army divisions and restructured existing military formations to improve operational coverage and enable troops to respond more swiftly to security threats.

The president has also approved the establishment of two additional army depots in Osogbo, Osun State, and Amasiri-Edda, Ebonyi State, to expand recruitment and training capacity.

The two facilities are designed to accommodate 6,000 recruits each, bringing their combined training capacity to 12,000 soldiers at a time.

The Osogbo facility currently has 5,210 recruits undergoing training, said Mr Alake.

The administration has also approved the recruitment of an additional 28,000 soldiers and 50,000 police officers to strengthen military manpower, internal security and the country’s response to criminal activities.

On military infrastructure and personnel welfare, Mr Alake highlighted a 700-unit military barracks project in Ikere-Ekiti, Ekiti State, which is intended to provide accommodation and operational support for military personnel in the area.

He said the five-year defence plan would also prioritise intelligence, surveillance and coordination, with government investments guided by identified security threats, operational requirements and national priorities.

He added that the framework was expected to improve combat readiness, address critical capability gaps, optimise available resources and minimise unnecessary expenditure and wastage.

However, Mr Alake did not provide a specific implementation date for the plan, its projected cost or details of its funding arrangements.

World.title: 2027: Jigawa ADC backs Atiku, passes vote of confidence in state leadership
World.content:
Candidates of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) in Jigawa State have declared their support for former Vice President Atiku Abubakar and his running mate, Rotimi Amaechi, for the 2027 presidential election.

They announced the commitment in Dutse on Sunday at a meeting of the party’s flagbearers in the state.

The gathering was led by the governorship candidate and state party leader, Sabo Nakudu—who recently received his Certificate of Return after clinching the party’s governorship ticket—and brought together 45 legislative candidates across the state.

The candidates pledged their loyalty to the ADC and vowed to work toward the electoral victory of their presidential candidate and other candidates contesting across Jigawa’s constituencies.

The flagbearers also passed a vote of confidence in both the current and legacy leadership of the party at the state and local government levels, led by Sani Gumel.

“We call on all party members, stakeholders, and supporters to remain united and work diligently for the victory of the ADC in Jigawa State,” the party leadership stated at the event as political activities intensify ahead of the 2027 polls.

The candidates committed to conducting peaceful, issue-based campaigns throughout the electoral cycle.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The party’s chairperson, Mr Gumel, commended the governorship candidate, Mr Nakudu, for his leadership and urged all flagbearers to remain focused and disciplined in their grassroots mobilisation.

Certificate of return

The meeting in Dutse followed Mr Nakudu’s formal receipt of his certificate of return following his victory in the party’s primary election held in May.

“I have received the certificate of return as the ADC governorship candidate for Jigawa State, following the primary election conducted in recent months.

“The ceremony took place at the national headquarters of the party located in the Federal Capital Territory, Abuja”, Mr Nakudu stated

The event showed Mr Nakudu displaying the certificate alongside the Jigawa State ADC chairperson, Mr Gumel and other state party chieftains.

The presentation of the certificate of return follows months of internal friction that fractured the Jigawa State chapter of the ADC following the May 2026 gubernatorial primary.

In the 28 May primary, Mr Nakudu defeated former federal lawmaker, Bashir Adamu.

Mr Adamu rejected the primary results, petitioned the party’s appeal committee, and accused Mr Nakudu’s camp of hijacking the party machinery.

World.title: 2027: Like Lagos, NDC campaign attacked in Kano
World.content:
Barely days after a town hall meeting of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) was attacked in Lagos State, a similar incident occurred in Kano State on Sunday, involving the party’s vice-presidential candidate, Rabiu Kwankwaso, and his campaign team in the Bichi Local Government Area.

In the incident, thugs attacked the convoy of Mr Kwankwaso and the party’s governorship candidate in the state, Aminu Abdussalam.

The spokesperson for the NDC governorship candidate, Ibrahim Shu’aibu, said the campaign team had earlier campaigned in Tofa, Rimingado, Kabo, Gwarzo, Shanono, and Bagwai local government areas without disruption.

Mr Shu’aibu said the team initially received reports that the road leading to Bichi had been barricaded by thugs.

Upon arriving in the town, he said the convoy was attacked by stone-throwing thugs before advancing past the local government secretariat, where more armed youths emerged and continued the attack.

Mr Shu’aibu alleged that several members of the campaign team sustained injuries and multiple vehicles in the entourage were vandalised, adding that he personally counted about seven smashed vehicles during the melee.

The Kano State Police Command could not be immediately reached for its reaction to the incident.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The Kano incident occurred just three days after hoodlums wielding cutlasses and cudgels stormed an NDC town hall meeting along Kudirat Abiola Way in Oregun, Ikeja.

The event was scheduled to be addressed by the party’s presidential candidate, Peter Obi, and his running mate, Mr Kwankwaso, though neither had arrived at the venue when the violence broke out.

The NDC accused supporters of the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) in Lagos of orchestrating the attack.

However, the APC Presidential Campaign Council, through its spokesperson Dele Alake, denied involvement, condemned the violence, and urged security agencies to apprehend the perpetrators.

Civil society groups, including the Socio-Economic Rights and Accountability Project (SERAP), also called on President Bola Tinubu and the Inspector-General of Police, Olatunji Disu, to launch an impartial investigation into such attacks.

World.title: COP31: Africa’s climate action network PACJA unveils plan to train 500 youths on climate justice
World.content:
The Pan African Climate Justice Alliance (PACJA), a coalition of over 2000 organisations dedicated to promoting climate action as an advocacy tool in 54 African countries, has launched the sixth cohort of its Nairobi Summer School on Climate Justice, aiming to train 500 youths.

The trainees, to be drawn from within and outside the continent, will attend a capacity development workshop in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, from 20 June to 3 July 2027, the group stated on Friday at the 31st meeting of the Conference of the Parties (COP31) to the UN Framework Convention on Climate Change.

Participants will learn how climate negotiations work and acquire insight into climate finance, adaptation, loss and damage, just transition and accountability. They will also take part in mock negotiations and meet negotiators and policymakers.

PACJA advances climate action through capacity building, policy advocacy, research, and support for local climate resilience and land restoration projects.

Mithika Mwenda, executive director of PACJA, said Africa’s young people hold less than five per cent of the positions where climate decisions are made, even though they constitute as much as 60 per cent of the continent’s population.

He said the school was set up in 2020 to close that gap. The five previous cohorts trained more than 2500 young people from 144 countries.

The programme will now be held every two years in line with the organisation’s strategic plan for 2026 to 2030.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“Young Africans should not only be invited to the table. They should arrive prepared,” said Augustine Njamnshi, chair of PACJA’s political and technical affairs, who unveiled the cohort.

Mr Njamnshi acknowledged the support given by the African Development Bank, the UN Economic Commission for Africa, the Swedish Development Agency, the East African Legislative Assembly and the HBCU Green Fund to the school.

Alumni’s testimonials

Mr Njamnshi said the school’s alumni include young negotiators, policy analysts, people working on the green economy and in academia.

Smriti Shah of the fourth cohort told PREMIUM TIMES she once believed climate justice was “highly political”, but PACJA has changed her perspective.

“PACJA taught me to carry the views of communities to policymakers, and now I include climate justice in every humanitarian programme I work on,” she said.

Shampi Anna, also from the same cohort, said alumni are helping young members of parliament in Kenya with bills, lobbying and advocacy.

“We worked, and we continue to work with young parliamentarians in Kenya,” Ms Anna said.

A Nigerian and member of the fifth batch, Anuoluwapo Otubusin, told FEMNET, an organisation promoting women’s development in Africa, that she had a remarkable experience that was more than just attending a climate action training.

“It was a turning point in how I currently view advocacy, policy influencing, solidarity and my role in shaping a feminist climate future,” she said.

Prospective applicants for the latest cohort must be 18 to 35 years old and hold at least a high school certificate.

PACJA said it will prioritise applicants from places most prone to climate change in Africa and the Global South, especially young people from indigenous communities, grassroots movements, women’s groups, universities and policy institutions.

World.title: State Police: Four states yet to transmit resolutions to NASS – Senate Leader
World.content:
The Senate Leader, Opeyemi Bamidele, said four of Nigeria’s 36 state Houses of Assembly have yet to transmit their resolutions on the proposed creation of state police to the National Assembly.

Mr Bamidele, who represents Ekiti Central Senatorial District, said although the National Assembly was still awaiting the resolutions from the four states, their failure to transmit them would not prevent federal lawmakers from proceeding with the process and forwarding the bill to the president for assent.

He stated this on Friday at an award ceremony organised by The Sun Publishing Limited, publisher of The Sun newspaper, in Abuja, according to a statement by his media office on Sunday.

Mr Bamidele was honoured with the newspaper’s Senator of the Year award.

On 4 November, during plenary, the Senate fixed 15 November as the deadline for state Houses of Assembly to transmit their resolutions on the proposed creation of state police to the National Assembly.

At the time, six states were yet to transmit their resolutions. They were Kano, Oyo, Cross River, Abia, Niger and Benue.

However, while speaking on the development, the Senate Leader did not identify the two state assemblies that had transmitted their resolutions since the deadline was announced or those that were yet to comply.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“We are now expecting four State Houses of Assembly to turn in their reports on or before the National Assembly reconvenes on November 17, 2026. This suggests that next week will be decisive and defining for the National Assembly. Whether the remaining states turn in their reports or not, we must move forward and fulfil the aspiration of our people,” he said.

Mr Bamidele said the National Assembly was under an obligation to transmit the bill to the presidency for assent in the interest of national peace, progress and stability.

“We are now under obligation to transmit the State Police (Constitution Alteration) Bill, 2026 to the President and Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces, His Excellency Bola Ahmed Tinubu, GCFR, for assent. This is a responsibility we must consciously discharge on behalf of our constituents and in the interest of national peace, progress, and stability,” he said.

The Senate leader said the proposed state police system was not meant to create ethnic or state armies but to establish state-led, community-anchored policing within clear constitutional safeguards.

Mr Bamidele’s remarks indicated that the proposal had met the constitutional requirement of approval by at least two-thirds of the 36 state assemblies, equivalent to 24 states.

The National Assembly can now proceed with the remaining stages of the constitutional amendment process, including harmonising the versions passed by both chambers before transmitting the bill to the president for assent.

The proposal was transmitted to the state assemblies in September for consideration as part of the ongoing amendment of the 1999 Constitution.

It seeks to establish state police services that would operate alongside the existing federal police system.

Under the proposed framework, state governors would appoint police commissioners, subject to confirmation by their respective Houses of Assembly. Governors would also be empowered to issue directives to state police on matters relating to insecurity.

While the federal police would continue to be headed by the Inspector-General of Police, each state police service would be headed by a commissioner appointed by the governor and confirmed by the state assembly.

The proposal, however, prohibits converting existing local security outfits into state police services or allowing them to exercise police powers under the new framework. It also bars them from bearing firearms.

Such outfits include Amotekun in the South-west, Ebube Agu in the South-east and Hisbah in parts of northern Nigeria.

Regulating social media

Mr Bamidele also expressed concern about the unregulated social media space, arguing that the platform needed regulation consistent with press freedom.

He said he had personally experienced the consequences of unregulated social media and questioned whether the space should continue to operate without adequate oversight.

“We have seen characters assassinated. We have seen public institutions blackmailed. We have watched people deliberately distort facts. We have seen people unjustifiably peddling lies. We cannot fold our hands and allow this illegality to continue.

“I have been a victim of these outlawed activities at different times. I know many Nigerians have been victims as well. But the urgent questions are: Should we leave unregulated the space that will define our lives unregulated in the decades to come? Or do we prefer a space where characters are assassinated daily, lies peddled, and public institutions unjustifiably discredited,” he said.

He urged newspaper proprietors and other journalism regulatory bodies to discuss the consequences of unregulated social media and work toward lasting solutions.

“These are questions that key media actors – Newspaper Proprietors’ Association of Nigeria, Broadcasting Organisations of Nigeria, Nigerian Guild of Editors, and Nigeria Union of Journalists – must honestly answer in this age of information technology. Otherwise, we must all brace up for the consequences of our inability to act at the time that matters most.

“We all know that information is critical to our national development as much as to our internal stability. Obviously, this suggests that the way we disseminate information, whether through the traditional or social media, must be well guided by international best practices.

“This further suggests that information must be disseminated objectively and responsibly with the intention to inform and not disinform; build and not destroy; develop and not blackmail,” Mr Bamidele stated.

World.title: Lagos health providers demand fair tariffs, prompt payment of claims
World.content:
The Permanent Secretary, Lagos State Health Management Agency (LASHMA) and the Chairman, Healthcare Providers Association of Nigeria, Lagos State Branch, Dr. Abimbola Julius Adekoya, during a courtesy visit by the HCPAN on LASHMA at Ikeja

… Seek inclusive participation in ILERA EKO, stronger partnership with LASHMA

By Chioma Obinna

Healthcare providers in Lagos State have called on the Lagos State Health Management Agency (LASHMA) to review reimbursement rates, ensure prompt payment of claims and guarantee inclusive participation of healthcare professionals in the implementation of the state’s health insurance programme.

The Healthcare Providers Association of Nigeria (HCPAN), Lagos State, made the demands during a courtesy visit by its newly elected executive members to the Permanent Secretary of LASHMA, Dr Emmanuella Zamba, at the agency’s office on Wednesday, November 11, 2026.

The delegation, led by the newly elected Chairman of HCPAN Lagos, Mr Adekoya Abimbola Julius, said addressing the concerns of healthcare providers was essential to strengthening the ILERA EKO Health Insurance Programme and achieving Universal Health Coverage in the state.

Adekoya identified inadequate reimbursement rates, delays in claims processing and payment, complicated enrolment procedures and insufficient professional inclusiveness as key challenges requiring attention.

He stressed that expanding health insurance coverage must go hand in hand with creating sustainable operating conditions for healthcare facilities delivering services under the scheme.

“The success of health insurance depends not only on citizens’ enrolment but also on the ability of healthcare providers to deliver quality services under fair, sustainable and clearly defined operating conditions,” he said.

The HCPAN chairman also called for the recognition of all professional groups affiliated with the association within the programme’s implementation framework, noting that the participation of different healthcare professionals was essential to comprehensive healthcare delivery.

He urged LASHMA to simplify enrolment procedures, strengthen engagement with providers and establish efficient mechanisms for processing and settling claims.

Responding, Zamba acknowledged the concerns and assured the association that the agency would give them attention.

She described the meeting as a “family meeting,” recognising HCPAN as a critical stakeholder in the actualisation of Universal Health Coverage in Lagos State.

On the demand for tariff adjustment, the Permanent Secretary acknowledged the need to review existing reimbursement rates but explained that the rates were also influenced by the premiums affordable to enrollees.

She disclosed that the existing tariff was due for review after the stipulated two-year period, expressing hope that the process would accommodate an adjustment in 2027.

Zamba also assured healthcare providers that the agency would work towards improving claims processing and payment mechanisms, acknowledging their importance to the sustainability of participating healthcare facilities.

She further expressed willingness to participate in the association’s proposed retreat and regular webinar series to deepen engagement, promote professional education and address emerging challenges in the health insurance system.

Earlier, LASHMA officials briefed the HCPAN delegation on the agency’s activities, operational framework and progress in implementing the state’s health insurance policy.

The presentations covered the Lagos State Executive Order EO/BOS/01 of 2024, provider onboarding into ILERA EKO, Provider-Led Enrolment, LASHMA-AID and the agency’s quality assurance framework.

Also speaking, the immediate past President of HCPAN Nigeria, Dr Jimmy Adeyeye Arigbabuwo, called for sustained capacity-building programmes to educate healthcare providers and other stakeholders on their responsibilities in achieving Universal Health Coverage.

He said continuous stakeholder education would improve understanding of the insurance system, strengthen service delivery and minimise operational challenges.

Similarly, the immediate past Chairman of HCPAN Lagos, Pharmacist Biola Paul-Ozieh, commended Zamba’s efforts in advancing the agency’s activities and urged both parties to sustain dialogue and cooperation.

She said the success of ILERA EKO depended on the willingness of government and healthcare providers to identify implementation challenges and work towards practical solutions.

The HCPAN delegation included the Deputy Chairman, Dr Deji Akinlade; General Secretary, Pharmacist Ajalo Abraham; and Publicity Secretary, Mr Jimoh Ayuba.

The engagement comes as Lagos State intensifies efforts to expand health insurance coverage and advance Universal Health Coverage, with stakeholders stressing that fair reimbursement, timely claims settlement and effective collaboration remain important to the sustainability of the programme.

World.title: Diabetes: CAPPA urges FG, states to impose 20% sugary drinks tax, reform food policies
World.content:
By Chioma Obinna

On this day World Diabetes Day, the Corporate Accountability and Public Participation Africa (CAPPA) on Saturday called on the Federal Government and state governments to urgently reform Nigeria’s food policies, impose a minimum 20 per cent tax on sugar-sweetened beverages and tighten regulations on unhealthy food products to curb the rising burden of diabetes.

The organisation warned that efforts to tackle the disease would yield limited results if government focused on screening and treatment while allowing aggressive marketing, widespread availability and affordability of ultra-processed foods and sugary drinks to continue unchecked.

Making the call in a message to mark the 2026 World Diabetes Day, marked November 14, with the theme, “Early Action on Diabetes”, CAPPA said Nigeria faced an escalating diabetes crisis that required decisive government intervention beyond public awareness and individual lifestyle changes.

According to the organisation, Nigeria has the highest number of adults aged 20 to 79 living with diabetes in Africa, while nearly three in four adults with diabetes across the continent remain undiagnosed.

It warned that delayed diagnosis exposes millions of Nigerians to potentially life-threatening complications, including kidney failure, blindness, stroke and amputations.

CAPPA also raised the alarm over the financial burden of diet-related non-communicable diseases, citing an estimated N1.92 trillion annual out-of-pocket expenditure by Nigerian households on their treatment.

Executive Director of CAPPA, Akinbode Oluwafemi, said diabetes prevention should not be reduced to individual discipline when commercial interests and unhealthy food environments increasingly shape people’s dietary choices.

He said: “We cannot keep telling Nigerians to eat healthily while allowing unhealthy food and beverages to dominate our markets, schools, s and public spaces.

“Early action on diabetes must begin with enacting and implementing strong regulatory policies that make healthy choices possible, affordable and accessible, not simply with advising people to change their dietary behaviour.”

The organisation cited its 2025 report, Junk On Our Plates, which documented aggressive marketing of ultra-processed foods and beverages high in sugar and sodium across seven Nigerian states.

It said the report exposed the targeting of children, young people and low-income communities through advertising, celebrity endorsements, misleading nutrition labels and cultural imagery designed to promote unhealthy products.

To reverse the trend, CAPPA outlined five major policy interventions, beginning with the conclusion and enforcement of the proposed Sugar-Sweetened Beverage (SSB) tax.

It urged the House of Representatives and the Federal Executive to complete legislative action following the Senate’s passage of the tax review bill earlier this year.

The organisation advocated an inflation-adjusted excise tax of at least 20 per cent of the final retail price, in line with World Health Organisation recommendations.

It further called for transparent utilisation of the revenue generated to fund diabetes prevention and control, primary healthcare, disease screening, subsidies for healthy local foods and nutrition programmes.

CAPPA also urged the Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare and the National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC) to introduce mandatory Front-of-Pack Warning Labels on packaged products containing excessive sugar, sodium and unhealthy fats.

“Consumers have a fundamental right to know what is in their food without having to decode tiny, obscured print on the back of packages, as is currently the case,” it said.

The organisation demanded statutory restrictions on the marketing and sponsorship of sugary drinks and ultra-processed foods targeting children and adolescents across television, digital platforms and public spaces.

It also called on state governments to enforce federal public food procurement guidelines to ensure that schools, hospitals and other public institutions serve nutritious meals rather than ultra-processed products.

On what it described as industry interference in nutrition policies, CAPPA cautioned against healthwashing by manufacturers, involving misleading health claims, selective fortification and lifestyle imagery to portray unhealthy products as nutritious.

“Adding selected micronutrients to a sugary drink or a high-sodium bouillon cube does not erase excessive sugar, salt or other nutritional concerns. Fortification must never become a marketing licence to disguise unhealthy products or undermine policies that seek to reduce their consumption,” the organisation said.

Beyond food regulation, CAPPA urged federal and state governments to increase funding for primary healthcare centres to provide free or subsidised blood glucose testing, essential medicines and improved access to insulin.

It also advocated agricultural incentives for smallholder farmers producing indigenous fruits, vegetables and whole grains to improve the availability and affordability of nutritious local foods.

Oluwafemi said: “Diabetes is not inevitable, and early action against the condition must include action against the commercial practices that make unhealthy diets increasingly difficult to avoid.

“On this World Diabetes Day, we call on Nigerian lawmakers and regulators to choose the health and productivity of our people over the profit margins of ultra-processed food corporations.”

World.title: France beat Turkey to finish top of Nations League group
World.content:
France’s players celebrate at the end of the UEFA Nations League Group A1 football match between France and Turkey at Stade Atlantique in Bordeaux on November 15, 2026. (Photo by FRANCK FIFE / AFP)

France top the group after bouncing back from defeat to Italy with a 2-1 win over rock-bottom Turkey in Bordeaux.

Les Bleus will head into the draw for the last eight, scheduled for Friday in Nyon, Switzerland, as a seeded team, a position that ensures they will host the return leg in March 2027 but could mean they face Spain.

An Emirhan Topcu own goal just after half-time and Eli Junior Kroupi’s first goal for France were enough for Zinedine Zidane’s team to prevail and take top spot in the final round of of matches.

World.title: England end Spain’s 44-game unbeaten run with 3-2 win
World.content:
England’s defender #05 Ezri Konza (C) celebrates scoring his team’s second goal with teammates during the UEFA Nations League – League A day 6 group 3 – football match between Spain and England at Metropolitano Stadium in Madrid on November 15, 2026. (Photo by Javier SORIANO / AFP)

England snapped world champions Spain’s record unbeaten run with a 3-2 victory in Madrid on Sunday to clinch the top spot in Nations League group A3.

Goals from Harry Kane, Ezri Konsa and Ben White inflicted La Roja’s first loss in a competitive game since March 2023, after 44 without defeat.

England’s Elliot Anderson was sent off in the second half as Spain fought back from three goals down with strikes from Mikel Oyarzabal and Nico Williams, but Luis de la Fuente’s World Cup winners could not find the equaliser.

Both sides were already sure to progress, but as group winners England will be seeded for the quarter-finals in March.

Spain had beaten England in the Euro 2024 final before adding a second world crown this summer, while the Three Lions finished third.

“We knew we were going to beat them tonight, the message from the manager after the Croatia game (on Thursday) has been so positive,” England midfielder Declan Rice told ITV.

“The first 10 minutes was the best we’ve played.”

England coach Thomas Tuchel hailed his team on their superb performance in the Spanish capital.

“We brought everything to the table,” Tuchel told ITV.

“We were brave. Spirit wise, energy wise and also football quality was (all at the) highest level.”

Tuchel selected James Trafford in goal over Jordan Pickford and also brought White and Konsa into the side.

Teenage star Lamine Yamal was fit to start for Spain at Atletico Madrid’s Metropolitano stadium after missing their midweek win over the Czech Republic.

However the youngster did not see much of the ball in the first half as England came out strongly.

Spain goalkeeper Unai Simon produced a strong reaction save to deny Jude Bellingham, while Anthony Gordon had a dangerous shot blocked.

Ballon d’Or winner Kane, who beat Yamal to the award, sent an effort narrowly wide.

Barcelona defender Pau Cubarsi handed England the advantage when he clumsily felled Kane in the area on the stroke of half time.

The Bayern Munich hitman powered a perfect penalty past Simon, who dived the right way but to no avail.

– Quickfire double –

De la Fuente tried to react at half-time with a triple change, including throwing on Barcelona duo Fermin Lopez and Pedri, but England quickly found more joy.

Konsa headed home the second from Declan Rice’s corner in the 53rd minute after the Arsenal defender was left unmarked by Spain’s defence.

Four minutes later England sliced open Spain’s defence with Kane and Bellingham combining to set up White for the third.

La Roja clawed their way back into the game when Anderson fouled Yamal in the area as the Spain striker ran in on goal.

The Manchester City midfielder was dismissed and Oyarzabal slotted home the penalty.

Spain found a second when Gordon gave the ball away and Yamal fed Williams, whose shot hit the post and bounced in.

Williams curled over and Trafford superbly denied Yamal and Marc Cucurella as Spain looked fruitlessly for the goal they needed to preserve their unbeaten record.

Including friendlies, Spain had gone 43 straight matches without defeat.

“On the pitch everything happens very fast, it’s a pity,” Oyarzabal told TVE about England’s two goals early in the second half.

“You have to focus on what came after, the reaction — the team never stopped pushing, never stopped trying… their goalkeeper also deserves credit for us not having equalised.”

World.title: 2027: Soludo urges politicians to keep off places of worship
World.content:
Gov. Chukwuma Soludo of Anambra has urged politicians to keep politics away from places of worship, saying religious institutions should remain centres of spiritual growth and unity.

Soludo made the call during a visit to the Mountain of Holy Ghost Intervention Deliverance Ministry Inc., Onitsha, to celebrate its 30th anniversary.

The ministry was founded by Prophet Chukwuemeka Ohanaemere, popularly known as Odumeje.

He said: “Politicians, keep off places of worship! I do not do politics in the house of God.

“I deliberately avoided church campaigns for six months before the last governorship election in Anambra.

“My visit to religious institutions is usually motivated by my commitment to ecumenism and responsibility as the father of all in the state”.

The governor described the anniversary as a significant milestone, noting that it marked maturity, preparation and a new phase in the ministry’s growth.

He recalled that his first encounter with the ministry was during the demolition of part of its structure by the state government to facilitate the dredging of the Sakamori drainage channel.

Soludo commended Odumeje for his contributions to charity and efforts towards societal development.

He also acknowledged the cleric’s support for the state’s campaign against criminal idolatry and activities of illegal traditional spiritual practitioners.

According to him, the advocacy, alongside the Anambra Homeland Security Law, has contributed to making the state safer.

Responding, Odumeje pledged continued partnership with the state government to drive progress and development.

World.title: Video: Sanwo-Olu hosts boxing legend Floyd Mayweather in Lagos
World.content:
American boxing legend Floyd Mayweather has paid a courtesy visit to Lagos State Governor, Babajide Sanwo-Olu, at Lagos House, Marina, as part of his visit to Nigeria.

Mayweather, a former world champion and one of boxing’s most celebrated figures, arrived in the country to launch a boxing development initiative aimed at identifying and supporting young Nigerian fighters.

The Legendary International Boxing Champion, Floyd Mayweather @FloydMayweather today paid a Courtesy Visit to the Governor of Lagos State, Mr Babajide Sanwo-Olu @jidesanwoolu at the Lagos House, Marina.



Floyd Mayweather arrived Nigeria to launch a boxing development initiative… pic.twitter.com/SkchSCnfRD — Jubril A. Gawat (@Mr_JAGs) November 15, 2026

The initiative is expected to create opportunities for emerging boxers and contribute to the development of the sport in Nigeria.
