World.title: Musk, tech leaders back Jensen Huang as report alleges he misled Nvidia top execs over affair
World.content:
SAN FRANCISCO: Tech billionaire Elon Musk and Uber co-founder Travis Kalanick are among more than 158,000 people who have signed an open letter urging Nvidia’s board to reinstate former chief executive Jensen Huang, despite the scandal that ended his 33-year leadership of the AI chip giant.

The letter, which had garnered signatures from more than 7,500 Nvidia employees as of Sunday, calls on the board to “bring Jensen back while an independent investigation establishes the facts.”

Huang stepped down on Thursday after reports revealed he had engaged in two extramarital relationships, including one with Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang, who has been the subject of US scrutiny over alleged ties to Chinese intelligence activities, and another involving a subordinate employee.

The high-profile show of support highlights Huang’s standing in Silicon Valley, where he is widely regarded as one of the architects of the artificial intelligence boom.

Signatories include Epic Games founder and chief executive Tim Sweeney, as well as Y Combinator president Garry Tan.

Kalanick wrote in support of Huang that he had “erred, yes — to err is to be human — but I do not believe anything he has done rises to the bar of separating him from his company.”

Under Huang’s leadership, Nvidia became the dominant supplier of AI chips and a major investor in data centers and startups, earning it the nickname “the central bank of AI.”

The campaign comes as some investors urge Nvidia’s board to keep open the possibility of Huang’s return. According to the Financial Times, Huang has discussed a potential comeback with allies and is assembling a crisis team to seek support from the White House.

At the same time, pressure on the company continues to mount. Speaking on Fox News on Sunday, US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said Nvidia should look outside the company for its next chief executive and called for greater transparency over allegations that Nvidia chips had found their way into China despite export restrictions.

Reuters: Huang allegedly misled Nvidia leaders

New questions about Huang’s conduct emerged in an exclusive Reuters report citing people familiar with the matter and internal correspondence reviewed by the news agency.

According to Reuters, Huang allegedly misled several senior Nvidia executives, including general counsel Tim Teter and chief marketing officer Alison Wagonfeld, about the nature of his relationship with Alice Huang.

Reuters reported that, in messages sent during 2025 and again in October 2026 in response to media inquiries, Huang described his interactions with Alice Huang and her company, Megaspeed International, as ordinary customer-related business dealings. Two people familiar with the matter told Reuters that he did not disclose that the relationship was romantic.

The news agency said it reviewed October correspondence, though it did not publish the messages verbatim.

Reuters also reported that Huang discussed possible legal action against The New York Times after the newspaper highlighted his meetings with Alice Huang in an article last year. According to Reuters, neither Nvidia nor Huang ultimately sued the publication, and a spokesperson for the newspaper said it never received a legal demand.

Neither Teter nor Wagonfeld responded to Reuters requests for comment. Representatives for Huang and Nvidia declined comment.

Reuters said it was unable to independently verify whether Alice Huang worked on behalf of the Chinese government. Beijing has denied allegations that she was a spy.

The allegations come as Nvidia’s independent directors oversee an investigation being conducted by law firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz. The probe was launched after reports by The New York Times and The Wall Street Journal detailed Huang’s relationship with Alice Huang and US authorities’ concerns about her alleged links to Chinese intelligence.

Huang apologized on Sunday for being unfaithful to his wife and for disappointing the company, though he did not specifically name Alice Huang in his statement.

Nvidia’s shares have fallen more than 30 percent from their Oct. 6 peak, wiping out more than $1.8 trillion in market value, according to Reuters.

World.title: Estonia to close Russian border crossings after attempted arson attack
World.content:
Estonia will close all its border crossing points with Russia from ​December 1, its foreign minister said on Sunday, following a suspected sabotage attack on an Estonian defense company that Tallinn blamed on Moscow.

Estonian authorities detained eight people overnight on suspicion of an attempted arson attack on drone ‌maker Threod Systems ‌that they said had ​been ‌ordered ⁠by ​Russia’s GRU ⁠military intelligence service.

The government said an attempted attack had been carried out early Saturday against Threod Systems in Viimsi, north of the capital, Tallinn, “with the aim of causing an explosion and setting the building on fire.”

“If Russia continues its hybrid operations in Estonia, and we know that Russian intelligence services exploit border crossings to exert influence over people, we must be prepared to reduce the risks we face,” Prime Minister Kristen Michal said in a statement.

“Closing the border would reduce the threat to people in Estonia and send a clear message that attacks on Estonia’s defense industry and defense capabilities are unacceptable,” Michal added.

In Moscow, Russian Foreign Ministry spokeswoman Maria Zakharova told state news agency TASS that if Estonia truly shut its border it would be yet another demonstration of Russophobia.

.”..If these are ⁠their real plans, then they ‌fit into ‌yet another bout of aggressive and ​unrestrained Russophobia,” TASS quoted ‌Zakharova as saying.

Moscow has regularly ‌denied accusations by European authorities of involvement in sabotage operations.

“Russia must understand that hostile actions against Estonia come with consequences,” Foreign Minister ‌Margus Tsahkna said in a post on X.

He did not specify ⁠how ⁠long the border closure would last or if an end date had been set.

Estonia, a NATO and European Union member state and a strong supporter of Ukraine, currently has three open border crossings with Russia at Narva, Luhamaa and Koidula, which admit pedestrians and freight, according to Estonian public broadcaster ERR.

World.title: Unbeaten Andreeva captures WTA Finals crown on debut
World.content:
INDIAN WELLS, California: Russian teenager Mirra Andreeva beat Ukraine’s Elina Svitolina 7-5 6-3 on Sunday to win the WTA Finals, capping an unbeaten run ​in her singles debut at the season-ending championships in Indian Wells.

Andreeva threw her racket into the air and jumped for joy when Svitolina put an overhead into the net on match point, before hugging coach Conchita Martinez.

The 19-year-old French Open champion won all five of her matches without dropping a set at the event, which ‌brings together ‌the top eight players of the ​season.

She ‌takes ⁠home ​the maximum ⁠prize money of $3.37 million and the Billie Jean King Trophy. King watched the final from the stands on a sunny day in the California desert.

Andreeva will rise to a career-high world number two in Monday’s rankings.

She also won a custom Mercedes-Benz SL 55 painted in the WTA’s signature ⁠purple, though she does not yet have ‌a driver’s license.

Andreeva was the ‌favorite against Svitolina, the 2018 champion, ​and had beaten her 6-4 ‌6-0 on Monday in the round-robin stage.

The first set ‌was tight, with long rallies as both players tried to control points by pushing the other from side to side and drawing them in off the baseline.

Andreeva served for the set ‌at 5-4 but struggled, hitting two double faults and a backhand long to let Svitolina ⁠back into ⁠it.

She stayed composed, though, breaking Svitolina in the next game and then showing great poise to serve out the 55-minute set.

The intensity stayed high in the second set, including a 10-minute seventh game, the longest of the tournament, which featured six deuces. Svitolina won the game when Andreeva sent a backhand wide to cut her opponent’s lead to 4-3.

But frustration began to mount for Svitolina during the subsequent changeover as she gestured to her ​team and Andreeva rolled ​on from there, breaking Svitolina for a sixth time to seal the win.

World.title: England beat Spain in Nations League to end record unbeaten run
World.content:
MADRID: England snapped world champions Spain’s unbeaten run with a 3-2 victory in Madrid on Sunday to clinch the top spot in Nations League group A3.

Goals from Harry Kane, Ezri Konsa and Ben White inflicted La Roja’s first loss in a competitive game since March 2023, after 44 without defeat.

England’s Elliot Anderson was sent off in the second half as Spain fought back from three goals down with strikes from Mikel Oyarzabal and Nico Williams, but Luis de la Fuente’s World Cup winners could not find the equalizer.

Both sides were already sure to progress, but as group winners England will be seeded for the quarter-finals in March.

England coach Thomas Tuchel selected James Trafford in goal over Jordan Pickford and also brought White and Konsa into the side.

Teenage star Lamine Yamal was fit to start for Spain at Atletico Madrid’s Metropolitano stadium after missing their midweek win over the Czech Republic.

However the youngster did not see much of the ball in the first half as England came out strongly.

Spain goalkeeper Unai Simon produced a strong reaction save to deny Jude Bellingham, while Anthony Gordon had a dangerous shot blocked.

Ballon d’Or winner Kane, who beat Yamal to the award, sent an effort narrowly wide.

Barcelona defender Pau Cubarsi handed England the advantage when he clumsily felled Kane in the area on the stroke of half time.

The Bayern Munich hitman powered a perfect penalty past Simon, who dived the right way but to no avail.

De la Fuente tried to react at half-time with a triple change, including throwing on Barcelona duo Fermin Lopez and Pedri, but England quickly found more joy.

Konsa headed home the second from Declan Rice’s corner in the 53rd minute after the Arsenal defender was left unmarked by Spain’s defense.

Four minutes later England sliced open Spain’s defense with Kane and Bellingham combining to set up White for the third.

La Roja clawed their way back into the game when Elliot Anderson fouled Yamal in the area as the Spain striker ran in on goal.

The Manchester City midfielder was dismissed and Mikel Oyarzabal slotted home the penalty.

Spain found a second when Gordon gave the ball away and Yamal fed Nico Williams, whose shot hit the post and bounced in.

Williams curled over and Trafford denied Yamal and Marc Cucurella as Spain looked fruitlessly for the goal they needed to preserve their unbeaten record.

World.title: Zelensky says Russia’s energy attacks helped by Starshield restrictions
World.content:
KYIV: Russia struck energy and railway ​infrastructure in eight regions of Ukraine overnight, President Volodymyr Zelensky said on Sunday, in attacks he said were made possible partly due to restrictions on Ukraine’s use of SpaceX’s ‌Starshield service.

“The ‌Russians are targeting ​substations ‌with ‘shaheds,’” Zelensky ⁠said ​on X, ⁠referring to the drones Russia commonly launches across Ukraine. “And many of these strikes are getting through because restrictions on the speed of Starshield terminals ⁠along the front line and ‌in ‌the temporarily occupied territories are ​still there.”

Speaking ‌later in his nightly ‌video address, Zelensky said Russian forces had lately been singling out specific regions and then repeatedly striking them ‌over several days. Zelensky said the southeastern Dnipropetrovsk and ⁠Zaporizhzhia ⁠regions had been particularly badly hit, with repair work proceeding on the grid and on specific substations.

“There have been many outages, and restoration is proceeding,” Zelensky said. “Power has been restored to some extent, but there is still a lot ​of work ​ahead.”

Darker days ahead



Zelensky warned that limitations on the system, operated by Elon Musk’s SpaceX, could weaken defenses around Ukraine’s energy infrastructure ahead of the winter months, when Moscow has repeatedly targeted the power grid.

Ukraine’s interceptor drones continue to lose contact with their operators when flying faster than 161 kph (100 mph) along the front line and over Russian-occupied territory, leaving them unable to catch Russian Shahed drones, Zelensky said.

“We are counting on these restrictions to be lifted,” he wrote on social media. “The protection of lives and Ukrainian energy infrastructure before winter depends on this. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs, the Ministry of Defense, and the President’s Office have been instructed to work closely with the American side and SpaceX. It is important to be on the right side of history. We need to help Ukraine.”

Zelensky questioned Saturday whether the problem was technical, saying the restrictions appeared to have been imposed by SpaceX despite earlier assurances from US Secretary of State Marco Rubio that Starshield was more under US government control.

Outages after Russian strike on power facility

Meanwhile, a Russian strike on Chornomorsk, a port city in Ukraine’s Odesa region, injured six people and damaged energy infrastructure, regional head Oleh Kiper said Sunday on Telegram.

The blast and falling debris also damaged a gas pipeline and nearby residential buildings, while two parked cars caught fire.

The strike hit a facility operated by DTEK Odesa Electric Networks, temporarily leaving about 41,000 customers without power, Kiper said.

Overnight Russian airstrikes on the southeastern city of Zaporizhzhia injured another six people, including a 2-year-old boy, Ukraine’s State Emergency Service said Sunday.

Russia launched more than 2,300 drones, 1,590 guided aerial bombs and 15 missiles of various types against Ukraine over the past week, Zelensky said.

Ukrainian attack kills 1 in Russia’s Rostov region

Ukrainian drone strikes damaged two electrical substations in Russia’s Rostov region, killing a chief engineer, Gov. Yuri Slyusar said Sunday.

Four people were injured when drone debris fell on their cars, Slyusar wrote on social media. A fifth person was wounded when debris struck a “production facility” in the village of Troitskoye, he said.

Ukrainian forces also targeted Russia’s Tatarstan region, officials said. Radmir Belyaev, mayor of Nizhnekamsk, the region’s third-largest city, said a “large-scale and prolonged attack” damaged its industrial zone.

Six people were injured, and heating and hot water supplies were disrupted in parts of the city, he said.

Ukraine’s General Staff said it had hit two sites in Nizhnekamsk: Nizhnekamskneftekhim, one of the largest petrochemical complexes in Europe, and a production site operated by petrochemical company Sibur. An oil refinery in the area was also hit, it said.

Russia’s Defense Ministry said its forces shot down 533 Ukrainian drones overnight across 13 Russian regions, the Russian-annexed Ukrainian peninsula of Crimea, and the Black and Azov seas.

Drones damage Black Sea ships, Romania says

Romanian Prime Minister Luca Niculescu said Sunday that three commercial vessels in the Black Sea were struck by drones overnight, the latest in a string of attacks that have raised fears of the war spilling over into NATO territory.

“Once again, maritime security in the Black Sea has been threatened,” Niculescu wrote on X.

Romania’s Ministry of National Defense said a Greek-flagged oil tanker was struck by a drone, sparking a fire that was extinguished by the crew. Two more ships were later struck by drones, and their crews also extinguished fires onboard, the ministry said. No casualties were reported and the ministry did not state the origin of the drones.

“These incidents are unacceptable and constitute a violation of international law,” Niculescu said, adding that they “reflect the deteriorating security situation caused by Russia’s ongoing war against Ukraine.”

Last month, a string of cargo ships and tankers were struck by aerial or naval drones near the Bulgarian and Romanian coastlines. At least 30 sailors on commercial ships were confirmed dead or reported missing.

“We will continue to take all necessary measures, alongside our Allies, to strengthen security in the Black Sea,” Niculescu added. “This remains a key priority for the Government, in close cooperation with our regional partners and NATO.”

World.title: Police ban protests near some Paris schools and universities
World.content:
PARIS, France: The police in Paris on Sunday issued a ban on protests near 10 high schools and five universities, amid a blockade movement that has gone on for two months.

The order prohibits unauthorized gatherings or marches within 100 meters of the sites from Monday through to Friday.

High school pupils began to blockade school entrances in mid-September to protest against substandard classroom conditions.

University students joined the movement, which quickly spread around France and fed into other demonstrations by unions over inflation and the cost of living.

The police ban applies to 10 of the French capital’s roughly 150 secondary schools, and to universities including faculties at the Sorbonne.

Paris police chief Patrice Faure said in the order that the ban was necessary because of “numerous disruptions and blockades around certain high schools and establishments of higher learning in Paris and the surrounding region, as part of a social movement at persistent scale and violence.”

He said 1,548 arrests had been made since the start of the protests and several public buildings vandalized.

Faure said the high school and university blockades were carried out “most often by a minority of students” who were stopping others from receiving education.

World.title: Pope laments Amazon’s ‘cry,’ says rainforest and peoples under threat
World.content:
PUCALLPA, Peru: Pope Leo XIV visited the Peruvian Amazon on Sunday, demanding justice for Indigenous leaders killed defending their territories and warning that environmental destruction was ravaging both the rainforest and its peoples.

“The blood of these brothers cries out to God and demands justice,” he told missionaries and representatives of Amazonian peoples in the jungle city of Pucallpa.

“The cry of the earth and the cry of the poor are inseparable,” he said.

Many in the crowd mixed traditional tunics and red-and-black face paint with baseball caps to shield themselves from the Amazon heat.

One banner carried by Indigenous communities read: “The world watches, our rainforest disappears.”

When a voice over the loudspeaker asked, “Where is the pope?” the crowd roared back: “In the Amazon!“

As they waited for his arrival, flutes echoed across the waterfront while dancers in sky-blue, red and yellow scarves and black skirts performed for the crowd.

The pope said many Indigenous leaders had been murdered in recent years while defending their lands and denounced what he called the unacceptable neglect suffered by many Indigenous communities.

He said it was unacceptable that many communities lacked access to health care and education because of geographical isolation and institutional neglect.

Leo also cited deforestation, illegal mining and oil pollution as examples of environmental damage threatening both the forest and the people who depend on it.

Several thousand people gathered along Pucallpa’s waterfront for the event, with organizers expecting around 3,000 participants and some 70,000 later for Mass.

As the pope arrived, children shouted “Pope in the red land” and stretched out their hands to greet him.

Among those attending was 17-year-old Cristiano Ricopa, dressed in a black-and-white tunic and a necklace of red seeds, preparing to sing for the pontiff in the language of his Aerija people.

World.title: Jeddah governor receives Libyan consul general as minister meets Chechen president
World.content:
Jeddah Governor Prince Saud bin Abdullah bin Jalawi received Libyan Consul General Abdulrazzaq Al-Menfi at the governorate headquarters in Jeddah on Sunday.

They exchanged cordial remarks and discussed issues of mutual interest, the Saudi Press Agency reported.

Meanwhile, on Saturday, Saudi Minister of State and Cabinet Member Prince Turki bin Mohammed met Chechen Republic President Ramzan Kadyrov at the presidential headquarters in Grozny.

World.title: Iraq plans to build new airport in Baghdad
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s National Investment Commission (NIC) announced that it is moving to build a new airport in Baghdad with an annual capacity of 20 million passengers.

Adel al-Yasiri, the chairman of the NIC, said that the commission is currently preparing a site spanning approximately 20 square kilometers near the capital, Baghdad, for the development of one of the largest airports.

With an operating capacity of up to 20 million passengers annually, the project is expected to be managed by large multinational companies and developed through an investment-based strategy.

The project is anticipated to be constructed using an investment-based strategy and operated by major international corporations, with an operational capacity of up to 20 million passengers annually.

According to al-Yasiri, the NIC has put forward proposals for both the development of Baghdad International Airport and the enhancement of Mosul International Airport.

The plans are part of broader efforts to develop infrastructure and enhance Iraq’s capacity to accommodate air traffic, the state-run Iraqi News Agency (INA) reported.

The Iraqi cabinet announced in late October that it awarded a contract to develop and operate Baghdad International Airport to a consortium comprising Corporacion America Airports and Amwaj International.

The $764 million contract includes the construction of a new terminal designed to handle up to 15 million passengers annually, according to the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO).

The consortium’s plan was chosen as the best offer, with 43.05 percent of the airport’s annual revenue flowing to the national treasury throughout the concession period.

World.title: Iraq crowned Asian Bodybuilding Champions in Thailand with 41 medals
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s national bodybuilding team clinched the overall team title at the IFBB Asian Championships in Pattaya, Thailand, on Sunday, November 15, 2026, dominating the continent with a commanding 41-medal haul and 518 total points.

Iraqi Bodybuilding and Fitness Federation President Faez Abdul-Hassan confirmed that Iraq’s delegation—comprising over 40 athletes—secured the top podium spot across the continental standings. The team’s medal tally broke down as follows:

Gold Medals: 9

Silver Medals: 16

Bronze Medals: 16

Iraq finished far ahead of its closest regional rivals in the overall team standings, topping runner-up Oman (174 points) by a margin of 344 points, while the United Arab Emirates secured third place.

Abdul-Hassan praised the technical caliber and preparation of the Iraqi athletes, emphasizing that the victory adds another milestone to Iraq’s sporting record—building directly on the squad’s recent 35-medal showing at the Mr. Universe International Championship in Beirut—and underscores the national team’s sustained regional dominance on international podiums.

World.title: Hajime Moriyasu demands direct talks with IFA chief Younis Mahmoud over Iraq coaching role
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Japanese manager Hajime Moriyasu has set a strict condition for entering negotiations with the Iraqi Football Association (IFA) to take over as head coach of the Iraqi national team, stipulating that all discussions must be conducted directly with him, completely bypassing intermediaries and sports marketing agencies.

IFA President Younis Mahmoud is considering traveling to Japan to hold direct face-to-face talks with Moriyasu to explore reaching a formal agreement, pending final executive approval to initiate the official mission.

The 58-year-old tactician is one of Asian football’s most accomplished coaches, having led Japan’s national squad since 2018. Under his tenure, Japan compiled a record of 78 wins and 15 draws across 112 matches, achieving several major milestones:

2019 AFC Asian Cup: Guided Japan to a runner-up finish.

2022 FIFA World Cup (Qatar): Reached the Round of 16 after securing upset group-stage victories over Germany and Spain.

2023 AFC Asian Cup: Advanced to the quarterfinals.

2026 FIFA World Cup: Led Japan to the Round of 32.

Recent Landmark Victory: Claimed a historic 3–2 friendly win over Brazil in Singapore on November 14, 2026.

Moriyasu is scheduled to conclude his eight-year tenure with the Japan Football Association following their upcoming friendly match against Paraguay on November 17, 2026, having brought forward his departure date in light of the postponement of the 2027 AFC Asian Cup.

World.title: Vodafone Qatar, Iraq’s ITPC sign deal on digital infrastructure
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Vodafone Qatar and Iraq’s state-owned Informatics and Telecom Public Company (ITPC) signed a cooperation agreement during Mobile World Congress (MWC) Doha 2026.

The deal establishes a framework to explore cross-border telecommunications and digital infrastructure projects.

The agreement was signed last week during the presence of Iraq’s Minister of Communications, Mustafa Sanad.

The framework outlines areas for technical and commercial evaluation rather than immediate, confirmed capital investments. Any resulting projects will require separate binding contracts and full regulatory compliance.

Both entities will evaluate data transit projects running through Iraq alongside fiber infrastructure opportunities.

The partnership seeks to evaluate the joint development of internet exchange points, which will enhance both regional and international internet connectivity.

Both firms will study linking their respective networks to optimize resource usage and streamline cross-border data traffic.

Additionally, technical teams will exchange knowledge on network management and operations to identify commercially viable joint ventures.

ITPC aims to leverage Iraq’s strategic geography to modernize its domestic telecom sector and serve as a major regional hub for data traffic.

The agreement aligns with wider regional infrastructure efforts, including recent partnerships between ITPC and Ooredoo to build digital transit corridors linking Asia, the Gulf, and Europe.

World.title: Zaidi gives Kata’ib Hezbollah end-of-week deadline to vacate Jurf Al Nasr
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister and Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces Ali Faleh Al-Zaidi has issued a final ultimatum giving Kata’ib Hezbollah until the end of this week to hand over full security and military control of the Jurf al-Nasr (Jurf al-Sakhar) subdistrict in northern Babylon Governorate to federal forces, warning of an impending military intervention led by the Counter-Terrorism Service (CTS) if mediation fails.

According to informed government and political sources, Al-Zaidi conveyed the non-negotiable deadline through intermediaries from the Popular Mobilization Forces (PMF/Hashd al-Shaabi) and the ruling Coordination Framework.

The Prime Minister warned that if the faction refuses to withdraw peacefully, elite CTS units will be deployed in the coming days to assert full state authority across the entire subdistrict, emphasizing that any party obstructing federal forces will be prosecuted under Iraq’s Anti-Terrorism Law with full backing from the judiciary.

The standoff escalated sharply after Al-Zaidi received the formal findings of the government commission investigating crude oil smuggling in Jurf al-Nasr. The report confirmed extensive pipeline breaches and clandestine oil-refining facilities inside the closed zone, noting that armed elements actively blocked federal investigators from inspecting several restricted sectors.

In immediate response to the commission’s report, the Commander-in-Chief ordered sweeping judicial referrals and administrative dismissals:

Judicial Referrals: Referred all suspects implicated in the smuggling network directly to the judiciary.

Security & Administrative Dismissals: Relieved multiple senior security, military, and administrative officials in Babylon Governorate—including the Provincial Police Chief and senior officers across intelligence agencies, National Security, the Hashd al-Shaabi, Energy Police, and the Oil Pipelines Company.

Maximum Alert Status: Placed military and security formations on Alert Level “C” (Indhar Jim)—Iraq’s highest state of operational readiness—accompanied by troop movements toward northern Babylon and additional Federal Police deployments tightening perimeter checkpoints.

Over recent days, Al-Zaidi held intensive crisis consultations with senior Coordination Framework and Hashd al-Shaabi leaders—including Badr Organization Secretary-General Hadi Al-Amiri, PMF Commission Chairman Falih Al-Fayyadh, and PMF Chief of Staff Abdul-Aziz Al-Muhammadawi (“Abu Fadak”)—who are attempting to broker a peaceful handover to avert an armed clash between state forces and Kata’ib Hezbollah.

Sources also revealed that an earlier federal contingency plan—which had envisioned deploying three brigades from the Shrine Brigades (Quwat al-Atabat), the Third Division of the Federal Police, and CTS detachments—was shelved after its operational axes were leaked, prompting Baghdad to formulate an alternative operation centered directly on elite Counter-Terrorism Service units to retake the entirety of Jurf al-Nasr rather than merely reinforcing outer perimeters.

World.title: 9 Iraqi officials dismissed following investigation into oil smuggling network
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi dismissed nine senior security and administrative officials on Saturday following an investigation into an oil smuggling network in the Jurf al-Sakhr area, ordering those involved to be referred to the judiciary.

The dismissals targeted senior provincial police, intelligence, the National Security Service, Popular Mobilization Forces (PMF), Energy Police, and Oil Ministry pipeline officials in Babil province. The Babil governor also resigned following earlier denials of the illicit activity.

An official committee confirmed illegal refineries and pipeline tampering via geospatial data.

Reports mentioned that the operation siphoned fuel from strategic pipelines south of Baghdad, accumulating up to $30 million monthly since 2021.

The Jurf al-Sakher area is a key stronghold of the Iran-backed group Kataib Hezbollah.

According to the state-run Iraqi News Agency (INA), intelligence documents with satellite images showed crude oil and oil-derivatives smuggling activities carried out by an armed faction in Jurf al-Sakher. The faction was accused of tapping into a pipeline in the area.

According to Iraq’s military spokesman Sabah al-Numan, the investigating committee confirmed the accuracy of the information.

World.title: Iraq’s oil shipments to Syria’s Baniyas port hit 150,000 bpd
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq is transporting between 120,000 and 150,000 barrels of crude oil per day by tanker trucks from its southern oil fields to the Syrian port of Baniyas on the Mediterranean Sea, according to Basim Abdul-Karim, head of the state-owned Basra Oil Company (BOC).

The transport operations began on October 26, using a land route that had seen little use for decades. This move comes as Iraq seeks alternative outlets for its oil exports following disruptions to shipping through the Strait of Hormuz.

Qatar-based UCC Holding is handling the transport of the crude under a deal with Iraq’s State Oil Marketing Organization (SOMO), according to Abdul-Karim. The daily volume transported depends on the number of tanker trucks available.

UCC Holding has transported approximately 1.6 million barrels from the Tuba field depot near Basra since the agreement went into effect, with hundreds of trucks lining up at the facility to load crude oil before heading toward the Syrian border.

Tanker trucks wait at the Syrian border until they can form a convoy of 100 to 150 vehicles each before continuing their journey to Baniyas, a round trip taking between four and five days.

In Baniyas, the crude oil is loaded onto vessels and transported to refineries across the Mediterranean—including those in Greece, Italy, and Turkey.

Reports indicate that the group plans to load between five million and 14 million barrels of heavy crude over a three-month period, at a discount of $38 per barrel. Under the agreement, the group receives $12 per barrel to cover the costs of trucking and transit across Syria.

World.title: US accuses Iran of plundering Iraq’s resources
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The US Department of State has accused Tehran of employing Iraqi militias—including Kata’ib Hezbollah—to steal Iraq’s resources.

The declaration was made in response to allegations of petroleum product smuggling in the Jurf al-Sakhr area, according to Sky News Arabia.

A spokesperson for the US State Department told the news outlet that Iran has a long history of using Iraqi militias to plunder the country’s resources.

The spokesperson accused these groups of undermining Iraq’s sovereignty and weakening its economy, noting that they use the funds of corruption to serve their interests and those of the regime in Tehran.

Washington has placed sanctions on Kata’ib Hezbollah and designated it as a foreign terrorist organization.

The United States will continue to target entities that generate illicit revenue, as well as those who facilitate their financial transactions, as part of a pressure campaign led by President Donald Trump against Iran.

A document issued by the office of the Commander-in-Chief of the Iraqi Armed Forces revealed that Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi has ordered the formation of a committee to investigate the smuggling of petroleum products in Jurf al-Sakhr—referred to in the document as Jurf al-Nasr.

World.title: Security booster for Bachchan, others on Lawrence's target list
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Against the backdrop of the Lawrence Bishnoi gang escalating threats against top Bollywood actors, the noose appears to be tightening around the jailed gangster, as investigators have sought his visitors' list from Ahmedabad's Sabarmati Central Jail and are reviewing the security of stars who have recently been threatened or attacked.

The developments in Delhi and Mumbai come amid the arrest of his shooters for allegedly attempting to target high-profile figures, including

, which has prompted

to reassess the security provided to celebrities on the syndicate's radar.

The gang's targets include

, who was attacked in Oct; threats have been issued to stars such as Salman Khan, Aamir Khan, Ranveer Singh, Kapil Sharma and Guru Randhawa.

Most of them already have Y and Y plus category security, but to bolster it further, these actors are being assigned an additional two to four commandos, alongside armed cops and personal security officers to ensure round-the-clock protection.



The letter to Sabarmati jail was sent by Delhi Police. Jail sources said the information has not been provided yet.

Focus on barring Lawrence from issuing orders from prison

The move to study Bishnoi's visitor logs stems from the revelation made during a separate but related investigation in which an individual, whose identity has not been disclosed, claimed he was taken to Sabarmati jail by Lawrence's arrested legal team member Deepak Khatri to allegedly settle an extortion demand.





A few individuals have also deposed before a magistrate in Delhi and recorded their statements regarding Khatri's alleged extortion racket being run on Lawrence's behalf, the sources said.

The investigators now aim to understand and dismantle the mechanism that allows his syndicate to issue orders from behind bars. Despite strict confinement restrictions, intelligence and police agencies suspect that physical visitors, alongside encrypted international conduits, could be used as couriers to relay instructions to his "shadow cabinet".

World.title: Those using Form 6 to re-enroll won't be prosecuted: EC to SC
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The

has assured

that all attempts will be made to include every eligible citizen in the electoral rolls and no prosecution would be launched against people whose names were deleted from the post-SIR draft electoral rolls, for using Form 6 for restoration of their names in the voters' lists.

EC's stand, spelt out in an affidavit filed Saturday, is in sync with the Oct 26 assurance given by a bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana while hearing petitions relating to alleged large-scale deletion of voters in Maharashtra and Delhi. The CJI-led bench had said, "No one will be prosecuted for filling Form 6 seeking re-entering of their names in voters' lists."

Petitioners had highlighted voters' apprehension that they might be prosecuted for giving a false declaration in Form 6, which is used for enrolling new voters, that they had never been registered as voters before.



Errors likely in weeding out dead, non-existent voters: EC

EC said, "No prosecution will be launched against anyone for filing Form 6 merely on the ground that the applicant/elector was previously enrolled in the electoral roll(s) prior to the SIR and their names did not appear in the draft electoral rolls during the SIR."

However, EC said those filling Form 6 to restore their names in the electoral rolls must ensure their names do not figure in the voters' lists in any other assembly or parliamentary constituency.





Assuring the court that efforts have been intensified to register every eligible citizen as a voter, EC said, "A mechanism has also been directed to be put in place to ensure that no elector is deprived of the opportunity to get his/her name included in the final electoral roll, subject to fulfilment of the prescribed eligibility conditions, while taking due care to avoid duplication in enrolment."

Accepting that there may have been errors in weeding out non-existent and dead voters from the electoral rolls through SIR, the commission said, "There are challenges on count of the large numbers involved, and also because the full data is being digitised.

There have been and will be problems that arise from time to time and the commission remains alive to the need to ensure that all those who are eligible to vote find their name in the voters' lists but equally, to ensure that all inconsistencies in these lists are addressed.

"

On complaints about large-scale deletion of voters in Delhi through SIR in the ASDD (absent, shifted, duplicate and dead) category, EC said those left out of the draft electoral rolls could submit fresh enumeration forms to electoral registration officers or assistant EROs at their current residential place.

"Electors who have not shifted may submit the signed enumeration form with the statement giving the reason for the earlier non-submission of the enumeration form. They can submit it to the ERO/AERO/BLO in person or through family members. Online submission option with e-sign will be available on ECINET," it said.

World.content:
London: IPL founder

Still have Vanuatu passport , says Lalit

It is one of the most difficult citizenships in world to get.

I just got a letter from Home Office in July saying it's approved." He said he will either apply for OCI or might get a visa if he decides to go to India.

World.title: Empty Vande Bharat allowed to run 463km despite 'poor power brake'
World.content:
NEW DELHI: An empty Vande Bharat train was allowed to travel around 463km from Hatia in Jharkhand to Deen Dayal Upadhyaya station in UP despite two loco pilots reporting "poor power brake".

The incident happened on Oct 24, as per a document of South Eastern Railway, and posed a potential risk to other passenger trains. In a Nov 7 order, the zone directed Ranchi divisional railway manager to investigate the incident "to ascertain the lapses on part of staff concerned" for taking necessary steps.

World.title: CRPF men in anti-Naxal ops diverted to Manipur
World.content:
New Delhi/Raipur:

has withdrawn a battalion comprising more than 1,000 personnel from the anti-Naxal operations theatre in Chhattisgarh and sent it to

for deployment.

The development marks the first such de-induction of any CAPF unit following Centre's declaration that Naxalism in India ended in March.

Temporary withdrawal of companies (part of a battalion) has occurred for various internal security duties, such as the West Bengal elections, the Amarnath Yatra and protests in Delhi.

Officials said the battalion was based in the former Maoist hotbed of Sukma. "This is the first full withdrawal of paramilitary unit from the anti-Naxal operations following the declaration that armed Maoism in the country ended in March," a security officer based in Delhi said.

World.title: Shah hits back at Rahul, says he's defaming India at global platforms
World.content:
PUNE:Union home minister

Sunday accused leader of the opposition

of attempting to tarnish India's image on an international platform, referring to his remarks at the Bharat Summit 2026 in Hyderabad.

The Union minister was addressing a gathering at the foundation stone-laying ceremony of National Heavy Engineering Cooperative Ltd in in Pune.

Referring to the Congress-organised summit in Hyderabad on Nov 13-14, Shah said, "The summit was named Bharat Summit, but Rahul expressed anti-India views at an international conference and attempted to defame India on the global platform."

Shah was referring to Rahul's statement at the summit that India was no longer a democracy and that BJP was "systematically weakening" democratic institutions.



"I strongly condemn Rahul ji's attempt to defame India, India's development story, India's democracy and our PM on an international platform," he said, adding, "Whether it is the governing party or the opposition, or any political party, can you defame India and India's PM at an international summit?"

World.title: India bucks trend, 38 institutions up in QS sustainability study
World.content:
NEW DELHI: India was only one of the world's five most represented systems to record more universities rising than falling in QS World University Rankings: Sustainability 2027.

Of 99 entries, 38 climbed, 34 declined and 19 were unchanged. The number in top 500 rose to 13 from five in 2023.

IIT-Delhi led India at 194th, up 11 places, followed by IIT-Kharagpur at 224th and Delhi University at 237th. JNU rose 192 places to 432nd. India has 42 universities in the top 1,000, joint third with mainland China, but none in the top 100. The gains masked a sharp divide: 61% of institutions slipped in governance rankings and 57% in environmental impact, even as 65% improved in social impact. IIT-Delhi was the only institution in top 100 for environmental impact, at 89th.

India, however, remained among the 18 lowest-scoring systems for impact of education. QS CEO Jessica Turner said India was improving in key sustainability metrics but lagged peers in impact of education. â- Manash Gohain

World.title: Yemeni government forces retreat from strait in major setback in war against Houthis
World.content:
Yemeni government forces announced on Sunday (November 15, 2026) that they were withdrawing from the area near the Bab el-Mandeb Strait to focus on a defence of their ​main base in Aden, in a major setback for the Saudi-backed campaign against the Iran-aligned Houthis.

The announcement signalled the apparent ‌end of a six-week government counteroffensive to reclaim the coast near the mouth of the ​Red Sea, seized by the Houthis in September in a lightning advance that ⁠squeezed oil exports.

Sunday's announcement of a government retreat raises the prospect of new Houthi advances towards Aden, and underscores the predicament faced by Saudi Arabia in trying to stop the Houthis' drone and missile attacks on the kingdom. The government ‌forces have been based in Aden on the southern coast since 2015 after the Houthis seized the capital Sanaa.

Houthi gains in Yemen and attacks on Saudi Arabia and ‌Red Sea shipping in recent months have strengthened the position of Iran in the wider West Asia conflict ⁠launched by the United States and Israel in February.

"The Southern Armed Forces announce the ⁠implementation of a redeployment operation for its forces from Dhubab Airport and the Bab el-Mandeb area, west of Taiz Governorate," the main military force fighting for Yemen's government in the south of the country said in a statement.

"This step is taken based ​on the priority of securing the capital, Aden, ‌and the neighbouring governorates, as well as strengthening the front lines and addressing existing threats."

There was no immediate response from the Houthis, or from Saudi Arabia, the Yemeni government's main international ally.

Houthi gains

Yemen's decade-long civil war, which had been dormant since 2022, abruptly reignited this summer as a ‌spillover from the Iran conflict. The Houthis made rapid gains to capture the coast along the ​Red Sea and the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, which controls access to it, while besieging government forces in Taiz, the country's third-biggest city, in mountains above the approach to Aden.

A ⁠Saudi-backed government offensive last month rapidly retook key positions around the strait, notably Dhubab, but failed to drive the Houthis entirely away from the area or to retake the city of al-Mocha further up the coast.

The ‌Houthis have responded by intensifying drone and missile attacks on Saudi Arabia, grounding flights with strikes on its main airports as well as setting global energy markets on edge by targeting energy facilities.

They also made significant advances in the highland areas north of Aden, cutting off Taiz in early October and putting increased pressure on the disparate coalition of forces fighting for the internationally recognised government.

Government forces still trying to push Houthis from coast

Around Bab el-Mandeb the government forces have redeployed to al-Suqyah, just south of ‌Dhubab and 150 km (95 miles) west of Aden, but are still trying to push the Houthis from coastal areas nearby, Yemeni ​military sources said.

In the highlands south of Taiz, the Houthis are positioned just outside the district of Tur al-Bahah in Lahj governorate, about 80 km (50 miles) from Aden.

The Houthi ⁠gains around Taiz, which has become the fiercest front of the civil war, undermined the government campaign around ⁠Bab el-Mandeb, the military sources said.

Fighting is still intensifying around the western region of Taiz, with humanitarian conditions worsening. The city, which hosts about half of the 300,000 people displaced across ‌Yemen by the latest fighting, remains besieged. Aid supplies are unable to enter, and civilians are unable to leave.

The Houthis have meanwhile released 600 prisoners, the International Committee of the Red Cross ​said on Sunday (November 15, 2026).

World.title: 13-year-old boy identified as fourth Indian killed in UAE road accident
World.content:
A 13-year-old boy has been identified as the fourth Indian killed in a multi-vehicle road accident in Fujairah in the UAE that left 14 people dead, according to authorities.

The accident in the early hours of Thursday (November 12, 2026) involved 23 vehicles, including trucks, and left 30 people injured.

“The deceased included 10 Emirati nationals and four Indian nationals, following the completion of procedures to verify their identities,” the UAE’s Ministry of Interior said on Saturday (November 14, 2026) in a post on X.

The Ministry added that “the injured included eight Emirati nationals, two Jordanian nationals, seven Indian nationals, two Pakistani nationals, three Egyptian nationals, six Omani nationals and two Brazilian nationals.”

The boy from Gujarat, identified as Aatif Mohmmed Imran Mansur, was travelling with his family, who were visiting the UAE, when the accident occurred, Gulf News reported on Saturday (November 14, 2026).

The family was on its way to Fujairah International Airport to return to India when the crash took place. His parents and elder sister were injured and are undergoing treatment in hospital, the report said.

The three other Indian victims, who were identified earlier, were members of a family from Vengara in Kerala’s Malappuram district.

Kerala Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan had identified them as Muhammed Asmil, his twin sister Misna Jubin and their three-year-old nephew Muhammed Fayis.

Meanwhile, an official of the Consulate General of India in Dubai visited hospitals in Fujairah to meet family members of the victims and enquire about the condition of injured Indians.

“An official from the Consulate General of India to Dubai and the Northern Emirates visited the hospitals in Fujairah today to meet family members of the victims of yesterday’s tragic road accident and conveyed deepest condolences for the loss of precious lives,” the Indian mission said in a post on X on Friday (November 13, 2026).

The official also met hospital authorities and doctors and enquired about the health and recovery of Indian nationals undergoing treatment, it said.

“All possible assistance is being extended to the families by the Consulate,” the mission added.

According to preliminary investigations by the UAE Public Prosecution, two consecutive accidents occurred on Sheikh Khalifa bin Zayed Road in the direction of Fujairah.

The first involved a vehicle colliding with a stationary truck. In the second, a truck carrying two shipping containers hit several vehicles before overturning.

The accidents occurred in an area where the right-hand lane had been closed for maintenance work, Gulf News said.

The truck driver involved in the second accident was hospitalised and placed under partial detention following interrogation, the Khaleej Times newspaper reported.

World.title: Bessent says Nvidia must ‘go outside the company’ to find new CEO
World.content:
U.S. Treasury ‌Secretary Scott Bessent on Sunday (November 15, 2026) said ​Nvidia needs to “go ⁠outside the company” as it seeks a new chief executive after ‌Jensen Huang abruptly stepped down last week.

Mr. Huang stepped ‌down on Thursday (November 12, 2026) after ‌revelations ⁠of extramarital affairs, including one ⁠involving a suspected Chinese spy, plunging the chipmaker into crisis.

“This makes me ​think that ‌as the board conducts a search for a new leader that they need to ‌go outside the company, ​that just (with) what was going on inside the ⁠company, they need a dramatic shakeup,” Mr. Bessent told Fox News’ “Sunday ‌Morning Futures” show.

Mr. Bessent also said Nvidia’s board and outside counsel needed to answer, within the next 10 days, questions about the company’s culture ‌of compliance with export restrictions.

Nvidia’s board ​has approached British chipmaker Arm Holdings CEO Rene ⁠Haas in its search for ⁠a potential replacement for Mr. Huang, the Financial Times said ‌on Friday (November 13, 2026).

World.title: Violent protests erupt in Hasina’s hometown as tensions rise over her proposed return to Bangladesh
World.content:
Supporters of deposed Bangladesh Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina’s Awami League party staged violent demonstrations in her hometown of Gopalganj on Sunday (November 15, 2026), attacking police vehicles and installations amid growing political tensions over her stated plan to return to the country in December.

Editorial | In a dilemma: On Sheikh Hasina and India-Bangladesh ties

The protests come amid renewed tensions over Ms. Hasina’s proposed return from India, where she has been staying since fleeing Bangladesh in August 2024 after a student-led uprising toppled her government.

Ms. Hasina was sentenced to death in absentia by Bangladesh’s International Crimes Tribunal in November 2025 for crimes against humanity over her government’s crackdown on protesters. She has rejected the charges and the proceedings.

Ms. Hasina, 79, has repeatedly said since July that she intends to return to Bangladesh in December and face legal proceedings, despite the death sentence against her.

The Bangladesh government has been seeking her extradition from India under a bilateral treaty. It has also declined a request made by a London-based law firm on Ms. Hasina’s behalf for a passport to facilitate her return.

Law Minister Md Asaduzzaman said on Saturday (November 14, 2026) that Bangladesh had completed the legal process to secure Ms. Hasina’s return and that the decision now rested with India.

Bangladesh has also linked progress on Ms. Hasina’s extradition to a possible visit to India by Prime Minister Tarique Rahman, saying her return and that of other fugitives sought by Dhaka would help create a conducive environment for the visit.

India has acknowledged receiving Bangladesh’s extradition requests but has not announced a decision.

On Friday (November 13, 2026), Ministry of External Affairs spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said in New Delhi that Ms. Hasina’s extradition was a legal matter and would be dealt with accordingly.

Meanwhile, the demonstrators on Sunday (November 15, 2026) pulled down a monument erected to mark the ouster of Ms. Hasina’s government on August 5, 2024, and broke through police barricades to enter several roads in Gopalganj town. Many women activists also joined the protests.

“Our movement on the streets will continue until we can bring former prime minister and Bangabandhu’s (Bangladesh’s founding father Sheikh Mujibur Rahman) daughter Sheikh Hasina back to the country,” Awami League’s Gopalganj district leader Ilyas Haque told a party rally.

The demonstrations followed the setting on fire of two offices of the ruling Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) in Tungipara — Hasina’s birthplace in Gopalganj — by unidentified persons overnight, reports said.

The developments prompted the government to withdraw the district’s deputy commissioner and police superintendent.

Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed said law enforcement agencies were determined to prevent sabotage and terrorism.

Authorities also called out platoons of paramilitary Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) to stand by riot police in the Gopalganj district, considered an Awami League stronghold.

The situation in Gopalganj was discussed at a Cabinet meeting chaired by Prime Minister Tarique Rahman on Sunday (November 15, 2026). The Prime Minister also met senior party leaders at Parliament, the Prothom Alo newspaper reported.

Quoting BNP leaders familiar with the meeting, the newspaper said Mr. Rahman asked party activists to “remain active” on the ground.

“The government will not let the situation spiral out of control,” Prothom Alo said, quoting a Home Ministry official.

The official said authorities would monitor the situation and increase the deployment of law enforcement personnel depending on developments.

World.title: Panchkula school attack: Ringing the school bell, raising a safety alarm
World.content:
The school’s auto-rickshaw arrived at its usual time around noon on October 28. Homemaker Aarti (name changed to protect privacy) took a quick, reassuring look at her six-year-old daughter’s uniform and schoolbag before waving her off with a smile. However, at 3:30 p.m., when the auto-rickshaw driver went to pick her up from her school in Haryana’s Panchkula district, the girl was nowhere to be found. Her bag was kept at the school’s reception area.

The driver informed her family, who live just five minutes away from the school, and her father came rushing. As he called out her name, his voice grew louder with every frantic step towards the school building. He asked the teachers about his daughter’s whereabouts, and they joined him in his search. Soon, a boy approached him, asked his daughter’s name and confirmed whether he was looking for her. When the father nodded, the boy led him to a classroom on the first floor, telling him that someone had beaten her up.

World.title: Prince William, Princess Kate to meet PM Modi in New Delhi this week
World.content:
The Prince and Princess of Wales, William and Catherine (Kate), are due to meet Prime Minister Narendra Modi in New Delhi on Wednesday. The couple will arrive in Mumbai for a three-day visit, with public engagements kicking off mid-morning on Monday (November 16, 2026). The visit is focused around the Prince’s annual Earthshot Prize, which will be given out on Tuesday evening at a ceremony in the city.

The couple, who were originally scheduled to spend their entire visit in Mumbai, will now conclude it with a meeting with Mr. Modi. Their schedule was changed on Sunday after Mr. Modi’s travel plans were confirmed, the Sunday Times reported. The Prime Minister is due to return from the ASEAN (Association of Southeast Asian Nations) Summit in the Philippines on Tuesday (November 17, 2026).

Also read: Royal couple take guard, Mumbai bowled out

The visit will include an event focused on gully cricket and an engagement with the film industry. Prince William played a round of cricket with cricketers Sourav Ganguly, Brian Lara and England captain Joe Root outside Buckingham Palace last month to promote his environmental prize.

Prince William, 44, is the heir to the British throne and shares a passion for the environment like his father, King Charles III. The Earthshot Prize was instituted by the Prince in 2020 and offers each of five finalists £1 million (approximately ₹12.5 crore) for solutions to pressing environmental problems.

India has produced more finalists for the prize than any other country, Kensington Palace said.

Cricket legend Sachin Tendulkar, actors Alia Bhatt and Rami Malek (the American actor who played one-time Mumbai resident Freddie Mercury in the 2018 film, Bohemian Rhapsody), are among those expected to attend the awards ceremony, hosted by celebrity talk show host Karan Johar. British pop group Take That will perform at Tuesday’s event.

‘Personal connections’

When in Mumbai, the Prince and Princess will also attend the inaugural Children’s Earthshot Awards Ceremony — the culmination of a contest among 15,000 schools across 24 States.

“The future of the U.K.-India partnership will not be shaped by our governments alone, it will be shaped by our people and this visit is a wonderful opportunity to celebrate those deep personal connections between our countries,” said Ben Mellor, Acting British High Commissioner to India, according to PTI.

This is Prince William and Princess Kate’s second official visit to India and the Princess’s first major overseas trip since she was treated for cancer in 2024 and had to step back from official duties.

World.title: Delhi CM offers prayer at Chhath ghat, lauds contribution by Purvanchal community
World.content:
Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta, along with senior BJP leaders, on Sunday evening (November 15, 2026) offered “arghya” (prayers) at a Chhath Ghat on the Yamuna in Sonia Vihar, amidst other devotees, and lauded the efforts of the Purvanchal community toward the development of the city.

Meanwhile, the politics over the Yamuna’s pollution refused to die down, as the AAP attacked the BJP government for arresting an alleged Dalit youth in connection with dead fish found in the upper stretch of the Yamuna River in Sonia Vihar. The party alleged that the police let the Dalit youth go only after the AAP raised the issue.

Niharika Bhatt said that Surender, aged around 30, was arrested in connection with the case. He was later released, as it was a bailable offence, denying any political pressure for the release, she added.

Earlier this week, a large number of fish were found dead in the river near Sonia Vihar, and the BJP accused the AAP of dumping those fish in the river.

Later, following a complaint by the Delhi government’s Irrigation and Flood Control Department, the Delhi Police registered an FIR against unidentified persons for allegedly spreading misinformation about the deaths of a large number of fish in the Yamuna, according to Delhi Police officials.

The Delhi Metro Rail Corporation (DMRC) said that Metros will operate from 4:30 a.m. on Monday instead of 6 a.m. to facilitate the movement of devotees for morning prayers. “Metro services will operate at a 15-minute frequency on all lines until the commencement of regular revenue services, as per the scheduled timetable for the day,” the DMRC said in a post on X.

Traffic regulations will continue to be in place on roads leading to and adjoining various ghats on the Yamuna, including Ram Ghat, Soor Ghat, Bajrangi Ghat, Vasudev Ghat, and Hathi Ghat, as per the Delhi Police.

CM praises Purvanchali community

The Chief Minister said that Delhi is home to people from every part of the country, and the Purvanchali community has made a significant contribution to the development and growth of the capital through its hard work and dedication.

“The Delhi government is committed to ensuring that its Purvanchali brothers and sisters feel at home and have access to better facilities while celebrating their festivals in the capital. Chhath is deeply connected to their faith and cultural identity, and the government is therefore committed to ensuring that devotees have access to better ghats, a clean environment and all necessary facilities for performing the rituals,” Ms. Gupta said.

The Chief Minister said that Chhath is not merely a religious observance but a unique celebration of faith, discipline, cleanliness, dedication, and social harmony. The festival teaches us to respect nature and the environment, and the tradition of worshipping both the setting and the rising sun conveys the message of expressing gratitude for every phase of life, she added.

AAP targets BJP

Meanwhile, AAP Delhi president Saurabh Bharadwaj also took part in Chhath Puja in Kondli, East Delhi, with AAP MLA from the area Kuldeep Kumar, and said that he prayed for everyone’s peace and prosperity.

Earlier in the day, Mr. Bharadwaj, addressing a press conference, said, “The Delhi government’s goondagardi has increased considerably. Minister Parvesh (Sahib Singh) Verma got an FIR registered against the Dalit youth who recorded a video showing fish dying due to pollution in the Yamuna and posted it on social media. The Dalit youth is a Bahujan Samaj Party worker. Following the FIR, Delhi Police arrested him on Saturday evening. When we raised the issue on social media, the police released the youth a short while later. But this is the BJP government’s goondagardi.”

Mr. Bharadwaj also alleged that Yamuna is polluted in Delhi and that it can affect children during the festival. “If the young children of our Purvanchali brothers and sisters drink this polluted water, they could fall seriously ill and may even end up in hospital,” he said.

The Yamuna holds religious significance for the people of Purvanchal, residents of eastern Uttar Pradesh and Bihar, who constitute a significant voter base in Delhi.

World.title: Don’t pay heed to rumours, candidate shortlisting yet to start: Yogi Adityanath, UP BJP chief tell party workers
World.content:
Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath and BJP’s state unit president Pankaj Chaudhary, in a joint statement, on Sunday said certain elements were spreading rumours to create confusion and apprehension among party workers over selection of candidates for next year’s Assembly elections in the state.

The two senior leaders’ joint statement came on the eve of the party’s crucial two-day strategy session (yojana baithak) in Mathura for the Assembly elections.



Both Adityanath and Chaudhary appealed to party workers and office-bearers not to pay heed to “such baseless and misleading reports” and to rely only on the party’s official communications.

In the single-page document, Adityanath and Chaudhary cited “reports” claiming that the BJP has shortlisted 209 candidates for the Assembly polls and has forwarded their names to the central leadership of the party. Terming them as “fake news”, both the leaders denied having prepared such a list.

World.title: ‘Stateless’ Gujarat woman recognised as Indian by descent, gets passport after 26 years
World.content:
On November 11, three days after Diwali, Dolly Vadalia received the best gift of her life, one that she had wanted literally all her life.

The 26-year-old woman, the child of Indian parents who has lived in India since she was 18 days old, received her Indian passport at last.

Only six months earlier, the Gujarat High Court had passed an order that had dealt a severe blow to her, and sent her into an orbit of potential statelessness.

On April 30, a single judge Bench of the court ruled that Dolly Vadalia, who was Dolly Baria before she got married, was “not an Indian citizen by birth or by descent as per the Citizenship Act, 1955”.

Therefore, the court said, she must apply for Indian citizenship.

This put Dolly in a Catch-22 situation: to proceed with the online process to apply for Indian citizenship, she was required to surrender her existing citizenship of a foreign country – which she did not have, and therefore could not surrender.

Dolly Vadalia, 26, is a trained dietitian who was born in Xai-Xai, Mozambique, but whose family was forced to leave the African country after a devastating and unexpected natural disaster in 2000. (Express Photo) Dolly Vadalia, 26, is a trained dietitian who was born in Xai-Xai, Mozambique, but whose family was forced to leave the African country after a devastating and unexpected natural disaster in 2000. (Express Photo)

Dolly, who lives with her family in Rajkot, appealed the order, but the hearing before the two-judge Division Bench of the High Court on October 5 was adjourned.



But now, when the court resumes on November 23 after its annual Diwali vacation, Dolly will withdraw the appeal.

The arrival of her passport in the mail on November 11 was the culmination of Dolly’s three-year journey through the labyrinthine processes of the Indian bureaucracy and judiciary to be recognised as a citizen of India – a success that she said she owes to the intervention of several senior BJP leaders.

“I am very happy. I have finally got my passport, which I felt would be impossible at one point,” she told The Indian Express.

The passport is also Dolly’s path to personal happiness – she can at last travel to be with her husband, Khilan Vadalia, who works in Calgary, Canada. “At last, we will be able to start our normal household life together,” she said.



Dolly’s story began even before she was born – when her parents, Ketan and Aarti Baria, migrated to the city of Xai-Xai in the southern Gaza province of the southern African country of Mozambique in 1995. They started a wholesale grocery business, partnering with a cousin who was already settled in Mozambique.

On February 18, 2000, Dolly was born. The very next day, Mozambique was hit by the full force of a once-in-a-century natural disaster.

Tropical Cyclone Leon-Eline, the second-longest lived cyclone in the Indian Ocean, dumped unheard-of quantities of rain on the country, and caused catastrophic floods that killed at least 800 humans and 20,000 heads of cattle, and swallowed the Barias’ home and business.

Dolly was 18 days old when she was eventually evacuated along with her parents by helicopter to Maputo, the capital of the country, about 210 km away. The government issued the infant an Emergency Certificate, and the family returned to India.



They would never go back to Mozambique – and that was where the trouble began.

Under Section 4(1) of the Citizenship Act, 1955, the birth of every child born abroad must be registered with the Indian consulate within a year of birth; only then does the child qualify to become a citizen of India. and eligible for an Indian passport.

But since Dolly’s parents never went back to Mozambique, they could never inform the Indian High Commission in Maputo of Dolly’s birth, leaving her nationality in limbo. The Centre had cited this provision of the law while arguing against Dolly’s original petition in the High Court.

In effect, this meant that Dolly, a trained dietician with a Master’s degree from an Indian university, who has an Aadhaar, PAN, and a voter’s identity card and has voted in local body elections, could not apply for a passport.



A person can apply to be a citizen of India under seven categories. However, the first requirement for the application is a “copy of a valid foreign passport”.

“Without this requirement being fulfilled in the online registration system, the system does not allow the user to proceed to the next step, effectively ending the process even before it has begun,” Dolly’s father Ketan Hasmukhrai Baria had told The Indian Express earlier this year.

For more than three years, the Barias and Dolly’s in-laws, the Vadalias, ran from pillar to post, knocking on the doors of the bureaucracy and the judiciary to try to find a way for her to get an Indian passport so she could travel to Canada to be with her husband.

But nothing seemed to work out.

Finally, the two families approached Ramesh Dhaduk, vice president of the Gujarat BJP and the former Lok Sabha MP for Porbandar, and Parshottam Rupala, the BJP MP from Rajkot.



“We approached Rameshbhai and Parshottambhai, who asked us to send them all the documents. They forwarded these papers with their reference to various ministries until it reached the Ministry of Home Affairs. We were then asked to send an offline application to the office of Home Minister Amit Shah. Thereafter, officials came to our home to conduct a verification process and found everything in order,” Dolly’s brother-in-law Ronak told The Indian Express.

Following this, the Citizenship Wing of the Foreigners Division of the MHA issued an Office Memorandum to the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) and the Indian High Commission in Mozambique on October 3, 2026, stating that the competent authority had, in light of a June 18 letter received from Dhaduk and Rupala, decided to register the birth of Dolly Vadalia as an Indian Citizen “under section 4(2) of the Citizenship Act, 1955, read with rule 11 of the Citizens (Registration at Indian Consulates) Rules, 1956”.

On October 21, the Indian High Commission in Maputo retrospectively issued a “Certificate of Birth of an Indian Citizen – birth within the Consular jurisdiction of the High Commission of India at Maputo” for Dolly.

Ramesh Dhaduk told The Indian Express, “The family has gone through a lot trying to get Dolly the citizenship and passport. There were tears in their eyes when they came to meet me a couple of days ago. With the blessings of Ambe Ma, they were able to get the passport. We wrote several emails and letters… The file was rejected several times but we managed to follow up, and with help from the office of Amitbhai Shah, managed to get her birth registered.”



Dolly said, “Until I got the passport in my hand, I did not believe that it would be possible. I had been disappointed so many times that I was afraid to be happy until the process was completed.”

World.title: Why cycles and tractors remain potent political symbols in Punjab
World.content:
From cycles and tractors to bullock carts, cometh election hour in Punjab; cometh the familiar assortment of vehicles that politicians turn to signal their proximity to people. As the battle for Punjab, scheduled for early next year, approaches, former Chief Minister and Punjab Congress leader Charanjit Singh Channi launched an eight-day cycle yatra, named the Jawani Sambhal Yatra, from Chamkaur Sahib on November 12. The day before, his party colleagues Partap Singh Bajwa, the Leader of Opposition (LoP) in the state, and state Congress chief Pargat Singh launched the “Punjab mangda insaaf (Punjab demands justice)” bus yatra in Mohali.

Describing the bicycle as “something accessible to ordinary people”, Channi has said he wants to connect with people on various issues through the tour and does not need to prove his “common man credentials” like Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann. In the first phase of the yatra, Channi, the Jalandhar MP, will be accompanied by around 2,000 cyclists and cover 28 of the state’s 117 Assembly constituencies. So far, leaders such as the All India Congress Committee’s Punjab in-charge Sachin Pilot, Pargat Singh, and MLA Sukhpal Khaira have joined the yatra.

Channi cycling with party colleague Malvika Sood, sister of actor Sonu Sood, in Moga on Sunday.

(Express photo) Channi cycling with party colleague Malvika Sood, sister of actor Sonu Sood, in Moga on Sunday.(Express photo)

Bajwa has said that not just the cycle, the Congress will use every mode of transport, including “buses and cars”, to reach people over the next two months. Channi emphasised he does not rely on cars — “main gaadiyan wala nahi hoon, main cyclon wala hoon” (I am not a car person, I am someone who rides cycles) — and that he will conduct the entire Punjab yatra on a bicycle.



This is not the first time that a politician in Punjab has used the humble bicycle to campaign. The ruling Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) has undertaken bicycle and two-wheeler campaigns, having built much of its political appeal around ending VIP culture.

Ex-AAP leader HS Phoolka while campaigning on a cycle during 2014 Lok Sabha polls in Ex-AAP leader HS Phoolka while campaigning on a cycle during 2014 Lok Sabha polls in Ludhiana . (Express photo)

Ahead of the 2014 Lok Sabha elections, the AAP’s Ludhiana candidate and senior Supreme Court advocate H S Phoolka cycled to the nomination centre to file his papers. He also organised bicycle rallies against “VIP culture”, presenting cycling as an accessible alternative to the privileges enjoyed by political elites. Phoolka subsequently won the 2017 Assembly election from Dakha, but later resigned from the AAP and moved to the BJP.



In the past five years, Bhagwant Mann has flagged off — and pedalled in — two major anti-drug cycle rallies: in his home turf, Sangrur, in 2022 and in Ludhiana in 2023.

CM Bhagwant Mann during an anti-drug cycle rally in Ludhiana in 2023. (Express photo) CM Bhagwant Mann during an anti-drug cycle rally in Ludhiana in 2023. (Express photo)

With Channi setting off on his yatra, the CM has taken aim at his predecessor, saying the Congress leader should have distributed cycles to the poor instead of making an attempt at this “political symbolism”. Referring to the bus yatra launched by Bajwa and Pargat Singh, Mann said Channi’s cycle had been “already run over by the Congress’s bus”

Congress leader Kuldip Singh Vaid campaigning on an e-rickshaw in 2022. (Express photo) Congress leader Kuldip Singh Vaid campaigning on an e-rickshaw in 2022. (Express photo)

E-rickshaws to tractors



While former IAS officer and Congress leader Kuldip Singh Vaid campaigned in an e-rickshaw in the constituency of Gill in Ludhiana in 2022 — his bid to win the seat was unsuccessful — Lok Sabha LoP Rahul Gandhi has often been pictured using tractors in rural outreach in Punjab, particularly during the 2020–’21 agitation against the central farm laws. Launching the Congress’s “Kisan Bachao Yatra” in 2020, Gandhi drove a tractor alongside then Chief Minister Amarinder Singh and Sunil Jakhar, both now in the BJP.

Rahul Gandhi on a tractor in 2020 with Sunil Jakhar and Captain Amarinder Singh. (Express photo) Rahul Gandhi on a tractor in 2020 with Sunil Jakhar and Captain Amarinder Singh. (Express photo)

AAP’s first-time MLAs who won in 2022 used the “aam aadmi” vehicles to build a perception and campaign. Sangrur MLA Narinder Kaur Bharaj had driven her scooty, while Nabha MLA Gurdev Singh Dev Maan went to the Assembly on a cycle on the first day. Ludhiana West MLA, the late Gurpreet Gogi, had filed nomination papers riding a vintage scooter, and so did Moga MLA Amandeep Kaur Arora.



AAP first-time MLAs Gurdev Dev Maan, Narinder Kaur Bharaj and late Gurpreet Gogi. (Express photos) AAP first-time MLAs Gurdev Dev Maan, Narinder Kaur Bharaj and late Gurpreet Gogi. (Express photos)

Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) president Sukhbir Badal and MP Harsimrat Kaur Badal, his wife, have also used tractors often for rural outreach.

Congress leader Amrinder Singh Raja Warring and his wife Amrita Warring on a bullock cart. (Express photo) Congress leader Amrinder Singh Raja Warring and his wife Amrita Warring on a bullock cart. (Express photo)

During the Punjab civic body elections this May, Raja Warring and his wife, Amrita, rode a bullock cart to a polling booth in Muktsar, saying they wanted to make a symbolic protest highlighting the “struggles of ordinary households” facing rising fuel prices.

World.title: 8-km stretch hangs fire: Look who all are responsible for stalling Mumbai-Goa highway
World.content:
A joint venture involving a company run by a former Congress minister of Rajasthan; a firm that featured in the RBI’s list of defaulters; a company owned by a businessman probed by the Enforcement Directorate (ED); and a venture headed by a former bureaucrat who helmed the showpiece Samruddhi Expressway project in Maharashtra.

These are some of the heavyweights linked to the five delayed stretches on the Maharashtra section of the 592-km Mumbai-Goa highway, with around 8 km of pending work involving cost overrun estimates of over Rs 2,000 crore in the final stretch, an investigation by The Indian Express shows.

At a glance NH-66 status and timeline Work Start Date October 2007 (conceived in 2006; in December 2016, the government told Parliament it would be completed by December 2018, later revised to 2021). Current Status 99% complete overall; around 8 km across 5 stretches pending in Maharashtra (89% to 98.5% done). New Completion Target April 2027 (per MoRTH Secretary V Umashankar, who says “99% of the highway is through now”). Source: Ministry of Road Transport and Highways, as reported by The Indian Express. Created by Chandrashekar Srinivasan, Express InfoGenIE

On September 9, speaking at the opening of a 5.15-km corridor in Goa’s Porvorim, Union Minister of Road Transport and Highways Nitin Gadkari said he was “ashamed for the delay that has happened” and would skip the inauguration of the highway — expected next year.



The pending stretch in the 472-km Maharashtra section covers five of the 13 packages involved: 3 km of two bypasses; a 192-metre bridge; another 1.8-km flyover; hill cutting at four locations for 1.5 km; and other ongoing road work, records show.

Flyover construction work at Indapur on the Mumbai-Goa highway. (Express photo By Narendra Vaskar) Flyover construction work at Indapur on the Mumbai-Goa highway. (Express photo By Narendra Vaskar)

The Mumbai-Goa highway was first conceived in 2006 as part of the four-lane upgradation of NH-66 as an economic corridor from Panvel near Mumbai to Kanyakumari. Work started in October 2007 on the first 21-km stretch in Maharashtra near the Goa border, which was completed in 2013. Subsequently, most of the other stretches were sanctioned in 2015-16 and contracts awarded in 2017-18. In December 2016, the Government told Parliament that the highway would be completed by December 2018.
